subjects.title: Chemistry: Empirical and Molecular Formula Determination
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: an empirical formula shows the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound, while a molecular formula shows the actual number of each atom present, and the molecular formula can be found from the empirical formula using the compound’s molar mass.

quiz.q: An empirical formula shows ___.
options: The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound
Only the mass of a compound, with no connection to atoms
A concept unrelated to chemical formulas
The exact, actual number of every atom in a compound

quiz.q: A molecular formula shows ___.
options: The actual number of each atom present in a compound
The exact colour of a compound in its solid state
A concept unrelated to chemical formulas
Only the simplest possible ratio of atoms, never the actual number

quiz.q: To determine an empirical formula from experimental data, a chemist typically first converts the mass of each element to ___.
options: Degrees Celsius, with no connection to mass
A unit unrelated to determining a formula
Litres, with no connection to mass
Moles

quiz.q: Why might a molecular formula be a whole-number multiple of its corresponding empirical formula?
options: A molecular formula can never relate mathematically to an empirical formula
The empirical formula only shows the simplest ratio, so the actual compound may contain that ratio repeated several times
Molecular and empirical formulas are always numerically identical for every compound
This relationship has no basis in a compound’s actual structure

quiz.q: Why is knowing a compound’s molar mass necessary to determine its molecular formula from its empirical formula?
options: The molar mass reveals how many times the empirical formula’s mass fits into the actual compound’s total mass
Molar mass has no connection to determining a molecular formula
This concept only applies to compounds with no measurable mass
A molecular formula can always be determined with no reference to mass at all

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Analyzing News Bias and Fact-Checking
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: news bias occurs when a report favours a particular perspective through word choice, source selection, or omission, and fact-checking practices help readers verify claims and identify that bias before accepting a report as accurate.

quiz.q: News bias occurs when a report favours a particular perspective through ___.
options: The exact font used to print the article
A concept unrelated to news reporting
The specific day of the week the article is published
Word choice, source selection, or omission

quiz.q: Which is an example of a fact-checking practice a reader might use to verify a claim?
options: A practice entirely unrelated to verifying information
Trusting a claim because it appeared in a single social media post
Accepting a claim immediately without any further investigation
Comparing the claim against multiple independent, credible sources

quiz.q: Why might the specific sources a journalist chooses to quote reveal a form of bias in a news report?
options: This factor has no connection to how a news report is constructed
The sources chosen for a report never have any influence on its perspective
Selectively quoting sources who share one perspective can present an incomplete picture of an issue
Every journalist is required to quote an identical number of sources

quiz.q: Why is omission — leaving out certain facts or context — considered a subtle but powerful form of bias?
options: A reason unrelated to how bias appears in news reporting
Every fact relevant to a story must always be included in a report
Omitting information can never influence how a reader interprets a report
Leaving out relevant information can shape a reader’s understanding without any single statement being false

quiz.q: Why is developing strong fact-checking habits especially important for navigating news encountered on social media?
options: All information shared on social media is automatically verified before posting
Information can spread quickly on social media before its accuracy has been verified by anyone
This skill has no relevance to how people consume news today
Fact-checking is never necessary for information found on social media

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Trigonometry: The Ambiguous Case of the Sine Law
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: when solving a triangle using the sine law with two sides and a non-included angle (SSA), the given information can sometimes produce two possible triangles, one possible triangle, or no triangle at all — a situation called the ambiguous case.

quiz.q: The ambiguous case of the sine law arises when a triangle is defined by ___.
options: Three sides and no angles at all
Two sides and a non-included angle
Two angles and no sides at all
A concept unrelated to solving triangles

quiz.q: In the ambiguous case, the given information can result in ___.
options: Two possible triangles, one possible triangle, or no triangle at all
Exactly one possible triangle in every single case
A number of triangles unrelated to the given information
Always three distinct possible triangles

quiz.q: Why might two different triangles both satisfy the same SSA information in the ambiguous case?
options: Two triangles can never share the same combination of two sides and a non-included angle
The unknown angle could be either acute or obtuse and still be consistent with the given side lengths
SSA information always determines a single unique triangle with no other possibility
This situation has no connection to how the sine law is applied

quiz.q: Why might no triangle exist at all for a particular set of SSA measurements in the ambiguous case?
options: A missing triangle can only occur when three sides are given instead of SSA
Every possible combination of SSA measurements always produces at least one valid triangle
The given side opposite the known angle may be too short to reach and close the triangle
This outcome has no connection to solving triangles with the sine law

quiz.q: Why is it important to check for the ambiguous case whenever a triangle is defined using two sides and a non-included angle?
options: The ambiguous case only applies to right triangles, never to any other triangle
Failing to check can lead to reporting only one solution when a second valid triangle also exists
This concept has no relevance to correctly solving a triangle
Checking for the ambiguous case is never necessary when solving a triangle

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Comparative Anatomy and Homologous Structures
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: comparative anatomy examines the physical structures of different species, and homologous structures — features with a shared underlying form despite different functions, such as a bat’s wing and a human arm — provide strong evidence for common ancestry.

quiz.q: A homologous structure is best described as a feature that shares a ___ despite serving a different function across species.
options: Identical function, with no connection to structure
Completely unrelated form across every species
Similar underlying form
A concept unrelated to comparative anatomy

quiz.q: Which is a commonly cited example of homologous structures?
options: A shark’s fin and a bird’s wing
A bird’s wing and an insect’s wing
Two entirely unrelated structures found in different species
A bat’s wing and a human arm

quiz.q: Why do homologous structures provide strong evidence for common ancestry between species?
options: Common ancestry can never be supported using evidence from anatomy
Homologous structures always indicate that two species are completely unrelated
A shared underlying structure suggests both species inherited that basic form from a common ancestor
This evidence has no connection to evolutionary relationships between species

quiz.q: An analogous structure differs from a homologous structure because it involves ___.
options: A similar function evolving independently, without a shared underlying structure
An identical underlying structure shared by two closely related species
A feature that always indicates the two species share a recent common ancestor
A concept unrelated to comparative anatomy

quiz.q: Why is comparative anatomy considered a valuable source of evidence alongside the fossil record when studying evolutionary relationships?
options: Structural similarities in living species can reveal shared ancestry even when a complete fossil record is unavailable
Anatomical evidence is always less reliable than every other type of evidence
Comparative anatomy has no connection to studying evolutionary relationships
This field has no relevance to the study of evolutionary biology

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Colorimetry and Beer’s Law
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: colorimetry measures how much light of a specific wavelength a coloured solution absorbs, and Beer’s law describes the direct relationship between that absorbance and the solution’s concentration, allowing an unknown concentration to be determined.

quiz.q: Colorimetry measures how much light of a specific wavelength a solution ___.
options: Reflects exclusively, with no connection to absorption
Absorbs
Produces on its own, with no light source involved
A concept unrelated to colorimetry

quiz.q: Beer’s law describes a direct relationship between a solution’s absorbance and its ___.
options: A property unrelated to colorimetry
Physical volume, with no connection to concentration
Exact temperature, with no connection to absorbance
Concentration

quiz.q: Why is a calibration curve, built from solutions of known concentration, useful when using Beer’s law to find an unknown concentration?
options: Beer’s law can only be applied without ever using a calibration curve
This tool is only useful for solutions with no colour at all
It lets an unknown sample’s absorbance be compared against a reliable, established relationship between absorbance and concentration
A calibration curve has no connection to determining an unknown concentration

quiz.q: Why might a more concentrated coloured solution generally absorb more light than a diluted one?
options: This relationship has no basis in the properties of the solution
A more concentrated solution always absorbs less light than a diluted one
A greater concentration means more light-absorbing particles are present for light to pass through
Concentration has no connection to how much light a solution absorbs

quiz.q: Why is colorimetry a valuable technique in fields such as water-quality testing and medical laboratories?
options: Colorimetry has no practical application outside of a chemistry classroom
Concentration can never be determined using a solution’s absorbance
This technique only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
It allows the concentration of a specific substance in a solution to be determined quickly and precisely

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: Debate Rebuttal and Cross-Examination
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: an effective rebuttal directly addresses an opponent’s argument with evidence and logical reasoning, while cross-examination uses targeted questions to expose weaknesses in an opponent’s position during a structured debate.

quiz.q: An effective rebuttal directly addresses an opponent’s argument using ___.
options: Personal insults directed at the opponent
A completely unrelated topic chosen at random
A concept unrelated to debate
Evidence and logical reasoning

quiz.q: Cross-examination in a debate primarily involves ___.
options: Asking targeted questions to expose weaknesses in an opponent’s position
A concept unrelated to debate
Reading a prepared speech with no questions asked at all
Agreeing with every point an opponent has made

quiz.q: Why is it important for a rebuttal to engage directly with an opponent’s specific claim, rather than simply restating one’s own original argument?
options: This distinction has no connection to effective debating
Directly addressing the claim shows the audience that the opposing argument has been carefully considered and refuted
A rebuttal never needs to reference what an opponent has actually argued
Restating one’s own argument is always a more effective strategy than engaging with an opponent’s claim

quiz.q: Why might a well-crafted cross-examination question be phrased to require a brief, specific answer rather than an open-ended one?
options: A brief, specific answer makes it harder for an opponent to avoid addressing a weakness directly
This strategy has no connection to exposing weaknesses in an argument
Open-ended questions are always the most effective type of question in cross-examination
The phrasing of a question has no effect on how easily it can be answered

quiz.q: Why do debate skills like rebuttal and cross-examination remain valuable beyond a formal debate setting?
options: These skills have no application outside of a formal debate
Rebuttal and cross-examination are only useful in a courtroom setting
They build the ability to evaluate arguments critically and respond to opposing viewpoints in many real-world contexts
A reason unrelated to communication skills

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Statistics: Measures of Central Tendency and Spread
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand (Data Management): measures of central tendency, such as the mean, median, and mode, describe a typical value in a data set, while measures of spread, such as range and interquartile range, describe how varied the data actually is.

quiz.q: The mean of a data set is calculated by ___.
options: Adding all the values and dividing by the number of values
Selecting the single largest value in the data set
A calculation unrelated to central tendency
Selecting the value that appears most frequently

quiz.q: The median of a data set is best described as ___.
options: The value that appears most often in the data set
The difference between the largest and smallest values
A concept unrelated to central tendency
The middle value when the data is arranged in order

quiz.q: The range of a data set is calculated by ___.
options: Subtracting the smallest value from the largest value
Adding every value in the data set together
A calculation unrelated to measures of spread
Dividing the largest value by the smallest value

quiz.q: Why might the median be a more appropriate measure of central tendency than the mean for a data set with an extreme outlier?
options: The mean is always the more appropriate measure regardless of outliers
The median is always affected more strongly by an outlier than the mean is
Outliers have no effect on either the mean or the median
The median is not pulled toward an extreme value the way the mean can be

quiz.q: Why is a measure of spread, such as the interquartile range, useful alongside a measure of central tendency?
options: Central tendency always provides a complete picture of a data set with no further information needed
A reason unrelated to interpreting a data set
It reveals how consistent or varied the data actually is, which a single central value cannot show on its own
Measures of spread provide no additional information beyond central tendency alone

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Extremophiles and the Limits of Life
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: extremophiles are organisms, primarily microorganisms, that thrive in conditions once thought too harsh for life, such as extreme heat, cold, pressure, or acidity, expanding scientific understanding of where and how life can exist.

quiz.q: An extremophile is best described as an organism that ___.
options: Can only survive in mild, temperate environments
Requires an environment identical to that of most other organisms
Thrives in conditions once thought too harsh for life
A concept unrelated to biology

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of an extreme condition in which an extremophile might live?
options: The near-boiling water of a deep-sea hydrothermal vent
A comfortable room-temperature environment with average humidity
A condition entirely unrelated to extremophiles
A typical backyard garden with no unusual conditions

quiz.q: Why has the discovery of extremophiles changed scientific understanding of where life might exist elsewhere in the universe?
options: It shows that life can adapt to conditions once assumed to make survival impossible, broadening the search for life on other worlds
The discovery of extremophiles proved that life can only exist under mild, Earth-like conditions
This discovery has no relevance to astrobiology or the study of extreme environments
Extremophiles have no connection to the scientific search for life beyond Earth

quiz.q: Why might enzymes from extremophiles, such as heat-tolerant bacteria, be valuable in industrial or laboratory applications?
options: Enzymes from extremophiles always stop functioning under any unusual condition
Industrial applications never make use of enzymes derived from any organism
This concept has no practical application outside of basic biology
These enzymes can remain functional under extreme conditions, such as high heat, where typical enzymes would stop working

quiz.q: Why do scientists classify many extremophiles within the domain Archaea rather than Bacteria or Eukarya?
options: This concept has no relevance to the classification of living things
All extremophiles are classified identically within a single domain with no distinctions made
Archaea often possess distinct cellular and genetic features suited to surviving extreme environments
Domain classification has no connection to an organism’s ability to survive extreme conditions

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Acid Rain and Atmospheric Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: acid rain forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released by burning fossil fuels react with water vapour in the atmosphere to produce sulphuric and nitric acid, lowering the pH of precipitation and damaging ecosystems.

quiz.q: Acid rain primarily forms when sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides react with ___ in the atmosphere.
options: Water vapour
Oxygen gas alone, with no other reactant involved
Solid particles exclusively, with no connection to water vapour
A substance unrelated to atmospheric chemistry

quiz.q: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides that contribute to acid rain are primarily released by ___.
options: The natural respiration of forest ecosystems alone
A process unrelated to acid rain formation
Burning fossil fuels
Ordinary evaporation of lake water, with no connection to combustion

quiz.q: Why does acid rain typically have a lower pH than unpolluted rainwater?
options: Acid rain always has a pH identical to that of unpolluted rainwater
This difference has no connection to the chemical reactions occurring in the atmosphere
The sulphuric and nitric acid formed in the atmosphere increase the concentration of hydrogen ions in the precipitation
Acid rain forms with no acids present at all

quiz.q: Why might acid rain be especially damaging to lakes and forests with limited natural buffering capacity?
options: Acid rain never has any measurable effect on soil or water pH
Buffering capacity has no connection to how an ecosystem responds to acid rain
Every ecosystem has an identical, unlimited capacity to neutralize acid rain
Without enough naturally occurring bases to neutralize the added acidity, the pH of soil and water can drop sharply

quiz.q: Why have regulations limiting sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide emissions from industrial sources helped reduce acid rain in many regions?
options: Reducing the emission of these gases directly reduces the raw materials available to form sulphuric and nitric acid in the atmosphere
Emission regulations always increase the rate of acid rain formation instead
Acid rain formation is entirely unrelated to industrial emissions
These regulations have no connection to the chemical formation of acid rain

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Character Study Essay
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a character study essay closely analyzes a single character’s motivations, relationships, and development, using specific textual evidence to build an interpretation of that character’s role within the larger work.

quiz.q: A character study essay primarily focuses on analyzing ___.
options: A concept unrelated to literary analysis
The publication history of the entire text
A single character’s motivations, relationships, and development
The biography of the author, with no connection to the character

quiz.q: Why is specific textual evidence, such as a direct quotation, important when writing a character study essay?
options: It grounds the writer’s interpretation of the character in details actually present in the text
Textual evidence is never necessary when analyzing a character
A reason unrelated to supporting a literary interpretation
An interpretation of a character should rely only on a reader’s personal opinion, with no evidence needed

quiz.q: Which is an example of a character’s development that a character study essay might trace?
options: The exact number of pages the character appears on
The font used to print the character’s dialogue
A shift in the character’s values after a significant event in the plot
A detail entirely unrelated to a character’s growth

quiz.q: Why might a character study essay examine a character’s relationships with other characters, rather than looking at that character in isolation?
options: Characters in a text never influence or reveal anything about one another
Relationships can reveal aspects of a character’s values and motivations that might not be visible otherwise
A character’s relationships with others are never relevant to understanding that character
This approach has no connection to analyzing a character’s development

quiz.q: Why might tracing a character’s internal contradictions strengthen a character study essay?
options: Contradictions can reveal a more complex, realistic portrait of a character than a purely consistent description would
A strong character study essay should ignore any contradictions found in a character
Internal contradictions have no connection to literary analysis
Every well-written character is entirely consistent, with no contradictions present

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Optimization Problems Using Quadratic Models
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: many real-world quantities, such as area or revenue, can be modelled with a quadratic function, and the vertex of that function’s parabola represents the maximum or minimum value the quantity can reach.

quiz.q: In a quadratic model, the vertex of the parabola represents the ___ value the modelled quantity can reach.
options: The value exactly halfway between the two x-intercepts, unrelated to the quantity itself
Maximum or minimum
A value unrelated to optimization problems
Only the minimum value, with no connection to a maximum

quiz.q: If a quadratic function opens downward, its vertex represents a ___ value.
options: Maximum
A value unrelated to the shape of the parabola
Minimum, with no connection to a downward-opening parabola
Value that can never actually be reached by the function

quiz.q: Which is an example of a real-world quantity that might be modelled and optimized using a quadratic function?
options: The maximum area that can be enclosed by a fixed length of fencing
A quantity entirely unrelated to optimization problems
A quantity that changes at a constant rate with no connection to a parabola
The exact colour of an object with no connection to area or revenue

quiz.q: Why is completing the square, or finding the vertex form of a quadratic function, a useful strategy for solving an optimization problem?
options: This strategy only applies to functions that have no vertex at all
Completing the square has no connection to identifying a maximum or minimum value
It directly reveals the coordinates of the vertex, which represent the optimal value being sought
Vertex form always hides the optimal value rather than revealing it

quiz.q: Why might a business use a quadratic model to determine the price that maximizes revenue?
options: Revenue always increases indefinitely as price increases, with no maximum value
Revenue often rises and then falls as price increases, a pattern that a parabola can accurately represent
This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no real-world use
Quadratic models have no practical application in business or economics

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Plant Biology: Pollination Strategies and Coevolution with Pollinators
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: flowering plants have evolved diverse pollination strategies, including traits like colour, scent, and nectar that attract specific pollinators, and this relationship has driven coevolution between plants and the animals that pollinate them.

quiz.q: Flowering plants attract pollinators using traits such as ___.
options: The thickness of the plant’s bark alone
Colour, scent, and nectar
The depth of the plant’s root system exclusively
A trait entirely unrelated to pollination

quiz.q: Coevolution between a plant and its pollinator describes a process in which ___.
options: Each species evolves in response to selective pressures exerted by the other
A concept unrelated to plant-pollinator relationships
Only the plant evolves, while the pollinator remains completely unchanged
The two species evolve in complete isolation from one another

quiz.q: Why might a flower’s shape closely match the body shape of a specific pollinator species, such as a particular species of moth?
options: This kind of specialized matching never occurs between plants and pollinators
A close structural match can make pollen transfer more efficient for that specific pollinator
Every flower is pollinated equally well by every possible pollinator species
A flower’s shape has no connection to which pollinators visit it

quiz.q: Why might a plant that relies on wind pollination typically produce flowers with less colourful petals and little scent compared to insect-pollinated flowers?
options: Attracting a specific animal pollinator is unnecessary when pollen is instead carried by the wind
Pollination strategy has no connection to a flower’s colour or scent
Wind-pollinated plants always produce the most brightly coloured, strongly scented flowers
This concept has no relevance to understanding plant reproduction

quiz.q: Why is the coevolutionary relationship between plants and pollinators considered ecologically significant?
options: Plants and their pollinators have no meaningful ecological connection to one another
Pollinator populations have no effect on plant reproduction rates
This relationship has no broader significance for ecosystems
A decline in pollinator populations can directly threaten the reproduction of the plant species that depend on them

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Photochemistry and Light-Induced Reactions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: photochemistry studies chemical reactions triggered when a molecule absorbs light energy, exciting an electron to a higher energy level and enabling reactions, such as photosynthesis or the breakdown of ozone, that would not otherwise occur.

quiz.q: Photochemistry studies chemical reactions that are triggered when a molecule ___.
options: Is cooled to an extremely low temperature, with no connection to light
Absorbs light energy
Is placed under extremely high pressure, with no connection to light
A process unrelated to photochemistry

quiz.q: When a molecule absorbs light energy in a photochemical reaction, an electron is typically ___.
options: Excited to a higher energy level
Removed from the molecule permanently, with no return possible
A change unrelated to photochemistry
Converted directly into a different element

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a naturally occurring photochemical reaction?
options: The freezing of water into ice
Photosynthesis in a green plant
A reaction entirely unrelated to the absorption of light
A reaction that occurs identically with or without the presence of light

quiz.q: Why does the breakdown of ozone in the atmosphere depend on a photochemical reaction?
options: Photochemical reactions never occur within the atmosphere
Ultraviolet light provides the energy needed to break the bonds within an ozone molecule
Ozone breaks down at an identical rate whether or not light is present
This process has no connection to the absorption of light energy

quiz.q: Why is photochemistry considered relevant to technologies such as solar panels and photographic film?
options: Photochemistry has no connection to any modern technology
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry with no practical use
These technologies rely on a chemical or electrical response triggered specifically by the absorption of light
Solar panels and photographic film function with no dependence on light at all

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Cohesion and Coherence in Extended Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: cohesion refers to how sentences and paragraphs are grammatically and lexically linked using devices like transitions and pronouns, while coherence refers to how logically and clearly the overall ideas in a piece of writing connect and flow.

quiz.q: Cohesion in writing refers to how sentences and paragraphs are ___.
options: Numbered in sequential order, with no connection to language
Grammatically and lexically linked, using devices like transitions and pronouns
A concept unrelated to writing structure
Printed on the page, with no connection to meaning

quiz.q: Coherence in writing refers to how ___.
options: A concept unrelated to writing structure
Many total paragraphs a piece of writing contains
Long each individual sentence in a piece of writing is
Logically and clearly the overall ideas in a piece connect and flow

quiz.q: Which is an example of a cohesive device a writer might use to link two sentences?
options: A transition word, such as “however” or “therefore”
A device entirely unrelated to linking sentences
Repeating the exact same sentence twice in a row
Leaving a blank line between every sentence

quiz.q: Why might a piece of writing be grammatically cohesive, with clear transitions, but still lack coherence overall?
options: This situation can never occur in a piece of writing
A lack of coherence always results from missing transition words alone
Cohesion and coherence always mean exactly the same thing, with no possible difference between them
The individual ideas may not logically build toward a clear, unified point, even if the sentences connect smoothly

quiz.q: Why is revising for both cohesion and coherence important in an extended piece of academic writing?
options: Extended academic writing never requires revision for either cohesion or coherence
A reason unrelated to producing clear, effective writing
Together, they ensure a reader can follow both the sentence-to-sentence connections and the overall logical argument
Revising for cohesion and coherence has no effect on how clearly a piece of writing communicates its ideas

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Solving Equations Graphically versus Algebraically
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: an equation can be solved algebraically by manipulating symbols to isolate a variable, or graphically by finding where a function’s graph crosses the x-axis or where two graphs intersect, with each approach offering different advantages.

quiz.q: Solving an equation graphically typically involves finding where a graph ___.
options: Reaches its exact maximum height, with no connection to solving equations
Crosses the x-axis or intersects another graph
A concept unrelated to solving equations
Changes colour, with no connection to its shape

quiz.q: Solving an equation algebraically typically involves ___.
options: A concept unrelated to solving equations
Manipulating symbols to isolate the variable
Guessing a solution with no further verification
Sketching an accurate graph with no symbolic manipulation involved

quiz.q: Why might a graphical approach be especially useful for solving an equation that is difficult or impossible to solve algebraically?
options: Every equation can always be solved exactly using algebra alone, with no exceptions
This advantage has no connection to solving equations
A graph can reveal an approximate solution even when an exact algebraic method is not readily available
Graphical approaches can never provide any useful information about a solution

quiz.q: Why might an algebraic approach be preferred over a graphical approach when an exact solution is required?
options: Algebraic methods can produce a precise value, while reading a graph often only gives an approximate one
Algebraic methods always produce a less precise answer than a graph
This distinction has no connection to how equations are solved
Graphical methods always provide a more exact solution than algebraic methods

quiz.q: Why is it valuable for a student to be able to solve the same equation using both graphical and algebraic methods?
options: A reason unrelated to understanding how equations and graphs are connected
Using both methods together provides no additional confidence in a solution
Comparing both methods can help confirm a solution is correct and build a deeper understanding of the relationship between an equation and its graph
Graphical and algebraic methods can never be used to verify one another

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biotechnology: Bioinformatics and DNA Sequencing
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: bioinformatics combines biology with computer science to analyze large sets of biological data, particularly DNA sequences, allowing researchers to compare genomes, identify genes, and study evolutionary relationships at a molecular level.

quiz.q: Bioinformatics combines biology with ___.
options: Computer science
Architecture, with no connection to biological data
Physical education, with no connection to biological data
A field entirely unrelated to analyzing biological data

quiz.q: DNA sequencing is best described as a process that determines ___.
options: The physical mass of a DNA molecule
The exact order of nucleotides in a DNA molecule
A concept unrelated to DNA sequencing
The colour of a cell’s nucleus

quiz.q: Why is bioinformatics necessary for analyzing the enormous amount of data produced by modern DNA sequencing technology?
options: Bioinformatics has no connection to analyzing DNA sequencing data
This field has no practical application in modern biology
DNA sequencing produces so little data that computational analysis is never needed
Computational tools can process and compare far more genetic data than would be possible using manual analysis alone

quiz.q: Why might comparing DNA sequences across different species be useful for studying evolutionary relationships?
options: DNA sequence comparisons provide no information about evolutionary relationships
Greater similarity between DNA sequences can indicate a more recent shared common ancestor
Every species shares an identical DNA sequence, regardless of ancestry
This concept has no connection to the study of evolution

quiz.q: Why is bioinformatics considered valuable in fields such as medicine, including the development of personalized treatments?
options: This concept only applies to purely theoretical research with no practical use
Bioinformatics has no application in modern medicine
Genetic data provides no useful information for developing medical treatments
Analyzing an individual’s genetic data can help identify specific genetic factors relevant to their health

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Flame Tests and Atomic Emission
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a flame test identifies certain metal ions by the characteristic colour they produce when heated, a result of electrons absorbing energy, jumping to a higher energy level, and then releasing that energy as light of a specific wavelength when they fall back down.

quiz.q: A flame test identifies certain metal ions based on the ___ they produce when heated.
options: A property unrelated to flame tests
Boiling point, with no connection to colour
Characteristic colour
Exact mass, with no connection to colour

quiz.q: The characteristic colour seen in a flame test results from an electron ___.
options: Being permanently removed from the atom, with no return possible
Splitting the nucleus of the atom into smaller fragments
A process unrelated to atomic emission
Falling back to a lower energy level and releasing energy as light

quiz.q: Why does heating a metal ion in a flame first cause an electron to jump to a higher energy level?
options: Electrons are removed from the atom entirely when the flame is applied
Heating a metal ion has no effect on the position of its electrons
The electron absorbs energy from the flame, allowing it to move to a less stable, higher-energy position
This process has no connection to atomic emission

quiz.q: Why does each metal ion tend to produce a distinct, characteristic flame colour rather than an identical colour for every metal?
options: This concept has no scientific basis
Flame colour has no connection to the internal energy levels of an atom
Each element has its own unique set of energy levels, so the light released has a specific wavelength
Every metal ion always produces an identical colour when heated in a flame

quiz.q: Why are flame tests considered a useful, quick qualitative technique in a chemistry laboratory?
options: This technique requires expensive, highly specialized equipment unavailable in most laboratories
Flame tests provide no useful information for identifying an unknown substance
They allow certain metal ions to be identified rapidly using a simple, low-cost procedure
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Confessional Poem
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a confessional poem draws directly on the poet’s own personal, often intimate or painful experiences, using a candid first-person voice to explore emotions that earlier poetic traditions frequently kept private.

quiz.q: A confessional poem draws directly on the poet’s own ___.
options: Purely factual, historical events with no personal connection
A concept unrelated to poetry
Personal, often intimate or painful experiences
Entirely invented experiences with no connection to the poet’s own life

quiz.q: Confessional poetry is typically written using a ___ voice.
options: Voice that avoids any expression of emotion
Candid first-person
Distant, impersonal third-person
A voice unrelated to confessional poetry

quiz.q: Why might a confessional poem address a topic that earlier poetic traditions often avoided discussing openly?
options: Confessional poetry always avoids any topic connected to personal experience
Earlier poetic traditions never avoided any particular subject matter
This choice has no connection to the goals of confessional poetry
Confessional poetry values direct honesty about personal experience over maintaining a more formal, reserved distance

quiz.q: Why might a reader find a confessional poem especially emotionally resonant compared to a more impersonal poem?
options: The poem’s candid, personal voice can create a strong sense of intimacy and honesty with the reader
This concept has no connection to how poetry communicates emotion
Confessional poems are always less emotionally engaging than impersonal poems
A poem’s use of a personal voice has no effect on how a reader experiences it

quiz.q: Why might critics debate whether a confessional poem should be read as strictly autobiographical?
options: A poet may shape or heighten real experiences for artistic effect, blurring the line between fact and craft
Every confessional poem is always an exact, unaltered record of true events
This question has no relevance to interpreting confessional poetry
Confessional poems never contain any element of artistic shaping or invention

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Systems of Three Linear Equations
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a system of three linear equations in three variables can be solved using elimination or substitution to systematically reduce the system, and its solution represents the single point where all three planes intersect, if one exists.

quiz.q: A system of three linear equations in three variables has a solution that represents ___.
options: The exact midpoint between any two of the three equations
The area enclosed by all three equations combined
A concept unrelated to systems of equations
The single point where all three planes intersect, if one exists

quiz.q: A common strategy for solving a system of three linear equations is to first ___.
options: Eliminate one variable to reduce the system to two equations with two variables
Add all three equations together with no further steps taken
Ignore two of the three equations entirely
A strategy unrelated to solving systems of equations

quiz.q: Why might a system of three linear equations have no solution at all?
options: Every system of three linear equations always has exactly one solution
A system with no solution can never occur when working with linear equations
The three planes represented by the equations may never intersect at a single common point
This outcome has no connection to how the equations relate to one another

quiz.q: Why might a system of three linear equations have infinitely many solutions?
options: The three equations may represent planes that intersect along a shared line or are otherwise dependent on one another
A system always has either exactly one solution or no solution at all, with no other possibility
This outcome has no connection to how the three planes are positioned relative to one another
Infinitely many solutions can never occur in a system of linear equations

quiz.q: Why might a system of three linear equations be useful for modelling a real-world situation involving three related unknown quantities, such as the cost of three different products?
options: Systems of three linear equations have no real-world modelling applications
This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no practical use
This type of situation can never be represented using a system of equations
It allows all three unknown quantities to be determined simultaneously using the relationships described by the equations

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Animal Adaptations to Extreme Environments
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: animals living in extreme environments, such as deserts, polar regions, or high altitudes, have evolved specialized structural, physiological, and behavioural adaptations that allow them to survive conditions that would be lethal to most other species.

quiz.q: An adaptation is best described as a trait that ___.
options: Always harms an organism’s chances of survival
Has no effect at all on an organism’s survival or reproduction
A concept unrelated to evolutionary biology
Improves an organism’s ability to survive and reproduce in its environment

quiz.q: Which is an example of a structural adaptation that helps an animal survive in a cold, polar environment?
options: Large ears that maximize heat loss
A thick layer of insulating blubber
A structural feature entirely unrelated to surviving cold temperatures
Thin fur with no insulating properties at all

quiz.q: Which is an example of a physiological adaptation that helps an animal survive in a hot desert environment?
options: A physiological process entirely unrelated to conserving water
A process that always increases water loss regardless of the environment
The complete inability to regulate internal body temperature
The ability to produce highly concentrated urine that conserves water

quiz.q: Why might a behavioural adaptation, such as being active only at night, help an animal survive in a hot desert environment?
options: Behavioural adaptations have no connection to helping an animal survive extreme temperatures
Being active only at night always increases an animal’s risk of overheating
This concept has no relevance to understanding animal adaptations
Avoiding activity during the hottest part of the day can reduce water loss and the risk of overheating

quiz.q: Why do animals living at high altitudes often have physiological adaptations related to oxygen use, such as an increased concentration of red blood cells?
options: Oxygen availability is identical at every altitude, with no variation at all
Air at high altitudes contains less available oxygen, so the body must adapt to transport it more efficiently
This concept has no relevance to understanding animal physiology
High-altitude environments have no connection to an animal’s oxygen-related adaptations

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Soaps, Detergents, and Surfactant Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: soaps and detergents are surfactants, molecules with a water-attracting head and a water-repelling, fat-attracting tail, allowing them to surround grease and oil particles so they can be lifted away and rinsed off with water.

quiz.q: A surfactant molecule, such as one found in soap, has a structure with ___.
options: Two identical water-repelling ends, with no water-attracting portion
A water-attracting head and a water-repelling, fat-attracting tail
Two identical water-attracting ends, with no water-repelling portion
A concept unrelated to surfactant chemistry

quiz.q: The water-attracting portion of a surfactant molecule is described as ___.
options: Hydrophilic
Hydrophobic, with no connection to attracting water
A term unrelated to surfactant chemistry
Insoluble, with no connection to water at all

quiz.q: Why can a surfactant molecule surround a grease or oil particle in water?
options: Its water-repelling tail attaches to the grease while its water-attracting head faces outward into the surrounding water
Grease and oil dissolve directly in water without any need for a surfactant
Surfactant molecules have no interaction at all with grease or oil particles
This process has no connection to the structure of a surfactant molecule

quiz.q: Why is soap generally less effective than synthetic detergents in hard water, which contains dissolved calcium and magnesium ions?
options: Soap can react with these ions to form an insoluble precipitate, often seen as soap scum, reducing its cleaning ability
Hard water has no effect on the cleaning ability of soap
This concept has no connection to surfactant chemistry
Soap always cleans more effectively in hard water than any synthetic detergent

quiz.q: Why are surfactants considered essential to the function of everyday cleaning products?
options: They allow water, which does not dissolve grease and oil on its own, to lift and rinse away those substances
Water alone is always equally effective at removing grease and oil without any surfactant
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
Surfactants have no practical role in cleaning products

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Elegy and Commemorative Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: an elegy is a reflective piece of writing, often a poem, composed to mourn or commemorate someone or something that has been lost, typically moving from an expression of grief toward some form of consolation or acceptance.

quiz.q: An elegy is best described as a reflective piece of writing composed to ___.
options: A concept unrelated to commemorative writing
Mourn or commemorate someone or something that has been lost
Celebrate an achievement with no connection to loss or grief
Provide a purely factual, unemotional record of an event

quiz.q: An elegy often moves from an initial expression of grief toward ___.
options: A concept unrelated to the structure of an elegy
An abrupt ending with no further development
A tone of anger that never resolves in any way
Some form of consolation or acceptance

quiz.q: Which is an example of a subject an elegy might commemorate?
options: An upcoming celebration with no connection to loss
The death of a loved one
A purely hypothetical event that never actually occurred
A subject entirely unrelated to loss or commemoration

quiz.q: Why might a writer use vivid, sensory imagery when composing an elegy?
options: Sensory detail can help preserve and honour a specific memory of what has been lost
Elegies are always written using flat, unemotional language with no imagery
Imagery has no connection to how an elegy conveys meaning
This technique has no relevance to commemorative writing

quiz.q: Why might writing an elegy be considered a meaningful way for a writer to process grief?
options: An elegy is only ever written for a stranger, with no personal connection to the writer
This concept has no connection to the purpose of commemorative writing
Writing about a difficult experience never has any emotional value for the writer
Putting loss into words can help a writer reflect on and find some sense of meaning in a difficult experience

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Number Theory: The Real Number System
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the real number system organizes numbers into nested categories — natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers, and irrational numbers — each broader category containing the ones before it.

quiz.q: A rational number is best described as a number that can be expressed as ___.
options: A concept unrelated to the real number system
A number that cannot be written as a fraction under any circumstances
A ratio of two integers, with a non-zero denominator
A decimal that never ends and never repeats

quiz.q: An irrational number is best described as a number whose decimal representation ___.
options: Always terminates after a small number of digits
Always repeats in an identical, predictable pattern
Never ends and never repeats in a pattern
A concept unrelated to the real number system

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of an irrational number?
options: Pi (the ratio of a circle’s circumference to its diameter)
The whole number 4
One-half, expressed as the fraction 1/2
A number entirely unrelated to the real number system

quiz.q: Why are all integers also considered rational numbers?
options: Every integer can be expressed as a ratio of itself to 1, satisfying the definition of a rational number
Integers and rational numbers describe two entirely separate, non-overlapping categories
This relationship has no connection to how numbers are classified
Integers can never be expressed as a ratio of two whole numbers

quiz.q: Why is understanding the nested structure of the real number system useful when solving equations, such as recognizing when a solution is irrational?
options: This structure has no connection to solving or interpreting equations
This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no practical use
Every solution to every equation is always a rational number
It helps identify what kind of number a solution actually is, which can affect how that solution is interpreted or approximated

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Human Biology: The Brain — Structure and Higher Function
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: the human brain is organized into regions, including the cerebrum, cerebellum, and brainstem, each responsible for different functions ranging from voluntary movement and higher-order thinking to basic life-sustaining processes.

quiz.q: The cerebrum is primarily responsible for ___.
options: Higher-order thinking, sensory processing, and voluntary movement
A concept unrelated to the brain’s structure
Only regulating heart rate, with no connection to thought
Producing red blood cells exclusively

quiz.q: The cerebellum primarily coordinates ___.
options: Balance and fine motor coordination
Long-term memory storage exclusively
Digestion of food within the stomach
A function unrelated to the brain’s structure

quiz.q: The brainstem is primarily responsible for regulating ___.
options: The five senses exclusively, with no connection to basic life functions
Complex, abstract problem-solving exclusively
Basic life-sustaining processes, such as breathing and heart rate
A concept unrelated to the brain’s structure

quiz.q: Why might damage to the cerebellum specifically affect a person’s balance and coordination, rather than their ability to think abstractly?
options: Different brain regions are specialized for different functions, so damage to one region primarily affects the processes it controls
This concept has no relevance to understanding brain structure
The cerebellum has no connection to controlling balance or coordination
Every region of the brain performs an identical function, so damage anywhere produces identical effects

quiz.q: Why is understanding the specialized regions of the brain useful in fields such as neurology and psychology?
options: It helps explain how specific injuries or conditions might affect particular abilities, such as movement, memory, or language
Every function of the brain is controlled equally by every brain region
This concept has no practical application outside of basic biology
Brain structure has no connection to understanding injury or illness

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Food Chemistry and the Maillard Reaction
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: the Maillard reaction is a chemical reaction between amino acids and reducing sugars that occurs when food is heated, producing the browning, flavour, and aroma characteristic of foods such as toasted bread and seared meat.

quiz.q: The Maillard reaction occurs between amino acids and ___.
options: Salt crystals, with no connection to amino acids
A substance unrelated to food chemistry
Reducing sugars
Water molecules exclusively, with no connection to sugars

quiz.q: The Maillard reaction is primarily responsible for producing a food’s ___.
options: A property unrelated to food chemistry
Colour before it has been heated at all
Exact nutritional content, with no connection to browning
Browning, flavour, and aroma when heated

quiz.q: Why does the Maillard reaction typically require heat in order to occur?
options: This reaction only occurs at temperatures below freezing
The Maillard reaction occurs at an identical rate regardless of temperature
Heat has no connection to the chemical reaction responsible for browning food
Heat provides the energy needed for the amino acids and sugars to react and form new flavour and colour compounds

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a food where the Maillard reaction produces a noticeable effect?
options: An example entirely unrelated to food chemistry
Seared meat developing a browned, flavourful crust
A food that shows no change at all when heated
A glass of cold water left at room temperature

quiz.q: Why is understanding the Maillard reaction useful for both home cooks and the food industry?
options: This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
The Maillard reaction has no practical application in cooking or food preparation
Cooking temperature has no effect on a food’s flavour or appearance
It helps explain how cooking temperature and time can be controlled to achieve a desired flavour, aroma, and appearance

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Independent Reading: Postmodern Fiction and Fragmented Narrative
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: postmodern fiction often rejects a single, linear plot in favour of a fragmented narrative structure, non-traditional chronology, and self-aware storytelling that challenges a reader’s expectations of how a story should be told.

quiz.q: Postmodern fiction often rejects a ___ in favour of a fragmented narrative structure.
options: Story with any characters at all
Story that contains any dialogue whatsoever
Single, linear plot
A concept unrelated to narrative structure

quiz.q: A fragmented narrative structure is best described as one that ___.
options: Always presents events in strict chronological order with no exceptions
Contains only a single scene with no other narrative content
A concept unrelated to postmodern fiction
Presents a story in disconnected or non-chronological pieces

quiz.q: Why might a postmodern novel present events out of chronological order?
options: Postmodern fiction always presents events in strict chronological order
This structure can mirror the fragmented, non-linear way memory or perception can actually work
Chronological order has no connection to how a story is structured
A fragmented structure always makes a story easier to follow than a linear one

quiz.q: Why might postmodern fiction draw attention to its own artificiality as a constructed story, similar to metafiction?
options: Postmodern fiction always presents itself as a completely objective, factual account
It can challenge a reader’s assumption that a story presents a single, objective version of reality
Drawing attention to a story’s construction has no effect on how a reader interprets it
This technique has no connection to postmodern literary traditions

quiz.q: Why might reading fragmented, postmodern narratives build valuable interpretive skills for a student?
options: This type of reading has no connection to building literary analysis skills
Piecing together a non-linear structure requires active inference and a tolerance for ambiguity
Fragmented narratives require no interpretive effort from a reader at all
A reason unrelated to independent reading

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Quadratic Relations: Introduction to Conic Sections (Circles)
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a circle is a conic section defined as the set of all points equidistant from a fixed centre point, and its equation can be written in standard form using the coordinates of the centre and the length of the radius.

quiz.q: A circle is defined as the set of all points that are ___ from a fixed centre point.
options: Equidistant
At a constantly changing distance, with no fixed relationship
A concept unrelated to conic sections
Located directly on the centre point itself

quiz.q: In the standard form equation of a circle, the value r represents the circle’s ___.
options: Diameter, with no connection to the radius
Circumference, with no connection to the radius
Radius
A value unrelated to a circle’s equation

quiz.q: For a circle with the equation x squared plus y squared equals 25, what is the radius of the circle?
options: A value unrelated to this equation

quiz.q: Why is a circle considered a type of conic section?
options: A circle can only ever be created by slicing a cube, not a cone
A concept unrelated to how conic sections are defined
Circles have no mathematical relationship to a cone of any kind
It can be formed by slicing a cone with a plane perpendicular to the cone’s axis

quiz.q: Why is being able to identify a circle’s centre and radius directly from its standard form equation useful for graphing it quickly?
options: This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no practical use
The standard form equation provides no useful information for graphing a circle
It allows the circle to be plotted immediately, without needing to generate and plot a long table of individual points
A circle can never be graphed using information from its equation alone

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Freshwater Ecosystems and Watershed Health
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: freshwater ecosystems, including lakes, rivers, and wetlands, form part of larger watersheds, and the health of these systems depends on factors such as water quality, nutrient levels, and the surrounding land use within that watershed.

quiz.q: A watershed is best described as an area of land that ___.
options: A concept unrelated to freshwater ecosystems
Drains into a common body of water, such as a river or lake
Never has any connection to a body of water
Contains only a single isolated pond with no surrounding drainage

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a freshwater ecosystem?
options: A coral reef found in the open ocean
An ecosystem entirely unrelated to freshwater
A wetland
A desert with no permanent water source

quiz.q: Why might excess nutrient runoff from surrounding farmland negatively affect the health of a freshwater lake within its watershed?
options: This concept has no relevance to understanding freshwater ecosystems
Nutrient runoff always improves the overall health of a freshwater ecosystem
Excess nutrients can trigger algal blooms that deplete oxygen levels in the water as they decompose
Land use within a watershed has no effect on the water quality of a connected lake

quiz.q: Why are wetlands often described as valuable for filtering pollutants before they reach a larger body of water?
options: Pollutants are never filtered or reduced by any natural process within a wetland
Wetland vegetation and soil can trap and break down certain pollutants as water slowly moves through them
This concept has no relevance to understanding watershed health
Wetlands have no effect on the water quality of a connected watershed

quiz.q: Why is understanding the connection between land use and water quality important for protecting freshwater ecosystems within a watershed?
options: Human activity anywhere within a watershed can ultimately affect the water quality of the freshwater systems it drains into
This concept has no relevance to ecological conservation efforts
Freshwater ecosystems are always completely unaffected by human activity
Land use has no meaningful connection to the health of a freshwater ecosystem

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Phase Diagrams and Sublimation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a phase diagram shows the conditions of temperature and pressure under which a substance exists as a solid, liquid, or gas, and sublimation is the direct transition from a solid to a gas without passing through a liquid state.

quiz.q: A phase diagram shows the conditions of ___ under which a substance exists as a solid, liquid, or gas.
options: Mass and volume exclusively, with no connection to phase
Temperature and pressure
Colour and density exclusively, with no connection to phase
A concept unrelated to a substance’s physical state

quiz.q: Sublimation is best described as a direct transition from a ___ to a gas.
options: Solid, without passing through a liquid state
Gas, with no connection to a change of state at all
A concept unrelated to phase changes
Liquid, without passing through a solid state

quiz.q: Which of these is a commonly cited example of a substance that readily sublimates at everyday pressures?
options: A substance entirely unrelated to sublimation
Table salt dissolved in water
Dry ice (solid carbon dioxide)
Liquid water at room temperature

quiz.q: On a phase diagram, the triple point represents the unique condition at which a substance can exist ___.
options: A concept unrelated to phase diagrams
Only as a solid, with no other phase possible
As a solid, liquid, and gas simultaneously, in equilibrium
Only as a gas, with no other phase possible

quiz.q: Why is a phase diagram a useful tool for predicting how a substance will behave under a specific set of conditions, such as at a very high altitude?
options: This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
A phase diagram provides no useful information about how a substance behaves under different conditions
Temperature and pressure have no connection to the phase a substance takes
It shows exactly which phase a substance will be in at a given combination of temperature and pressure

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Review: Epistolary Novels, Manifestos, and Fragmented Narrative
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: this lesson revisits the epistolary novel, the persuasive manifesto, news bias and fact-checking, debate rebuttal and cross-examination, the character study essay, cohesion and coherence, the confessional poem, the elegy, and postmodern fragmented narrative.

quiz.q: An epistolary novel tells its story primarily through ___.
options: A single omniscient narrator describing events from outside the story
A series of stage directions with no narration at all
A concept unrelated to novel structure
Documents such as letters, diary entries, or emails

quiz.q: A manifesto is best described as a public declaration of ___.
options: A private, confidential opinion never meant to be shared
Purely factual, statistical data with no viewpoint expressed
Beliefs and intentions
A concept unrelated to persuasive writing

quiz.q: An elegy is best described as a reflective piece of writing composed to ___.
options: Provide a purely factual, unemotional record of an event
A concept unrelated to commemorative writing
Celebrate an achievement with no connection to loss or grief
Mourn or commemorate someone or something that has been lost

quiz.q: A fragmented narrative structure is best described as one that ___.
options: Always presents events in strict chronological order with no exceptions
A concept unrelated to postmodern fiction
Contains only a single scene with no other narrative content
Presents a story in disconnected or non-chronological pieces

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review these varied reading, writing, and communication skills together?
options: Review is never useful for English language skills
These skills have no connection to each other
They reinforce complementary approaches to interpreting and producing texts effectively
Each skill must be studied with no connection to the others

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Review: Discrete Math, Trigonometry, and Number Systems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand review: this lesson revisits set theory and Venn diagrams, graph theory, the ambiguous case of the sine law, measures of central tendency and spread, optimization with quadratic models, solving equations graphically versus algebraically, systems of three linear equations, the real number system, and conic sections.

quiz.q: A set is best described as ___.
options: A well-defined collection of distinct objects
A concept unrelated to discrete mathematics
A single object with no connection to a collection
A collection that may repeat the same object many times

quiz.q: The ambiguous case of the sine law arises when a triangle is defined by ___.
options: Three sides and no angles at all
A concept unrelated to solving triangles
Two angles and no sides at all
Two sides and a non-included angle

quiz.q: The median of a data set is best described as ___.
options: The difference between the largest and smallest values
A concept unrelated to central tendency
The middle value when the data is arranged in order
The value that appears most often in the data set

quiz.q: An irrational number is best described as a number whose decimal representation ___.
options: Never ends and never repeats in a pattern
Always terminates after a small number of digits
A concept unrelated to the real number system
Always repeats in an identical, predictable pattern

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review discrete mathematics, trigonometry, and number systems together?
options: Each topic must be learned in complete isolation
It reinforces how these mathematical tools and reasoning skills connect and build on one another
These topics have no connection to each other
Review is never useful in math

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Review: Genetics, Anatomy, and Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: this lesson revisits sex-linked inheritance and pedigree analysis, the Hardy-Weinberg principle, comparative anatomy, extremophiles, pollination strategies, bioinformatics, animal adaptations to extreme environments, the brain, and freshwater ecosystems.

quiz.q: A sex-linked trait is carried on ___.
options: A structure found only in plant cells
A concept unrelated to inheritance
The X or Y chromosome
An autosome that is unrelated to sex chromosomes

quiz.q: A homologous structure is best described as a feature that shares a ___ despite serving a different function across species.
options: A concept unrelated to comparative anatomy
Completely unrelated form across every species
Similar underlying form
Identical function, with no connection to structure

quiz.q: An extremophile is best described as an organism that ___.
options: Requires an environment identical to that of most other organisms
Thrives in conditions once thought too harsh for life
A concept unrelated to biology
Can only survive in mild, temperate environments

quiz.q: A watershed is best described as an area of land that ___.
options: A concept unrelated to freshwater ecosystems
Drains into a common body of water, such as a river or lake
Never has any connection to a body of water
Contains only a single isolated pond with no surrounding drainage

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review genetics, anatomy, and ecosystem concepts together?
options: Each topic must be studied with no connection to the others
Review is never useful in biology
These topics have no connection to each other
It reinforces how these interconnected biological concepts relate to one another

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Review: Atomic Trends, Analytical Techniques, and Applied Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand review: this lesson revisits periodic trends in atomic properties, empirical and molecular formula determination, colorimetry, acid rain, photochemistry, flame tests, surfactant chemistry, food chemistry, and phase diagrams.

quiz.q: Atomic radius generally ___ across a period from left to right.
options: Stays exactly the same in every case
A pattern unrelated to atomic structure
Decreases
Increases, with no connection to nuclear charge

quiz.q: Beer’s law describes a direct relationship between a solution’s absorbance and its ___.
options: Physical volume, with no connection to concentration
A property unrelated to colorimetry
Concentration
Exact temperature, with no connection to absorbance

quiz.q: The characteristic colour seen in a flame test results from an electron ___.
options: Splitting the nucleus of the atom into smaller fragments
Falling back to a lower energy level and releasing energy as light
Being permanently removed from the atom, with no return possible
A process unrelated to atomic emission

quiz.q: Sublimation is best described as a direct transition from a ___ to a gas.
options: A concept unrelated to phase changes
Gas, with no connection to a change of state at all
Liquid, without passing through a solid state
Solid, without passing through a liquid state

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review atomic trends, analytical techniques, and applied chemistry together?
options: Review is never useful in chemistry
It reinforces how these interconnected chemistry concepts relate to one another
These topics have no connection to each other
Each topic must be studied with no connection to the others

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: Absurdist Fiction and the Theatre of the Absurd
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: absurdist literature, exemplified by playwrights such as Samuel Beckett and Eugène Ionesco, portrays a universe that resists rational explanation, using illogical plots, circular dialogue, and characters trapped in meaningless routines to dramatize the human search for purpose in an indifferent world.

quiz.q: Absurdist literature typically portrays a universe that ___.
options: A concept unrelated to literary movements
Always resolves every conflict with a clear, satisfying moral
Resists rational explanation or meaning
Follows a strictly logical and orderly plot at every turn

quiz.q: Which is a stylistic feature commonly associated with the Theatre of the Absurd?
options: A feature entirely unrelated to absurdist drama
Illogical plots and circular, repetitive dialogue
A tightly logical plot with no repetition of any kind
Dialogue that always builds toward a clear resolution

quiz.q: Why might absurdist playwrights use characters trapped in meaningless, repetitive routines?
options: The repetition can dramatize a sense of purposelessness in an indifferent universe
Repetitive routines always signal that a story has a clear, logical purpose
This technique has no connection to the themes of absurdist drama
Absurdist plays never depict any form of repeated action

quiz.q: Why might a reader initially find an absurdist play confusing or frustrating before recognizing its purpose?
options: Absurdist plays always follow the same predictable structure as a traditional play
A reason unrelated to the goals of absurdist literature
Confusion has no connection to how absurdist drama achieves its effect
The play deliberately withholds conventional plot logic to convey a world without inherent meaning

quiz.q: Why is the Theatre of the Absurd often connected to the philosophical idea that human existence lacks inherent meaning?
options: Its illogical, fragmented style enacts that philosophical idea directly through form rather than only stating it
This movement always presents existence as having a single, clear, universal purpose
A reason unrelated to the movement’s philosophical roots
Absurdist drama has no connection to philosophical ideas about meaning or existence

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Algebra strand: a rational expression is a fraction with polynomials in the numerator and denominator, and simplifying it involves factoring and cancelling common factors.

quiz.q: A rational expression is best described as ___.
options: A fraction with polynomials in the numerator and denominator
A whole number with no fractions involved
An expression with no variables at all
A fraction that can never be simplified

quiz.q: Simplifying a rational expression typically involves ___.
options: Adding all terms together with no factoring
Ignoring the denominator entirely
Factoring and cancelling common factors
Multiplying the numerator by an unrelated number

quiz.q: Simplify the rational expression (x squared minus 4) over (x minus 2).
options: x squared minus 2

quiz.q: Why is it important to identify restrictions (values that make the denominator zero) when simplifying rational expressions?
options: Division by zero is undefined, so those values must be excluded from the domain
Simplifying never requires considering the denominator’s value
The denominator can always safely equal zero
Restrictions have no relevance to rational expressions

quiz.q: Why might factoring be a necessary first step before simplifying a rational expression?
options: It reveals common factors in the numerator and denominator that can be cancelled
Common factors are never present in these expressions
Factoring has no connection to simplifying rational expressions
Rational expressions can only be simplified without factoring

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biochemistry: Enzyme Structure, Function, and Inhibition
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: enzymes are protein catalysts with a specific active site that binds a substrate, lowering the activation energy needed for a reaction, and their activity can be reduced by inhibitors that block or alter that active site.

quiz.q: An enzyme is best described as a protein that functions as a ___.
options: Source of long-term energy storage exclusively
Catalyst that speeds up a chemical reaction
A concept unrelated to biochemistry
Structural fibre with no chemical role at all

quiz.q: The specific region of an enzyme where a substrate binds is called the ___.
options: Nucleus
Cell wall
Active site
A structure unrelated to enzyme function

quiz.q: Why does an enzyme typically only bind to one specific substrate or a small group of similar substrates?
options: Substrate specificity has no connection to an enzyme’s active site
Every enzyme can bind equally well to any substrate molecule
The active site’s shape and chemical properties fit only molecules with a complementary structure
Enzymes never interact with any substrate in a specific way

quiz.q: Why does an enzyme lower the activation energy required for a reaction to proceed?
options: Enzymes always raise the activation energy needed for a reaction
Activation energy has no connection to how an enzyme functions
It stabilizes the transition state of the reaction, making it easier for the reaction to occur
This effect has no basis in the chemistry of enzyme catalysis

quiz.q: Why might a competitive inhibitor reduce an enzyme’s activity by binding directly to its active site?
options: It can block the actual substrate from binding, reducing the rate at which the enzyme catalyzes the reaction
Competitive inhibitors always increase how quickly an enzyme catalyzes a reaction
An enzyme’s active site can never be blocked by another molecule
Inhibitors have no connection to how an enzyme’s active site functions

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Stoichiometry: Hydrates and Water of Crystallization
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a hydrate is an ionic compound with a fixed number of water molecules incorporated into its crystal structure, known as water of crystallization, and heating a hydrate drives off that water, allowing its formula to be determined from the resulting mass loss.

quiz.q: A hydrate is best described as an ionic compound that incorporates a fixed number of ___ within its crystal structure.
options: A component unrelated to hydrate compounds
Water molecules
Carbon atoms exclusively
Oxygen atoms exclusively

quiz.q: The water incorporated into a hydrate’s crystal structure is known as ___.
options: A substance unrelated to hydrate chemistry
Heavy water exclusively
Water of crystallization
Distilled water exclusively

quiz.q: Why does heating a hydrate typically cause a measurable decrease in its mass?
options: Hydrates never lose any mass when heated under any conditions
The water of crystallization is driven off as vapour, leaving only the anhydrous compound behind
Heating a hydrate always increases its total mass instead of decreasing it
Mass loss has no connection to the water contained within a hydrate

quiz.q: Why is the mass lost during heating used to help determine a hydrate’s chemical formula?
options: A hydrate’s formula can only ever be determined without any reference to mass
This concept only applies to compounds that contain no water at all
Comparing the mass of water lost to the mass of the remaining anhydrous compound reveals the mole ratio between them
Mass measurements provide no useful information for determining a hydrate’s formula

quiz.q: Why might a hydrate’s crystals change in appearance, such as losing their defined shape, after being heated and losing water?
options: Removing water from a hydrate’s structure never has any visible effect on its appearance
