Removing the water of crystallization can disrupt the structure that gave the original crystal its defined shape
A hydrate’s crystal shape has no connection to the water contained within it
This concept has no basis in the chemistry of hydrate compounds

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: The Dramatic Monologue — Voice and Persona
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a dramatic monologue is a poem spoken entirely in the voice of a single fictional or historical speaker addressing a silent listener, revealing that speaker’s character, motives, and blind spots through what they say and how they say it.

quiz.q: A dramatic monologue is a poem spoken entirely in the voice of ___.
options: A single fictional or historical speaker addressing a silent listener
A narrator who never expresses any specific point of view
Multiple speakers taking turns throughout the poem
A concept unrelated to poetic form

quiz.q: In a dramatic monologue, the poem’s speaker is best understood as ___.
options: A character who never reveals anything about themself
A concept unrelated to dramatic monologue
A persona distinct from the poet, who reveals their own character through their words
Always identical to the poet writing the poem

quiz.q: Why might a dramatic monologue reveal more about its speaker than the speaker consciously intends to share?
options: Dramatic monologues always present a speaker who is fully aware of every flaw they reveal
A speaker in a dramatic monologue can never reveal anything unintentionally
A reader can notice gaps or contradictions between what the speaker claims and how they actually behave or speak
This effect has no connection to how a dramatic monologue is constructed

quiz.q: Why is the presence of a silent, implied listener significant in a dramatic monologue?
options: This concept has no relevance to interpreting a dramatic monologue
A dramatic monologue never involves any implied listener within the poem
The speaker’s words are shaped by an audience within the poem, giving the monologue a sense of dramatic occasion and urgency
The listener’s presence has no effect on how the speaker’s words are shaped

quiz.q: Why might a poet choose a dramatic monologue over first-person confessional poetry to explore a troubling perspective?
options: Adopting a persona lets the poet examine a perspective critically without it being mistaken for the poet’s own view
Confessional poetry and dramatic monologue are always identical in form and effect
A dramatic monologue always expresses the poet’s own personal opinion directly
This choice has no connection to how a poet might want a perspective to be received

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to Modular Arithmetic
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Number strand (pre-high-school extension): modular arithmetic involves working with remainders after division, often used in real-world contexts like telling time on a 12-hour clock.

quiz.q: Modular arithmetic focuses on ___.
options: The remainder after division
Only whole numbers with no remainders
Ignoring division entirely
A concept unrelated to division

quiz.q: On a 12-hour clock, 15 o’clock would correspond to which hour, using modular arithmetic?
options: 15 o’clock exactly, with no adjustment
3 o’clock
12 o’clock
5 o’clock

quiz.q: What is 17 mod 5 (the remainder when 17 is divided by 5)?
Why is modular arithmetic useful for understanding clocks and calendars?
options: Modular arithmetic has no real-world applications
Clocks and calendars have no connection to remainders
These systems repeat in cycles, similar to how remainders repeat in modular arithmetic
Time never involves any repeating patterns

quiz.q: What is 22 mod 7 (the remainder when 22 is divided by 7)?

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Molecular Biology: DNA Replication, Transcription, and Translation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: DNA replication copies a cell’s genetic material before division, transcription copies a gene’s DNA sequence into messenger RNA, and translation uses that RNA sequence at the ribosome to assemble a specific chain of amino acids into a protein.

quiz.q: DNA replication is best described as the process that ___.
options: Converts RNA directly into a finished protein
Breaks down proteins into individual amino acids
A concept unrelated to molecular biology
Copies a cell’s genetic material before cell division

quiz.q: Transcription is best described as the process that copies a gene’s DNA sequence into ___.
options: A second, identical strand of DNA
A concept unrelated to molecular biology
Messenger RNA
A finished, folded protein directly

quiz.q: Why is DNA replication described as semi-conservative, producing two DNA molecules each containing one original and one new strand?
options: DNA replication always produces molecules built entirely from new material, with no original strand retained
Semi-conservative replication means that DNA is destroyed rather than copied
This description has no connection to how DNA replication actually occurs
Each original strand serves as a template for building a new complementary strand, so every resulting molecule retains half of the original DNA

quiz.q: Why must messenger RNA travel to a ribosome for translation to occur?
options: This process has no connection to where translation physically takes place in a cell
The ribosome is the cellular structure that reads the RNA sequence and assembles the corresponding chain of amino acids
Ribosomes have no role in converting an RNA sequence into a protein
Translation can occur anywhere in the cell with no involvement of the ribosome at all

quiz.q: Why is the flow of information from DNA to RNA to protein often called the central dogma of molecular biology?
options: Protein is always built directly from DNA with no RNA intermediate involved
This concept has no connection to how genetic information is expressed
This sequence of information flow has no broader significance in molecular biology
It describes the fundamental sequence most genetic information follows on its way to building a functional protein

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Gas Laws: The Ideal Gas Law and Molar Volume
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: the ideal gas law, PV = nRT, relates a gas’s pressure, volume, moles, and temperature in a single equation, building on Boyle’s and Charles’s laws, and at standard temperature and pressure one mole of an ideal gas occupies a molar volume of about 22.4 litres.

quiz.q: The ideal gas law relates a gas’s pressure, volume, number of moles, and ___.
options: A quantity unrelated to the behaviour of gases
Temperature
Colour
Density exclusively, with no connection to the other variables

quiz.q: At standard temperature and pressure, one mole of an ideal gas occupies a molar volume of approximately ___.
options: 22.4 litres
1 litre
100 litres
A volume unrelated to molar volume

quiz.q: Why is the ideal gas law considered a combination of the earlier gas laws, such as Boyle’s and Charles’s laws?
options: Boyle’s and Charles’s laws describe relationships that contradict the ideal gas law
The ideal gas law has no mathematical connection to Boyle’s or Charles’s laws
This concept only applies to a single, narrow situation with no broader connection
It incorporates the same relationships those earlier laws describe while also accounting for the number of moles of gas present

quiz.q: Why does the ideal gas law assume that gas particles have negligible volume and no intermolecular attractions?
options: The ideal gas law was designed specifically to describe liquids, not gases
This assumption has no connection to how the ideal gas law was developed
This simplification makes the mathematical relationship manageable while still closely approximating the behaviour of many real gases under common conditions
Real gas particles always have enormous volume and extremely strong intermolecular attractions

quiz.q: Why might a real gas deviate noticeably from ideal gas law predictions under very high pressure or very low temperature?
options: Real gases always behave identically to an ideal gas under every possible condition
Pressure and temperature have no connection to how closely a real gas matches ideal gas behaviour
Under those conditions, the volume of gas particles and the attractions between them become significant enough to no longer be negligible
This concept has no basis in the physical behaviour of real gases

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Data Visualization and Statistical Rhetoric in Reporting
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: journalists and advertisers often use graphs and charts to support a claim, and choices such as a truncated axis, an inconsistent scale, or a cherry-picked time frame can make a data visualization technically accurate yet visually misleading to an unwary reader.

quiz.q: A data visualization used in a news report can be technically accurate yet still ___.
options: Visually misleading, based on choices such as a truncated axis or scale
Impossible to construct using real data
A concept unrelated to media literacy
Guaranteed to represent every possible interpretation fairly

quiz.q: A truncated axis on a bar graph refers to an axis that ___.
options: A feature unrelated to data visualization
Does not begin at zero, exaggerating the apparent difference between values
Always begins at zero with no possible exaggeration
Displays every single data point without exception

quiz.q: Why might selecting a narrow, cherry-picked time frame distort how a trend appears in a graph?
options: A cherry-picked time frame always reveals the complete, unbiased picture of a trend
Time frame has no effect on how a trend appears in a data visualization
This concept has no connection to statistical rhetoric in reporting
A short window can hide a longer-term pattern, making a temporary fluctuation look like a significant trend

quiz.q: Why is it useful for a critical reader to check the scale and labels of a graph before accepting its implied conclusion?
options: Every graph published in a credible source is guaranteed to use an unbiased scale
Checking a graph’s scale and labels never affects how its implied conclusion should be interpreted
This concept has no relevance to evaluating media messages
Careful labels reveal whether the visual difference between values genuinely reflects the size of the underlying difference

quiz.q: Why might understanding statistical rhetoric be considered an extension of the media literacy skills used to detect other forms of bias, such as biased word choice?
options: This concept has no relevance to developing critical media literacy skills
Both require a reader to look past a surface presentation to evaluate how a message has been shaped to support a particular impression
Data visualizations can never be used to shape a reader’s impression of an issue
Statistical rhetoric has no connection to other forms of bias found in media

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to the Quadratic Formula
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Algebra strand (pre-high-school extension): the quadratic formula, x equals negative b plus or minus the square root of b squared minus 4ac all over 2a, can be used to solve any quadratic equation in the form ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Introduction to the Quadratic Formula

quiz.q: The quadratic formula is used to solve equations in the form ___.
options: ax squared plus bx plus c equals zero
a plus b equals c
ax plus b equals zero
a divided by b equals c

quiz.q: In the quadratic formula, which symbol represents the coefficient of the x squared term?
options: c
b
x
a

quiz.q: The quadratic formula includes a square root of ___.
options: c squared minus a
b squared minus 4ac
a squared plus b squared
b plus c

quiz.q: Why is the quadratic formula considered a powerful tool in algebra?
options: The quadratic formula has no practical use in algebra
It only works for linear equations, not quadratics
It can only be used with equations that are already factored
It can solve any quadratic equation, even ones that are difficult to factor

quiz.q: For the equation x squared plus 3x plus 2 equals zero, what are the values of a, b, and c?

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Taxonomy: Binomial Nomenclature and the Three-Domain System
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: binomial nomenclature assigns every species a standardized two-part Latin name consisting of its genus and species, while the three-domain system — Bacteria, Archaea, and Eukarya — organizes all life into broad categories based on fundamental cellular differences.

quiz.q: Binomial nomenclature assigns every species a standardized name consisting of its ___.
options: Genus and species
A concept unrelated to biological classification
Common name and country of origin
Family and order exclusively

quiz.q: The three-domain system organizes all life into the domains Bacteria, Archaea, and ___.
options: A domain unrelated to the three-domain system
Eukarya
Fungi, exclusively separate from all other domains
Protista, exclusively separate from all other domains

quiz.q: Why is a standardized, Latin-based binomial name useful for scientists communicating about a species across different countries and languages?
options: This system has no practical benefit for international scientific communication
Common names are always more precise than a standardized binomial name
Binomial names change depending on the country in which a scientist is working
It provides a single, universally recognized name that avoids the confusion caused by many different common names

quiz.q: Why are Bacteria and Archaea classified as separate domains despite both consisting of single-celled organisms without a nucleus?
options: Differences in their cell membrane chemistry and genetic machinery reveal they are not as closely related as their similar appearance suggests
Bacteria and Archaea are always classified within the exact same domain
This distinction has no basis in actual cellular or genetic differences
Domain classification depends only on whether an organism has a nucleus, with no other criteria considered

quiz.q: Why might the three-domain system be considered a more accurate reflection of evolutionary relationships than older classification systems based mainly on visible physical traits?
options: This concept has no relevance to the modern study of taxonomy
It relies on genetic and biochemical evidence that can reveal deep evolutionary divisions not always visible through physical appearance alone
Physical appearance always provides a completely accurate picture of evolutionary relationships
Genetic evidence never reveals any information relevant to classifying organisms

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Organic Chemistry: Aromatic Compounds and Benzene Derivatives
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: aromatic compounds are built around a benzene ring, a stable six-carbon ring with alternating bonds often represented as a delocalized system of electrons, giving these compounds distinct properties from other hydrocarbons and forming the basis of many dyes, medicines, and plastics.

quiz.q: Aromatic compounds are built around a stable six-carbon ring structure known as a ___.
options: Five-carbon ring exclusively
Straight-chain alkane
Benzene ring
A concept unrelated to organic chemistry

quiz.q: The bonding within a benzene ring is often represented as a system of ___ electrons distributed around the ring.
options: Delocalized
Completely absent, with no electrons involved at all
Fixed permanently between only two specific carbon atoms
A feature unrelated to aromatic compounds

quiz.q: Why is the delocalization of electrons around a benzene ring associated with its unusual chemical stability?
options: This concept has no basis in the structure of aromatic compounds
Electron delocalization has no connection to the chemical stability of benzene
Spreading electron density around the entire ring lowers the molecule’s overall energy compared to a structure with fixed, alternating single and double bonds
Delocalized electrons always make a molecule less stable than one with fixed bonds

quiz.q: Why do many dyes, medicines, and plastics contain a benzene ring or a similar aromatic structure?
options: The aromatic ring provides a stable structural foundation that can be modified with different attached groups to produce a wide range of properties
Benzene rings have no practical role in the chemistry of dyes, medicines, or plastics
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry with no practical use
Aromatic rings are always chemically unstable and unsuitable for use in manufactured products

quiz.q: Why is benzene’s ring structure considered distinct from a simple straight-chain or branched hydrocarbon of the same number of carbon atoms?
options: Ring structure has no effect on a hydrocarbon’s chemical properties
Benzene and a straight-chain hydrocarbon with the same number of carbons always behave identically
Its closed ring shape and delocalized electron system give it chemical and physical properties not shared by an open-chain hydrocarbon
This distinction has no basis in the actual structure of these molecules

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Independent Reading: Literary Journalism and Creative Non-Fiction
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: literary journalism applies techniques usually associated with fiction, such as scene-setting, dialogue, and a developed narrative voice, to factual reporting, producing creative non-fiction that aims to be both accurate and vivid.

quiz.q: Literary journalism applies techniques usually associated with fiction, such as ___, to factual reporting.
options: Purely statistical data presented with no narrative element at all
Scene-setting, dialogue, and a developed narrative voice
A complete disregard for factual accuracy
A concept unrelated to non-fiction writing

quiz.q: Creative non-fiction aims to be both accurate and ___.
options: A concept unrelated to creative non-fiction
Vivid, or engaging in its telling
Entirely free of any narrative structure
Written using only fictional, invented events

quiz.q: Why might a literary journalist include specific sensory details about a real setting, rather than only reporting facts in a neutral summary?
options: Sensory detail can immerse a reader in an actual event the way a well-crafted scene does in fiction
Neutral, fact-only summaries are always the most effective way to engage a reader
This technique has no connection to how literary journalism is written
Sensory detail always undermines the factual accuracy of a piece of journalism

quiz.q: Why must a literary journalist balance the narrative techniques of fiction with a responsibility to represent real events accurately?
options: This balance has no relevance to how creative non-fiction is evaluated
Accuracy and narrative technique have no connection to one another in literary journalism
Using fiction-like techniques irresponsibly could mislead a reader into doubting where factual reporting ends and creative embellishment begins
A literary journalist has no responsibility to represent real events accurately

quiz.q: Why might literary journalism be considered a valuable bridge between the reporting skills developed in media literacy study and the narrative skills developed in fiction writing?
options: Reporting skills and narrative skills can never be combined in a single piece of writing
This concept has no relevance to studying different forms of writing
It shows how the two skill sets can combine to make factual material more engaging without sacrificing accuracy
Literary journalism has no meaningful connection to either media literacy or fiction writing

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to Cubic Functions
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Algebra strand (non-linear relations): a cubic function, such as y equals x cubed, produces a curved graph distinct from both linear and quadratic relations, often with an S-shaped or inflected pattern.

quiz.q: A cubic function includes a variable raised to the power of ___.
options: One
Zero
Two
Three

quiz.q: The graph of a basic cubic function, such as y equals x cubed, is often described as having a ___ shape.
options: A perfect circle
Perfectly straight
S-shaped or inflected
A simple U-shape identical to a parabola

quiz.q: How does a cubic function’s graph generally differ from a quadratic function’s graph?
options: Quadratic functions always have more complex graphs than cubic functions
They are always identical in shape
A cubic function never produces a curved graph
A cubic graph can have a different curve pattern, including an inflection point, unlike a parabola

quiz.q: What is the value of y when x equals 2 in the function y equals x cubed?
Why might cubic functions be used to model certain real-world situations?
options: Cubic functions can never model any real-world situation
This type of function has no practical application
Some real-world relationships involve more complex curvature than linear or quadratic models can capture
All real-world relationships are always linear

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Keystone Species and Trophic Cascades
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a keystone species has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance, and removing it can trigger a trophic cascade, a chain reaction of population changes that ripples through multiple feeding levels of the food web.

quiz.q: A keystone species is best described as a species that has ___.
options: No measurable effect on its ecosystem whatsoever
An effect on its ecosystem that is always exactly proportional to its abundance
A concept unrelated to ecology
A disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem relative to its abundance

quiz.q: A trophic cascade is best described as a chain reaction of population changes that ___.
options: Affects only a single species with no further consequences
A concept unrelated to ecosystem dynamics
Ripples through multiple feeding levels of a food web
Always remains confined to a single trophic level

quiz.q: Why might removing a top predator from an ecosystem trigger a trophic cascade affecting even the plant community?
options: Predators have no connection to the size of herbivore or plant populations
This concept has no basis in how food webs are actually structured
A predator’s absence can allow herbivore populations to grow unchecked, increasing grazing pressure on plants further down the food web
Removing a top predator always has no measurable effect on any other species in the ecosystem

quiz.q: Why is a sea otter often cited as an example of a keystone species in kelp forest ecosystems?
options: Kelp forests remain completely unaffected regardless of how many sea otters are present
Sea otters control sea urchin populations that would otherwise overgraze and destroy the kelp forest habitat
Sea otters have no measurable effect on sea urchin populations or kelp forest health
This example has no relevance to understanding keystone species

quiz.q: Why is identifying keystone species considered important for conservation and ecosystem management decisions?
options: Keystone species have no greater importance to an ecosystem than any other species present
Protecting a keystone species can help maintain the broader stability of an entire ecosystem more efficiently than protecting every species individually
This concept has no practical application in ecosystem management
Conservation decisions never need to consider how different species affect one another

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Nuclear Chemistry: Fission, Fusion, and Nuclear Power
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: nuclear fission splits a heavy atomic nucleus into smaller nuclei, releasing energy that commercial nuclear power plants harness, while nuclear fusion combines light nuclei into a heavier one, releasing even more energy per reaction but requiring extreme conditions to sustain.

quiz.q: Nuclear fission is best described as a process in which a heavy atomic nucleus ___.
options: A process unrelated to nuclear chemistry
Combines with another nucleus to form a single heavier nucleus
Remains completely unchanged while releasing energy
Splits into smaller nuclei, releasing energy

quiz.q: Nuclear fusion is best described as a process in which light nuclei ___.
options: Combine into a heavier nucleus, releasing energy
Remain completely unchanged while absorbing energy
A process unrelated to nuclear chemistry
Split apart into smaller, lighter nuclei

quiz.q: Why do commercial nuclear power plants currently rely on fission rather than fusion to generate electricity?
options: Fusion is already used in every commercial nuclear power plant currently operating
Fission and fusion require identical conditions to sustain a reaction
This distinction has no connection to the current state of nuclear power technology
Fission reactions can be sustained and controlled using current technology, while fusion requires extreme conditions that are still difficult to maintain reliably

quiz.q: Why does nuclear fusion release more energy per reaction than nuclear fission, according to current scientific understanding?
options: Combining light nuclei into a more stable heavier nucleus converts a comparatively large amount of mass into energy
Fusion reactions always release less energy than an equivalent fission reaction
This concept has no basis in nuclear chemistry
Energy release has no connection to the type of nuclear reaction taking place

quiz.q: Why are extremely high temperatures and pressures required to sustain a nuclear fusion reaction?
options: Overcoming the strong electrostatic repulsion between positively charged nuclei requires an enormous amount of energy to force them close enough to fuse
Temperature and pressure have no connection to whether a fusion reaction can be sustained
Fusion reactions can occur spontaneously at room temperature and normal atmospheric pressure
This concept has no basis in the physics of nuclear fusion

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: The Art of the Anecdote in Storytelling
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: an anecdote is a short, focused account of a real or realistic incident used within a speech or conversation to illustrate a larger point, and effective anecdotes rely on concrete detail, a clear structure, and a purposeful connection back to the speaker’s larger message.

quiz.q: An anecdote is best described as a short, focused account of a real or realistic incident used to ___.
options: Illustrate a larger point within a speech or conversation
A concept unrelated to oral communication
Distract an audience from the speaker’s actual message
Replace the need for any other form of evidence entirely

quiz.q: An effective anecdote typically relies on ___.
options: Vague, general statements with no specific detail at all
A quality unrelated to effective storytelling
A structure that deliberately avoids any connection to the speaker’s main point
Concrete detail and a clear structure

quiz.q: Why might a well-chosen anecdote make an abstract idea more memorable to a listening audience?
options: This technique has no connection to effective oral communication
A specific, concrete story can help an audience picture and emotionally connect with an idea that might otherwise remain abstract
Concrete detail has no effect on how memorable a spoken idea becomes
Anecdotes always make an abstract idea harder for an audience to understand

quiz.q: Why is it important for a speaker to clearly connect an anecdote back to their larger message, rather than leaving that connection unstated?
options: An anecdote never needs to connect to any larger point within a speech
Without a clear connection, an audience may enjoy the story but miss the point it was meant to illustrate
Audiences always understand the intended connection automatically, without it ever being stated
This concept has no relevance to effective public speaking

quiz.q: Why might over-relying on lengthy anecdotes weaken an otherwise well-organized speech?
options: Anecdotes of any length always strengthen a speech with no possible drawback
Speech length and structure have no connection to how effectively an anecdote is used
Excessive length can crowd out other important content and cause an audience to lose track of the speaker’s overall structure
This concept has no relevance to organizing an effective speech

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Trigonometry: Modelling Periodic Phenomena with Sinusoidal Functions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: many real-world phenomena, such as tides, sound waves, and seasonal temperature patterns, repeat in a regular cycle and can be modelled using a sinusoidal function, whose amplitude, period, and vertical shift correspond to measurable features of the phenomenon.

quiz.q: A sinusoidal function is well suited to modelling a real-world phenomenon that ___.
options: Increases without ever repeating or levelling off
A concept unrelated to modelling periodic behaviour
Repeats in a regular, predictable cycle
Changes in a completely random, unpredictable way

quiz.q: In a sinusoidal model, the amplitude corresponds to ___.
options: Half the difference between the maximum and minimum values of the phenomenon
A quantity unrelated to sinusoidal modelling
The vertical position of the midline of the graph
The exact time it takes for one complete cycle to occur

quiz.q: Why might the height of ocean tides at a particular location be modelled effectively using a sinusoidal function?
options: Tides rise and fall in a regular, repeating pattern closely resembling the shape of a sine or cosine curve
Sinusoidal functions can only model phenomena that never repeat
Tidal height changes in a completely random pattern that no mathematical function could model
This concept has no connection to how tides actually behave

quiz.q: Why does the period of a sinusoidal model correspond to the time required for one complete cycle of the phenomenon it represents?
options: The period of a sinusoidal function has no connection to how long a real cycle takes to repeat
A sinusoidal function’s period is always identical regardless of the phenomenon being modelled
This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no real-world use
The period is defined as the horizontal length needed for the function’s pattern to repeat itself exactly

quiz.q: Why might a vertical shift be added to a sinusoidal model of seasonal average temperature rather than using a plain sine or cosine function?
options: A vertical shift adjusts the midline of the graph to match the actual average value around which the temperature fluctuates
A vertical shift always changes how frequently the temperature pattern repeats
Vertical shifts have no connection to how a real-world average value is represented in a model
This concept has no relevance to modelling seasonal temperature data

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Human Health: Blood Glucose Regulation and Diabetes
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: blood glucose levels are regulated through a negative feedback system involving the hormones insulin and glucagon, released by the pancreas, and diabetes occurs when this regulation fails, either because the body produces too little insulin or cannot respond to it effectively.

quiz.q: Blood glucose levels are regulated primarily through a negative feedback system involving the hormones insulin and ___.
options: Melatonin, with no connection to glucose regulation
Adrenaline exclusively, with no connection to glucose regulation
A hormone unrelated to blood glucose regulation
Glucagon

quiz.q: Insulin and glucagon are both released by the ___.
options: Liver exclusively, with no involvement from any other organ
Kidneys exclusively, with no involvement from any other organ
A structure unrelated to blood glucose regulation
Pancreas

quiz.q: Why does insulin release increase after a meal high in carbohydrates?
options: This process has no basis in how the body regulates glucose
Rising blood glucose after digestion signals the pancreas to release insulin, which helps cells absorb the excess glucose
Insulin release always decreases after a meal high in carbohydrates
Blood glucose levels have no connection to the release of insulin

quiz.q: Why is glucagon considered to have an effect opposite to that of insulin on blood glucose levels?
options: Glucagon signals the liver to release stored glucose, raising blood glucose levels rather than lowering them
This concept has no basis in the physiology of glucose regulation
Glucagon has no measurable effect on blood glucose at all
Glucagon and insulin always produce an identical effect on blood glucose levels

quiz.q: Why does Type 1 diabetes typically require insulin injections, while Type 2 diabetes is often managed initially through diet, exercise, and other medications?
options: Type 1 and Type 2 diabetes always involve an identical underlying cause requiring an identical treatment
This distinction has no basis in the physiology of these two conditions
Type 1 diabetes involves very little or no insulin production, while Type 2 diabetes often involves cells that respond poorly to the insulin that is still produced
Insulin production has no connection to how diabetes is managed or treated

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Acids and Bases: Weak Acid and Base Equilibria (Ka and Kb)
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: unlike a strong acid or base, which ionizes completely in water, a weak acid or base only partially ionizes, establishing an equilibrium described by an acid or base ionization constant, Ka or Kb, that indicates the relative strength of that weak acid or base.

quiz.q: Unlike a strong acid, a weak acid in water ___.
options: Ionizes completely, leaving no un-ionized acid remaining
Only partially ionizes, establishing an equilibrium
Never ionizes at all under any circumstances
A behaviour unrelated to acid strength

quiz.q: The acid ionization constant, Ka, indicates the relative ___ of a weak acid.
options: Physical mass
A property unrelated to acid-base chemistry
Strength
Colour

quiz.q: Why does a weak acid establish an equilibrium between its ionized and un-ionized forms in solution, rather than fully converting to ions?
options: This concept has no basis in the chemistry of acids and bases
Equilibrium has no connection to how a weak acid behaves in solution
Only a fraction of the weak acid’s molecules react with water at any given time, leaving a dynamic balance between the two forms
Weak acids always convert completely into ions with no equilibrium established

quiz.q: Why does a larger Ka value indicate a relatively stronger weak acid compared to one with a smaller Ka value?
options: A larger Ka value always indicates a weaker acid than one with a smaller Ka value
This concept has no basis in acid-base equilibrium chemistry
The size of Ka has no connection to how readily an acid releases hydrogen ions
A larger Ka reflects a greater proportion of ionized acid at equilibrium, indicating the acid releases hydrogen ions more readily

quiz.q: Why is knowing whether an acid is strong or weak important when predicting the pH of a solution of a given concentration?
options: A weak acid ionizes only partially, so its solution will have a higher pH than an equally concentrated strong acid
Ionization behaviour has no connection to the pH of an acidic solution
Strong and weak acids of the same concentration always produce an identical pH
This concept has no practical application in predicting a solution’s pH

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: The Semicolon, Colon, and Sentence-Combining for Sophistication
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a semicolon joins two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction, while a colon introduces a list, explanation, or elaboration following a complete independent clause, and skillful use of both can combine short sentences into more sophisticated, varied prose.

quiz.q: A semicolon is used to join two ___.
options: Sentence fragments that could never stand alone
Unrelated independent clauses that share no logical connection
A concept unrelated to sentence punctuation
Closely related independent clauses, without a coordinating conjunction

quiz.q: A colon is typically used to introduce ___ that follows a complete independent clause.
options: A brand-new, unrelated sentence with no connection at all
A list, explanation, or elaboration
A punctuation mark unrelated to introducing further information
A single unrelated word with no connection to the preceding clause

quiz.q: Why might combining two short, related sentences with a semicolon create a more sophisticated effect than simply placing a period between them?
options: A semicolon always weakens the logical connection between two related ideas
A semicolon signals a closer logical relationship between the two ideas than two separate, disconnected sentences would suggest
Semicolons can never be used to connect two related independent clauses
Sentence-combining techniques have no effect on a piece of writing’s sophistication

quiz.q: Why must the clause preceding a colon always be a complete, independent clause on its own?
options: A colon can be correctly placed after any group of words, regardless of whether it forms a complete clause
A colon is meant to introduce further information after a grammatically complete statement, not interrupt an incomplete one
This rule has no basis in standard English punctuation conventions
A colon should never be preceded by a complete independent clause

quiz.q: Why might overusing short, simple sentences throughout an essay make a writer’s style feel less sophisticated than varying sentence length and structure?
options: Varying sentence length and structure always makes writing harder for a reader to follow
Short sentences are always considered more sophisticated than combined, complex sentences
Repetitive short sentences can create a choppy rhythm that fails to show the logical relationships between ideas the way combined sentences can
Sentence variety has no connection to how sophisticated a piece of writing feels

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Statistics: Box-and-Whisker Plots and Outlier Detection
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand (Data Management): a box-and-whisker plot displays a data set’s median, quartiles, and range in a compact visual form, and it can help identify outliers — values that fall unusually far from the rest of the data — using the interquartile range as a reference.

quiz.q: A box-and-whisker plot displays a data set’s median, quartiles, and ___.
options: Mean exclusively, with no connection to quartiles
Mode exclusively, with no connection to quartiles
A quantity unrelated to summarizing a data set
Range

quiz.q: An outlier in a data set is best described as a value that ___.
options: Falls exactly at the mean of the data set
Falls exactly at the median of the data set
Falls unusually far from the rest of the data
A concept unrelated to analyzing a data set

quiz.q: Why is the interquartile range often used as a reference for identifying outliers in a box-and-whisker plot?
options: Outliers are always identified using the full range of a data set instead of the interquartile range
It measures the spread of the middle half of the data, providing a consistent standard for how far a value must fall to be considered unusual
The interquartile range has no connection to identifying unusually high or low values
This concept has no basis in how box-and-whisker plots are constructed

quiz.q: Why might a box-and-whisker plot be a more useful visual summary than a single average value when comparing two data sets?
options: This concept has no relevance to interpreting or comparing data
A box-and-whisker plot provides no more information than a single average value
Comparing two data sets never benefits from information about spread or skew
It reveals the spread and skew of each data set, not just a single central value, allowing a more complete comparison

quiz.q: Why might an unusually long whisker on one side of a box-and-whisker plot suggest that a data set is skewed rather than symmetrical?
options: A long whisker always indicates that a data set is perfectly symmetrical
A long whisker shows that some values extend much farther from the median on one side than on the other, indicating an uneven spread
This concept has no basis in how a box-and-whisker plot is constructed
Whisker length has no connection to how a data set’s values are distributed

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Marine Ecosystems and Ocean Zonation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: marine ecosystems are organized into distinct zones based on depth and distance from shore, including the intertidal, neritic, and open ocean zones, each shaped by differing levels of sunlight, pressure, and temperature that determine which organisms can survive there.

quiz.q: Marine ecosystems are organized into distinct zones primarily based on ___.
options: Depth and distance from shore
A concept unrelated to ocean ecosystems
The exact species of fish present in a given area
The temperature of the surrounding land alone

quiz.q: The intertidal zone is best described as the area of ocean that is ___.
options: Permanently submerged at the deepest part of the ocean
A zone unrelated to marine ecosystems
Located entirely on land, far from any ocean water
Alternately exposed to air and submerged by tides

quiz.q: Why do organisms living in the intertidal zone need adaptations to survive both submersion in water and direct exposure to air?
options: Organisms in the intertidal zone are never exposed to changing conditions of any kind
This zone is alternately covered and uncovered by the tide, exposing its organisms to changing conditions throughout the day
The intertidal zone remains permanently submerged with no exposure to air
This concept has no basis in how tides affect coastal marine environments

quiz.q: Why does sunlight availability decrease sharply with increasing ocean depth, limiting where photosynthetic organisms can survive?
options: Sunlight penetrates equally to every depth of the ocean with no reduction at all
Water absorbs and scatters light, so less usable light penetrates to greater depths
Depth has no connection to how much sunlight reaches a given part of the ocean
This concept has no basis in the physical properties of water

quiz.q: Why might the open ocean zone support a different community of organisms than the shallower neritic zone closer to shore?
options: Differences in light, pressure, temperature, and nutrient availability between the zones favour organisms adapted to each specific set of conditions
This concept has no relevance to understanding marine ecosystems
Every zone of the ocean supports an identical community of organisms with no variation at all
Depth and distance from shore have no effect on which organisms can survive in a given zone

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Activity Series of Metals and Single-Displacement Reactions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: the activity series ranks metals by how readily they lose electrons and undergo oxidation, and it can be used to predict whether a single-displacement reaction will occur, since a more reactive metal will displace a less reactive metal from a compound in solution.

quiz.q: The activity series ranks metals according to how readily they ___.
options: Change colour when exposed to air
Gain protons and become negatively charged
Lose electrons and undergo oxidation
A criterion unrelated to metal reactivity

quiz.q: In a single-displacement reaction, a more reactive metal will ___ a less reactive metal from a compound in solution.
options: Always fail to react with, at all, in any way
A behaviour unrelated to single-displacement reactions
Displace
Combine permanently with, forming a stable alloy

quiz.q: Why can the activity series be used to predict whether a piece of solid zinc will react when placed into a solution containing copper ions?
options: Copper is always ranked as more reactive than zinc on the activity series
The activity series provides no useful information for predicting whether this reaction will occur
This concept has no basis in the chemistry of single-displacement reactions
Zinc is ranked as more reactive than copper on the activity series, so it will readily displace copper from the solution

quiz.q: Why would placing a piece of solid copper into a solution containing zinc ions be predicted to produce no reaction?
options: Any two metals will always react with each other’s ionic solutions, regardless of their relative reactivity
This concept has no connection to how the activity series is used
Copper is always more reactive than zinc according to the activity series
Copper is less reactive than zinc, so it cannot displace zinc from the solution according to the activity series

quiz.q: Why is the activity series a useful practical tool in fields such as metal extraction and corrosion prevention?
options: The activity series has no practical application outside of a chemistry classroom
Metal reactivity has no connection to how metals are extracted or protected from corrosion
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
It helps predict which metals will react with or protect other metals, informing decisions about extraction methods and protective coatings

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: Historical Fiction and the Ethics of Fictionalizing the Past
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: historical fiction blends invented characters and plots with real settings, events, or figures from the past, raising ongoing questions about how much creative license an author should take when representing real history within a fictional narrative.

quiz.q: Historical fiction blends invented characters and plots with ___.
options: Real settings, events, or figures from the past
Purely factual, unaltered historical documents
A concept unrelated to literary genre
Entirely imaginary settings with no connection to any real time period

quiz.q: A central ethical question raised by historical fiction concerns how much ___ an author should take when representing real history.
options: Creative license
Grammatical correctness
Punctuation, with no connection to historical accuracy
A concept unrelated to historical fiction

quiz.q: Why might an author of historical fiction research a time period extensively before beginning to write invented scenes set within it?
options: This concept has no relevance to writing historical fiction
Authors of historical fiction never need to research the time periods they write about
Grounding invented events in accurate historical detail can make the fictional narrative feel authentic and respectful of the real past it depicts
Historical research has no connection to how convincingly a historical novel represents its setting

quiz.q: Why might readers and historians debate whether it is appropriate for a historical novel to invent private thoughts or conversations for a real historical figure?
options: This kind of invention is never included in historical fiction
Doing so blurs the line between documented fact and imaginative interpretation, which can shape how readers understand that real person
This question has no relevance to evaluating historical fiction
Inventing private thoughts for a real person has no effect on how a reader understands that historical figure

quiz.q: Why might historical fiction be considered a valuable way to engage readers with a period of history, despite its blend of fact and invention?
options: A compelling narrative can make historical events feel immediate and human in a way that a purely factual account sometimes cannot
This concept has no relevance to why readers engage with historical fiction
Historical fiction always distorts a reader’s understanding of history with no possible benefit
Fiction and factual history can never be meaningfully connected in a single work

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Rational Functions — Point Discontinuities and Domain Restrictions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a rational function can have a point discontinuity, or hole, where a common factor cancels from the numerator and denominator, distinct from a vertical asymptote where the denominator alone equals zero, and both features restrict the function’s domain at that value.

quiz.q: A point discontinuity, or hole, in a rational function occurs where ___.
options: The function’s value reaches its absolute maximum
A common factor cancels from both the numerator and the denominator
A concept unrelated to rational functions
The numerator alone equals zero, with no connection to the denominator

quiz.q: A vertical asymptote in a rational function occurs where the denominator equals zero and ___.
options: A common factor always cancels it out with the numerator
A concept unrelated to rational functions
The numerator also always equals zero at that same value
No common factor cancels it out with the numerator

quiz.q: Why does a value that creates a point discontinuity still need to be excluded from a rational function’s domain, even though the graph appears continuous there after simplifying?
options: The original expression is still undefined at that value, since it would require dividing by zero before any cancellation
Point discontinuities never actually need to be excluded from a rational function’s domain
This concept has no connection to how a rational function’s domain is determined
A rational function is always defined at every value where a factor has been cancelled

quiz.q: Why is it important to factor both the numerator and denominator of a rational function before determining whether a restricted value produces a hole or a vertical asymptote?
options: Factoring a rational function never affects whether a restricted value produces a hole or a vertical asymptote
Factoring reveals whether the problematic factor cancels out entirely or remains only in the denominator, which determines which feature appears
This concept has no relevance to graphing rational functions
Every restricted value of a rational function always produces a vertical asymptote, with no exceptions

quiz.q: Why might a graphing calculator fail to visually display a point discontinuity in a rational function’s graph, even though it exists?
options: This concept has no relevance to interpreting a rational function’s graph
Graphing calculators always display every point discontinuity with complete accuracy
Point discontinuities have no connection to how a rational function is graphed
The graphing screen’s resolution often cannot represent a single missing point precisely, so the hole may not appear as a visible gap

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Human Biology: The Stress Response and the HPA Axis
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: the body’s stress response is coordinated by the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis, in which the hypothalamus signals the pituitary gland, which in turn signals the adrenal glands to release cortisol, preparing the body to respond to a perceived threat.

quiz.q: The body’s stress response is coordinated primarily by the ___ axis.
options: Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal
Skeletal-muscular-integumentary
Digestive-respiratory-circulatory
A structure unrelated to the body’s stress response

quiz.q: In the stress response, the adrenal glands are ultimately signalled to release the hormone ___.
options: Insulin, with no connection to the stress response
Melatonin, with no connection to the stress response
Cortisol
A hormone unrelated to the stress response

quiz.q: Why does the hypothalamus signal the pituitary gland rather than the adrenal glands directly at the start of the stress response?
options: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis relies on a sequential chain of hormonal signals, with the pituitary gland acting as an intermediate step
The pituitary gland has no role whatsoever in the body’s stress response
This sequence has no basis in how the stress response is physiologically coordinated
The hypothalamus always signals the adrenal glands directly, with no involvement from the pituitary gland at all

quiz.q: Why might cortisol released during the stress response temporarily raise blood glucose levels?
options: Cortisol helps mobilize energy reserves, making more glucose available to respond quickly to a perceived threat
This concept has no basis in the physiology of the stress response
Cortisol always lowers blood glucose levels during a stress response
Cortisol has no measurable effect on blood glucose levels

quiz.q: Why might chronic activation of the stress response, with prolonged elevated cortisol, be associated with negative long-term health effects?
options: Chronic activation of the stress response always has an identical effect to a single short-term stress response
Cortisol has no connection to any long-term health outcome
This concept has no relevance to understanding the HPA axis
A stress response evolved for short-term threats can disrupt normal physiological processes if it remains active over a long period

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Solubility Product Constant (Ksp) and Precipitation Predictions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: the solubility product constant, Ksp, is an equilibrium constant that describes the extent to which a sparingly soluble ionic compound dissolves in water, and comparing the calculated ion product to Ksp allows a chemist to predict whether a precipitate will form when two solutions are mixed.

quiz.q: The solubility product constant, Ksp, describes the extent to which a sparingly soluble ionic compound ___.
options: Reacts with oxygen gas exclusively
Conducts electricity in its solid state
A concept unrelated to solubility
Dissolves in water

quiz.q: To predict whether a precipitate will form when two solutions are mixed, a chemist compares the calculated ion product to ___.
options: The Ksp value for the relevant compound
The molar mass of the relevant compound
A quantity unrelated to precipitation predictions
The boiling point of the resulting mixture

quiz.q: Why does a calculated ion product greater than a compound’s Ksp value indicate that a precipitate will form?
options: Exceeding the equilibrium solubility limit means the solution is supersaturated, so excess solid will form until equilibrium is restored
The relationship between the ion product and Ksp has no connection to precipitation
This concept has no basis in solubility equilibrium chemistry
An ion product greater than Ksp always indicates that no precipitate will ever form

quiz.q: Why is a compound with a very small Ksp value considered only sparingly soluble in water?
options: The size of a Ksp value has no connection to how soluble a compound actually is
A small Ksp value always indicates that a compound is highly soluble in water
This concept has no basis in how solubility equilibrium constants are defined
A small Ksp reflects that only a very small concentration of dissolved ions can exist in equilibrium with the undissolved solid

quiz.q: Why is understanding Ksp useful in practical situations such as predicting mineral deposits or preventing unwanted precipitation in industrial processes?
options: Precipitation reactions can never be predicted or controlled using an equilibrium constant
It allows the conditions under which a particular compound will precipitate out of solution to be predicted and controlled
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
Ksp values have no practical application outside of a chemistry classroom

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Definition Essay — Arguing What a Word Really Means
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a definition essay goes beyond a dictionary entry to argue for a fuller, more nuanced understanding of a complex or abstract term, using examples, contrasts, and context to support an original interpretation of what that word truly means.

quiz.q: A definition essay goes beyond a dictionary entry to argue for ___.
options: A shorter, simpler definition than any dictionary would provide
A concept unrelated to essay writing
A fuller, more nuanced understanding of a complex or abstract term
A definition that deliberately ignores all context or examples

quiz.q: A definition essay commonly uses examples and ___ to support its interpretation of a term.
options: A technique unrelated to definition essays
A list of synonyms with no further explanation given
A single, isolated fact with no further support
Contrasts with related or opposite terms

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose an abstract term, such as courage or success, rather than a concrete term, as the subject of a definition essay?
options: Abstract terms always have a single, universally agreed-upon meaning that leaves nothing further to explore
Abstract terms often carry multiple, contested meanings that reward a deeper, more original exploration than a simple concrete term would
Concrete terms are always more suitable subjects for a definition essay than abstract ones
This choice has no connection to the purpose of a definition essay

quiz.q: Why might a definition essay contrast what a term is not with what it is?
options: This technique has no connection to how a definition essay builds its argument
Contrasting a term with what it is not always confuses a reader rather than clarifying the term
A definition essay should never reference what a term does not mean
Clarifying what falls outside a concept can sharpen a reader’s understanding of what the concept actually includes

quiz.q: Why might a definition essay be considered a genuinely argumentative form of writing, despite resembling an extended explanation?
options: A definition essay never takes any specific position on how a term should be understood
This concept has no relevance to understanding the purpose of a definition essay
It takes and defends a specific, debatable position on how a contested term should be understood, rather than simply reporting an agreed-upon fact
Argumentative writing and definition essays have no meaningful connection to one another

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Exponential Functions: The Number e and Continuous Growth
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the number e, approximately 2.718, is an important irrational constant that arises naturally when modelling continuous growth or decay, and it forms the base of the natural exponential function, which behaves differently from exponential functions with other bases in calculus-related contexts.

quiz.q: The number e is an irrational constant approximately equal to ___.
options: A value unrelated to exponential functions

quiz.q: The number e forms the base of what is known as the ___ exponential function.
options: A term unrelated to exponential functions
Discrete, exclusively, with no connection to exponential growth
Natural
Rational, exclusively, with no connection to exponential growth

quiz.q: Why does the number e arise naturally when modelling continuous growth, such as continuously compounded interest, rather than growth calculated at fixed intervals?
options: As the number of compounding intervals per year increases without bound, the growth factor approaches the value of e
This concept has no basis in how exponential growth is mathematically modelled
Continuous growth situations always eliminate any mathematical connection to the number e
The number e only ever applies to situations involving a fixed, small number of compounding intervals

quiz.q: Why is the natural exponential function, with base e, considered especially useful in fields such as calculus, compared to an exponential function with a different base?
options: The natural exponential function has mathematical properties, particularly regarding its own rate of change, that make certain calculations notably simpler
The number e has no particular mathematical significance compared to any other base
This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no real-world use
Every exponential function, regardless of its base, behaves in an identical way in calculus-related contexts

quiz.q: Why might a biologist modelling continuous population growth choose to use a natural exponential function with base e?
options: This concept has no relevance to modelling growth in a real-world context
It closely reflects how population growth can compound continuously rather than only at fixed, discrete time intervals
Population growth never occurs in a way that could be modelled using an exponential function
Natural exponential functions can never be used to model any real-world biological process

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Genetics: Mutations — Types and Effects on Protein Function
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a mutation is a change in a DNA sequence that can arise spontaneously or from exposure to a mutagen, and depending on its type — such as a silent, missense, nonsense, or frameshift mutation — it can leave a protein unaffected, alter its function, or prevent it from forming correctly.

quiz.q: A mutation is best described as a change in a ___.
options: Fully formed, folded protein exclusively
DNA sequence
A concept unrelated to genetics
Cell’s overall physical size

quiz.q: A frameshift mutation occurs when nucleotides are inserted or deleted in a way that shifts ___.
options: Only the very first nucleotide of an entire chromosome
The physical location of the gene on a completely different chromosome
A concept unrelated to genetic mutations
The reading frame used to translate the rest of the gene’s sequence

quiz.q: Why does a silent mutation typically have no effect on the protein that is produced?
options: A silent mutation always prevents a protein from being produced at all
This type of mutation has no basis in how the genetic code actually functions
The altered codon still codes for the same amino acid due to the redundancy of the genetic code
Silent mutations always change the amino acid sequence of the resulting protein significantly

quiz.q: Why might a frameshift mutation tend to have a more disruptive effect on a protein than a single missense mutation?
options: A frameshift mutation always affects only the single amino acid at the site of the mutation
This concept has no basis in how mutations affect protein translation
Shifting the reading frame changes the identity of every subsequent codon, often altering a large portion of the resulting amino acid sequence
A missense mutation always disrupts a protein more severely than a frameshift mutation

quiz.q: Why is exposure to a mutagen, such as ultraviolet radiation, associated with an increased risk of harmful mutations?
options: This concept has no basis in the biology of mutation and mutagen exposure
Exposure to a mutagen has no connection to the likelihood of a mutation occurring
Mutagens can damage or alter DNA in ways that increase the likelihood of an error being introduced into the genetic sequence
Mutagens always repair existing damage within a DNA sequence rather than causing further changes

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Organic Chemistry: Combustion Reactions and Fuel Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: combustion is an exothermic reaction between a fuel, typically a hydrocarbon, and oxygen, producing carbon dioxide and water when combustion is complete, and the amount of energy released per unit of fuel is an important factor in comparing different fuels for practical use.

quiz.q: Combustion is best described as an exothermic reaction between a fuel and ___.
options: A substance unrelated to combustion reactions
Hydrogen gas exclusively, with no connection to oxygen
Nitrogen gas exclusively
Oxygen

quiz.q: Complete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel produces carbon dioxide and ___.
options: Methane, with no connection to complete combustion
Pure carbon exclusively, with no other product formed
Water
A product unrelated to combustion reactions

quiz.q: Why is combustion classified as an exothermic reaction?
options: Combustion always absorbs energy from its surroundings rather than releasing it
It releases energy, typically as heat and light, as chemical bonds in the fuel and oxygen are rearranged into new, more stable products
This classification has no basis in the chemistry of combustion reactions
Exothermic reactions never release energy in the form of heat or light

quiz.q: Why might incomplete combustion of a hydrocarbon fuel produce carbon monoxide instead of carbon dioxide?
options: Incomplete combustion always produces the exact same products as complete combustion
Oxygen supply has no connection to which products form during a combustion reaction
A limited supply of oxygen can prevent the fuel’s carbon from being fully oxidized to carbon dioxide
This concept has no basis in the chemistry of hydrocarbon combustion

quiz.q: Why is the amount of energy released per unit of fuel an important factor when comparing different fuels for practical use, such as in vehicles?
options: Energy released per unit of fuel has no connection to how practical a fuel is for real-world use
This concept only applies to purely theoretical chemistry problems
Every fuel releases an identical amount of energy per unit of mass, regardless of its chemical composition
A fuel that releases more usable energy per unit of mass or volume can potentially provide more power or range for the same quantity of fuel

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Literary Analysis Thesis and Outline
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Writing strand: a literary analysis thesis presents a specific, arguable claim about a text, and an outline organizes supporting evidence and reasoning into a clear structure before drafting the full essay.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Writing: The Literary Analysis Thesis and Outline

quiz.q: A literary analysis thesis should present ___.
options: A list of random facts with no central claim
A concept unrelated to literary analysis
A simple summary of the text’s plot
A specific, arguable claim about a text

quiz.q: An outline for a literary analysis essay is used to ___.
options: List unrelated ideas with no connection to the thesis
A step that is never useful before writing an essay
Organize supporting evidence and reasoning before drafting the full essay
Replace the need for any evidence in the final essay

quiz.q: Which is an example of an arguable literary analysis thesis?
options: This book was published in a particular year.
Through its use of symbolism, the novel critiques the dangers of unchecked ambition.
The novel has characters and a plot.
A statement with no arguable claim about the text.

quiz.q: Why should a literary analysis thesis avoid being simply a statement of fact?
options: A thesis should never make any kind of claim
Facts are always considered strong, arguable theses
A factual statement alone provides nothing for the essay to argue or prove
This distinction has no effect on the strength of an essay

quiz.q: Why is creating an outline before drafting a literary analysis essay considered good practice?
options: Essays are always stronger when written with no planning at all
Outlines never improve the organization of an essay
It helps ensure the essay’s evidence and reasoning are logically organized in support of the thesis
An outline has no connection to how well-organized an essay is

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Financial Mathematics: Mortgages and Amortization Schedules
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand (Discrete Mathematics): a mortgage is a long-term loan repaid through regular fixed payments, and an amortization schedule shows how each payment is split between interest and principal, with the proportion going toward principal increasing over the life of the loan.

quiz.q: A mortgage is best described as a long-term loan repaid through ___.
options: Payments that never include any portion applied to interest
Regular fixed payments over an extended period
A concept unrelated to financial mathematics
A single lump-sum payment made immediately

quiz.q: An amortization schedule shows how each mortgage payment is split between ___.
options: Only interest, with no portion ever applied to principal
Interest and principal
Two entirely separate, unrelated loans
A concept unrelated to mortgage repayment

quiz.q: Why does the portion of each mortgage payment applied to principal typically increase over the life of the loan, while the portion applied to interest decreases?
options: The portion applied to principal always decreases steadily over the life of a mortgage
As the remaining principal balance shrinks, the interest charged on that smaller balance also shrinks, leaving more of each fixed payment to reduce the principal
This concept has no basis in how amortization schedules are calculated
Interest and principal portions of a mortgage payment always remain exactly equal throughout the loan

quiz.q: Why might a borrower who makes extra payments toward the principal of a mortgage reduce the total interest paid over the life of the loan?
options: Extra payments toward principal always increase the total interest paid over the life of a mortgage
Reducing the principal balance sooner lowers the amount of interest calculated on that balance in future payments
The size of a loan’s remaining principal balance has no connection to the amount of interest charged
This concept has no basis in how mortgage interest is calculated

quiz.q: Why is understanding an amortization schedule useful for someone comparing mortgage offers with different interest rates or repayment terms?
options: This concept only applies to purely abstract mathematics with no practical use
Amortization schedules provide no useful information for comparing different mortgage offers
It reveals how much of the total cost will go toward interest versus principal under each option, helping compare the true long-term cost of borrowing
Every mortgage offer results in an identical total cost, regardless of its interest rate or term

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Ecological Succession — Primary and Secondary
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: ecological succession describes the gradual, predictable change in a community of organisms over time, with primary succession beginning on bare, lifeless substrate and secondary succession beginning in an area where an existing community has been disturbed but soil remains.

quiz.q: Ecological succession describes the gradual, predictable change in a ___ over time.
options: Individual cell within an organism
Community of organisms
Single, isolated organism
A concept unrelated to ecology

quiz.q: Primary succession begins on a substrate that is ___.
options: Already covered by an established, mature community
A condition unrelated to ecological succession
Permanently underwater, with no possibility of succession occurring
Bare and lifeless, with no existing soil

quiz.q: Why does secondary succession typically proceed more quickly than primary succession after a disturbance?
options: Secondary succession begins with soil and often some surviving organisms already present, unlike primary succession, which must start from bare substrate
Secondary succession always begins with no soil present at all, just like primary succession
This concept has no basis in how ecological succession occurs
Primary and secondary succession always proceed at an identical rate

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of an area that would likely undergo primary succession?
options: A forest recovering after a wildfire that left the soil intact
An example entirely unrelated to ecological succession
A farm field left unplanted for a single growing season
Bare rock exposed after a retreating glacier

quiz.q: Why is understanding the pattern of ecological succession useful for predicting how an ecosystem might recover after a major disturbance, such as a wildfire or volcanic eruption?
options: Ecological succession provides no useful information for predicting how an ecosystem will change after a disturbance
It provides a general model for the sequence of species likely to colonize and gradually transform the disturbed area over time
This concept has no relevance to understanding ecosystem recovery
Every disturbed ecosystem recovers in a completely random, unpredictable way with no general pattern at all

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Ocean Acidification and Carbon Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: ocean acidification occurs when the ocean absorbs excess atmospheric carbon dioxide, which reacts with seawater to form carbonic acid and lower the water’s pH, reducing the availability of carbonate ions that many marine organisms need to build their shells and skeletons.

quiz.q: Ocean acidification occurs when the ocean absorbs excess atmospheric ___.
options: A substance unrelated to ocean chemistry
Oxygen gas exclusively, with no connection to acidification
Nitrogen gas exclusively
Carbon dioxide

quiz.q: Dissolved carbon dioxide reacts with seawater to form ___, which lowers the water’s pH.
options: A substance unrelated to ocean acidification
Carbonic acid
A stable, unreactive compound with no effect on pH
Pure oxygen gas, with no connection to pH

quiz.q: Why does an increase in dissolved carbon dioxide lower the pH of seawater?
options: Dissolved carbon dioxide always raises the pH of seawater instead of lowering it
This concept has no basis in the chemistry of ocean acidification
The carbonic acid formed increases the concentration of hydrogen ions in the water, making it more acidic
Carbon dioxide has no connection to the chemical reactions occurring in seawater

quiz.q: Why does ocean acidification reduce the availability of carbonate ions that marine organisms need to build shells and skeletons?
options: This concept has no basis in the chemistry of shell-building marine organisms
Ocean acidification always increases the availability of carbonate ions for marine organisms
Carbonate ion availability has no connection to the pH of seawater
The increased concentration of hydrogen ions reacts with carbonate ions, converting them into a form less available for shell-building organisms to use

quiz.q: Why is ocean acidification considered closely linked to the same rising atmospheric carbon dioxide levels associated with climate change?
options: Much of the excess carbon dioxide released by human activity is absorbed by the ocean, directly connecting atmospheric emissions to changing ocean chemistry
This concept has no relevance to understanding global environmental chemistry
Ocean acidification has no connection to atmospheric carbon dioxide levels of any kind
The ocean never absorbs any atmospheric gases under any circumstances

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Review: Absurdism, Monologue, Media Rhetoric, and Framing Devices
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: this lesson revisits absurdist fiction and the Theatre of the Absurd, the dramatic monologue, data visualization and statistical rhetoric, literary journalism, the anecdote in oral storytelling, semicolons and colons, historical fiction, the definition essay, and paratext and the epigraph.

quiz.q: Absurdist literature typically portrays a universe that ___.
options: Follows a strictly logical and orderly plot at every turn
Resists rational explanation or meaning
Always resolves every conflict with a clear, satisfying moral
A concept unrelated to literary movements

quiz.q: A dramatic monologue is a poem spoken entirely in the voice of ___.
options: A single fictional or historical speaker addressing a silent listener
Multiple speakers taking turns throughout the poem
A narrator who never expresses any specific point of view
A concept unrelated to poetic form

quiz.q: A data visualization used in a news report can be technically accurate yet still ___.

Impossible to construct using real data
Visually misleading, based on choices such as a truncated axis or scale
Guaranteed to represent every possible interpretation fairly

quiz.q: An epigraph is best described as a brief quotation placed ___.
options: In the exact middle of a work, unconnected to its beginning or end
At the very end of a work, after the story has fully concluded
A concept unrelated to paratext
At the start of a work, to frame a reader’s expectations

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review these varied literary forms, media literacy skills, and writing techniques together?
options: Review is never useful for English language skills
Each skill must be studied with no connection to the others
They reinforce complementary approaches to interpreting and producing texts effectively
These skills have no connection to each other

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Review: Conics, Discrete Math, Trigonometric Modelling, and Financial Math
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand review: this lesson revisits ellipses and hyperbolas, matrices, the pigeonhole principle, direct and indirect proof, sinusoidal modelling of periodic phenomena, box-and-whisker plots, point discontinuities in rational functions, the number e, and mortgages and amortization.

quiz.q: An ellipse is defined as the set of all points for which the ___ of the distances to two fixed foci is constant.

Sum
Product

Every container must hold exactly one item

At least one container must hold more than one item

quiz.q: A sinusoidal function is well suited to modelling a real-world phenomenon that ___.

Changes in a completely random, unpredictable way

quiz.q: The number e is an irrational constant approximately equal to ___.

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review discrete mathematics, trigonometric modelling, and financial applications of functions together?
options: It reinforces how these mathematical tools and reasoning skills connect and build on one another
Each topic must be learned in complete isolation
Review is never useful in math
These topics have no connection to each other

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Review: Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Ecology, and Human Physiology
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: this lesson revisits enzyme structure and inhibition, DNA replication, transcription, and translation, taxonomy and the three-domain system, keystone species and trophic cascades, blood glucose regulation, marine ecosystems, the stress response, mutations, and ecological succession.

quiz.q: An enzyme is best described as a protein that functions as a ___.

Source of long-term energy storage exclusively
Structural fibre with no chemical role at all

quiz.q: A keystone species is best described as a species that has ___.
