quiz.q: Ecological succession describes the gradual, predictable change in a ___ over time.
options: Individual cell within an organism
A concept unrelated to ecology
Single, isolated organism
Community of organisms

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review biochemistry, molecular biology, and ecological concepts together?
options: It reinforces how these interconnected biological concepts relate to one another
Review is never useful in biology
Each topic must be studied with no connection to the others
These topics have no connection to each other

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Review: Hydrates, Gas Laws, Nuclear Chemistry, and Environmental Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand review: this lesson revisits hydrates and water of crystallization, the ideal gas law, aromatic compounds, nuclear fission and fusion, weak acid and base equilibria, the activity series of metals, solubility product constants, combustion reactions, and ocean acidification.

Temperature
Colour

quiz.q: Ocean acidification occurs when the ocean absorbs excess atmospheric ___.
options: Carbon dioxide
Oxygen gas exclusively, with no connection to acidification
Nitrogen gas exclusively
A substance unrelated to ocean chemistry

quiz.q: Why is it useful to review hydrate chemistry, gas laws, nuclear chemistry, and environmental chemistry together?
options: These topics have no connection to each other
Review is never useful in chemistry
Each topic must be studied with no connection to the others
It reinforces how these interconnected chemistry concepts relate to one another

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing Epistolary Narratives
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Language strand: an epistolary narrative tells a story through letters, diary entries, or other documents, giving readers a direct, personal window into a character’s voice and perspective.

quiz.q: What do we call a narrative told through letters or diary entries?
options: A recipe
A concept unrelated to reading

options: This format only ever uses a third-person narrator
Yes
No, this format never reveals a character’s voice

options: Epistolary narratives never create any sense of intimacy
This format always distances readers from the characters

options: This concept has no connection to reading comprehension
Only one single perspective is ever possible in this format

subjects.subject: Functions

subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: logarithmic scales, such as pH, the Richter scale, and the decibel scale, compress a huge range of values into a more manageable set of numbers.

options: Expand small numbers into much larger ones with no practical use
Compress a huge range of values into a more manageable set of numbers
Convert numbers into fractions only

options: A concept unrelated to logarithmic scales
Yes
The Richter scale only measures ocean tides

options: Yes
No, the intensity remains exactly the same

subjects.subject: Biology

subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: photoperiodism describes how plants respond to the relative length of day and night, often triggering processes like flowering at specific times of year.

How plants respond to the relative length of day and night

How plants convert sugar into starch

Flowering only depends on soil temperature, never light exposure

options: This concept has no connection to biology
Continuous light would prevent the plant from experiencing the shorter day length needed to trigger flowering
Artificial light never has any effect on a plant’s flowering response
All plants flower at the exact same time regardless of light conditions

quiz.q: Why is understanding photoperiodism useful for farmers growing crops on a commercial schedule?
options: Farmers never need to consider day length when growing crops
This concept has no relevance to biology
It can help them control lighting conditions to influence when crops flower and produce yield

quiz.q: Why might plants native to different latitudes have evolved different photoperiodic responses?

subjects.subject: Chemistry

A concept unrelated to buffer chemistry
The Henderson-Hasselbalch equation

Yes

quiz.q: Why are buffer solutions important in biological systems, such as human blood?
options: They help maintain a stable pH despite small chemical changes, which is essential for proper cell function
Buffer solutions have no role in maintaining stable conditions in biological systems
This concept has no relevance to chemistry

subjects.subject: English

subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a eulogy or occasional speech is written to mark a significant event, often balancing personal reflection, respect for the audience, and a clear central message.

options: A routine weekly meeting
A concept unrelated to writing
A scientific experiment result

options: Yes
A concept unrelated to occasional speeches
Personal reflection has no place in this type of speech

A clear focus helps unify personal stories and reflections into a coherent, memorable speech

subjects.subject: Functions

By multiplying the term’s position by two

By adding the two preceding terms

quiz.q: What are the first two terms of the Fibonacci sequence?

0 and 1
2 and 3

subjects.subject: Chemistry

subjects.subject: English

subjects.subject: Chemistry

subjects.subject: English

subjects.subject: Biology

subjects.subject: English

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Evolution: Adaptive Radiation and Niche Diversification
subjects.summary: Students explore how a single ancestral species can rapidly diversify into many descendant species that fill different ecological niches, using classic examples such as Darwin's finches and Anolis lizards.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Evolution: Adaptive Radiation and Niche Diversification

quiz.q: Adaptive radiation is best defined as:
options: The rapid diversification of one ancestral lineage into many species occupying different niches
A sudden mass extinction event
The gradual convergence of unrelated species toward one body form
The migration of a species to a new continent

quiz.q: Darwin's finches on the Galápagos Islands are a classic example of adaptive radiation because they show:
options: A single species that never diverged
Identical beak shapes across all islands
Beak shapes that vary with each species' food source
No genetic differences among islands

quiz.q: Which condition most favours adaptive radiation after a species colonizes a new island?
options: Intense competition from many established species
A completely uniform habitat
Few competitors and many unused ecological niches
Total isolation from all resources

quiz.q: Adaptive radiation typically results in species that are:
options: Unrelated species sharing one niche
Genetically identical but behaviourally different
Distantly related but structurally identical
Closely related but structurally and ecologically distinct

quiz.q: Which of the following would NOT typically drive adaptive radiation?
options: Complete absence of genetic variation in the population
Lack of predators in a new habitat
Geographic isolation on separate islands
Availability of unexploited resources

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Perfumes and Fragrances
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: perfumes are complex mixtures of volatile organic compounds, including esters and essential oils, carefully blended and diluted in a solvent to create layered scents that evaporate at different rates.

quiz.q: What are perfumes chemically composed of?
options: A single pure element with no other compounds
Complex mixtures of volatile organic compounds
Only water with no other chemicals
Only inorganic salts

quiz.q: Which class of organic compounds is commonly used to create pleasant scents in perfumes?
options: Esters
Only noble gases
Only strong bases
Only strong acids

quiz.q: Why do different scent notes in a perfume evaporate at different rates?
options: All compounds in a perfume evaporate at the exact same rate
Different compounds have different volatilities
Perfumes contain no volatile compounds at all
Evaporation rate has no connection to scent

quiz.q: What is typically used to dilute the concentrated fragrance compounds in perfume?
options: Liquid nitrogen
A solvent, such as alcohol
Concentrated acid with no dilution
Pure solid metal

quiz.q: The layered structure of a perfumes scent, changing over time as it is worn, is due to ___.
options: All ingredients evaporating instantly and simultaneously
The perfume having no chemical structure at all
Compounds with different evaporation rates being released at different times
A single unchanging compound with no variation

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: The TED-Style Talk
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a TED-style talk delivers a single, focused idea to a general audience using clear structure, storytelling, and engaging delivery, typically within a concise, well-rehearsed time limit.

quiz.q: What is a defining feature of a TED-style talk?
options: Reading directly from a dense, technical script with no engagement
Covering as many unrelated topics as possible
Delivering a single, focused idea clearly to a general audience
Avoiding any structure or preparation

quiz.q: Why do TED-style talks often use storytelling?
options: To make complex ideas more relatable and engaging for the audience
To avoid connecting with the audience emotionally
To confuse the audience about the main idea
Storytelling is never used in this format

quiz.q: What is typically true about the length of a TED-style talk?
options: Length is never a consideration in this format
It is always exactly one minute long
It is concise and well-rehearsed, often under a set time limit
It has no time limit and can last for many hours

quiz.q: Why is clear structure important in a TED-style talk?
options: Clear structure only matters in written essays, not speeches
It helps the audience follow and remember the central idea
Structure is unnecessary since audiences never need guidance
A talk with structure is always less effective

quiz.q: What is a common goal of a TED-style talk?
options: To inspire, inform, or persuade an audience about a single idea
To provide no clear takeaway for the audience
To avoid any audience engagement whatsoever
To read a list of unrelated facts with no theme

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Matrices: An Introduction
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: a matrix is a rectangular arrangement of numbers organized into rows and columns, used to represent and solve certain types of mathematical problems.

quiz.q: What is a matrix?
options: A type of geometric shape only
A rectangular arrangement of numbers in rows and columns
A concept unrelated to math
A single number with no structure

quiz.q: What are the two directions a matrix is organized by?
options: A concept unrelated to matrices
Only rows, with no columns
Only diagonals
Rows and columns

quiz.q: In a matrix with 2 rows and 3 columns, how many total numbers does it contain?
Why might a matrix be useful for organizing data, like scores from multiple games and players?
options: This concept has no connection to math
It provides a clear, organized way to display data across two categories at once
Matrices never help organize any kind of data
Rows and columns never actually represent meaningful data

quiz.q: What is the size of a matrix with 3 rows and 2 columns often written as?
options: A concept unrelated to matrices
3 by 2
2 by 3
5 by 5

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Bioremediation — Using Organisms to Clean Pollution
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: bioremediation uses living organisms, such as bacteria and fungi, to break down or remove pollutants from contaminated soil, water, or air, offering an environmentally friendly cleanup strategy.

quiz.q: What is bioremediation?
options: A method of building new factories
A type of chemical warfare technology
Using living organisms to break down or remove pollutants
A process that always increases pollution levels

quiz.q: Which organisms are commonly used in bioremediation?
options: Only reptiles
Bacteria and fungi
Only large mammals
Only birds

quiz.q: What can bioremediation help clean up?
options: Only clean, unpolluted environments
Contaminated soil, water, or air
Only man-made structures with no pollutants
Only outer space debris

quiz.q: Why is bioremediation often considered an environmentally friendly cleanup method?
options: It uses natural biological processes rather than harsh chemical treatments
It destroys the environment further
It has no connection to environmental cleanup at all
It always requires more toxic chemicals than traditional methods

quiz.q: Which pollutant might certain bacteria be used to break down through bioremediation?
options: Sunlight
Pure oxygen gas
Fresh drinking water
Oil from an oil spill

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Tears — Lachrymatory Agents
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: lachrymatory agents, such as the compound released when cutting an onion, are volatile chemicals that irritate the eyes and trigger tear production through a reaction with enzymes in plant cells.

quiz.q: What is a lachrymatory agent?
options: A compound that has no effect on the eyes
A volatile chemical that irritates the eyes and triggers tears
A solid mineral with no chemical reactivity
A gas used only in refrigeration

quiz.q: What triggers the release of a lachrymatory compound when cutting an onion?
options: Damage to the onions cells releases enzymes that react to form the irritant
The onion releases the compound only when fully intact and uncut
The compound is released only after the onion is cooked
Heat alone causes the reaction with no cutting required

quiz.q: Why do lachrymatory compounds cause eyes to water?
options: They only affect the sense of taste, not the eyes
They have no chemical interaction with the eyes at all
They cause a permanent change in eye colour
They irritate sensitive tissue in the eyes, triggering a tear reflex

quiz.q: What might reduce the tear-inducing effect when cutting an onion?
options: Adding more of the irritant compound directly
Chilling the onion beforehand to slow the chemical reaction
Avoiding cutting the onion cells at all is impossible when slicing
Cutting the onion at a much higher temperature to speed up the reaction

quiz.q: Studying lachrymatory agents connects chemistry to which everyday experience?
options: Only industrial manufacturing, with no connection to daily life
Common kitchen chemistry, like preparing food
Only nuclear physics
Only astronomy

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing Foil Characters
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a foil character has traits that contrast sharply with a main character, and this contrast helps highlight and clarify the main characters own qualities, choices, and moral position.

quiz.q: What is a foil character?
options: A character whose traits contrast with a main character to highlight them
A character identical to the main character
A type of narrator
A character who never appears in the story

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a foil character?
options: To replace the main character entirely
To highlight and clarify the main characters qualities through contrast
To confuse the reader about the plot
To remove all conflict from the story

quiz.q: If a protagonist is idealistic, a foil character might be ___.
options: Nonexistent in the story
A narrator only
Pragmatic and cynical
Also idealistic in the exact same way

quiz.q: Foil characters are most useful for revealing ___.
options: Only the setting of a story
Nothing about the characters
Personality traits and moral positions through comparison
Only the time period of a story

quiz.q: Which is an example of a foil relationship?
options: A morally rigid character paired with a morally flexible character
A character and a map
A character and the weather
Two identical characters with no differences

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to Normal Distribution
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: a normal distribution is a symmetric, bell-shaped pattern of data where most values cluster near the mean, with fewer values appearing farther from the average.

quiz.q: What shape does a normal distribution typically form?
options: A completely flat line
A concept unrelated to statistics
A symmetric, bell shape
A perfectly straight diagonal line

quiz.q: In a normal distribution, do most values cluster near the mean or far from it?
options: A concept unrelated to normal distribution
Values never cluster anywhere in particular
Far from the mean
Near the mean

quiz.q: Why might test scores from a large group of students often form a roughly normal distribution?
options: Test scores never form any kind of predictable pattern
Most students tend to perform near an average level, with fewer scoring extremely high or low
This concept has no connection to statistics
A normal distribution never applies to real-world data like test scores

quiz.q: In a bell-shaped normal distribution, where is the peak of the curve typically located?
options: At the mean
A concept unrelated to normal distribution
At the very lowest value
At the very highest value only

quiz.q: Why is understanding normal distribution useful for interpreting large data sets?
options: It helps identify what values are typical versus unusually high or low
This concept has no relevance to statistics
Normal distribution never helps with interpreting any data
All data sets always form the exact same shape regardless of pattern

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Hydrothermal Vent Ecosystems and Chemosynthesis
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: hydrothermal vent ecosystems exist on the deep ocean floor, where specialized bacteria use chemosynthesis to convert chemicals like hydrogen sulfide into energy, supporting entire food webs without sunlight.

quiz.q: Where are hydrothermal vent ecosystems typically found?
options: In desert regions with no water
In shallow freshwater lakes
On mountain peaks
On the deep ocean floor

quiz.q: What process do bacteria at hydrothermal vents use to produce energy?
options: Cellular respiration using oxygen from the surface only
Photosynthesis, using direct sunlight
A process requiring constant sunlight exposure
Chemosynthesis

quiz.q: What chemical is commonly used by chemosynthetic bacteria at hydrothermal vents?
options: Table salt
Hydrogen sulfide
Pure oxygen gas only
Liquid nitrogen

quiz.q: How can hydrothermal vent ecosystems support life without sunlight?
options: Life cannot exist in these ecosystems at all
Sunlight has no connection to any ecosystems energy source
Chemosynthetic bacteria form the base of the food web, replacing the role of sunlight-driven photosynthesis
These ecosystems actually require significant sunlight to function

quiz.q: Why are hydrothermal vent ecosystems significant to scientists studying the origins of life?
options: They demonstrate that life can thrive in extreme conditions without sunlight
They were discovered before any other ecosystem on Earth
They prove that sunlight is required for all forms of life everywhere
They have no scientific significance at all

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Photography — Silver Halides
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: traditional photographic film relies on the light sensitivity of silver halide compounds, which undergo a chemical reaction when exposed to light, forming the basis of the image before further chemical development.

quiz.q: What compounds are traditional photographic film coated with to capture images?
options: Pure carbon
Liquid mercury
Table salt only
Silver halides

quiz.q: What happens to silver halide compounds when exposed to light?
options: They instantly evaporate with no chemical change
They turn into a gas with no further reaction
They remain completely unaffected by light exposure
They undergo a chemical reaction that begins forming the image

quiz.q: Why are silver halides useful for photography?
options: They are highly sensitive to light, allowing them to capture an image
They react only to sound waves, not light
They cannot be chemically developed after exposure
They are completely insensitive to light of any kind

quiz.q: What additional step is needed after light exposure to fully reveal a photographic image?
options: Freezing the film at extremely low temperatures
No further steps are needed after light exposure
Chemical development in a darkroom process
Exposing the film to additional direct sunlight only

quiz.q: The chemistry of photography connects to which broader concept in chemistry?
options: Only organic chemistry, with no connection to light
Only nuclear chemistry, with no connection to light
Only thermochemistry, with no connection to light
Photochemistry, the study of light-induced chemical reactions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: Poetry, Rhetoric, and Literary Devices
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: students revisit juxtaposition, the prose poem, letters of recommendation, the dash, ekphrastic poetry, native advertising, extended metaphor and conceit, TED-style talks, and foil characters.

quiz.q: What is juxtaposition?
options: Combining two similar ideas into one
A grammar rule for verb tense
A type of punctuation mark
Placing two contrasting elements side by side

quiz.q: How is a prose poem structured?
options: In continuous prose paragraphs rather than verse lines
Only as a list of single words
Only as a series of questions
Only in strict rhyming couplets

quiz.q: What is ekphrastic poetry?
options: Poetry that vividly describes or responds to a work of visual art
Poetry written only about nature
Poetry with no descriptive language at all
A type of poem with a strict rhyme scheme only

quiz.q: What distinguishes a conceit from a typical extended metaphor?
options: A conceit is always exactly one word long
A conceit is especially elaborate or surprising, connecting very different ideas
A conceit never involves any comparison at all
A conceit is identical to a simple simile

quiz.q: What is a foil character?
options: A character whose traits contrast with a main character to highlight them
A character who never appears in the story
A character identical to the main character
A type of narrator

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Algebra: Completing the Square
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: completing the square is a method for rewriting a quadratic expression into a perfect square trinomial plus a constant, useful for solving quadratic equations.

quiz.q: What does completing the square help rewrite a quadratic expression into?
options: A simple linear expression
A completely different type of equation
A perfect square trinomial plus a constant
A concept unrelated to algebra

quiz.q: Is completing the square a method useful for solving quadratic equations?
options: Yes
A concept unrelated to algebra
No, it has no connection to quadratic equations
It only works for linear equations

quiz.q: In the expression x squared plus 6x, what number would you add to complete the square?
Why might completing the square be useful for finding the vertex of a parabola?
options: Rewriting the equation in vertex form directly reveals the coordinates of the vertex
This concept has no connection to algebra
Parabolas never actually have a vertex to find
Completing the square never helps identify a parabola’s vertex

quiz.q: In the expression x squared plus 10x, what number would you add to complete the square?

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology Review: Adaptations, Cell Biology, and Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: students revisit desert ecosystems, bioluminescence, camouflage and mimicry, the placenta, telomeres, apoptosis, the gut-brain axis, bioremediation, and hydrothermal vent ecosystems.

quiz.q: What defines a desert ecosystem?
options: No sunlight at all
Constant freezing temperatures only
Very little precipitation
Extremely high precipitation

quiz.q: What is bioluminescence?
options: The production of light by living organisms through a chemical reaction
A type of camouflage using colour change alone
The absorption of light by an organism with no light produced
A process only found in plants

quiz.q: What is apoptosis?
options: A process where cells grow uncontrollably forever
An uncontrolled process where cells burst open randomly
A type of cell division unrelated to cell death
A regulated, programmed process by which cells self-destruct

quiz.q: What is bioremediation?
options: Using living organisms to break down or remove pollutants
A method of building new factories
A process that always increases pollution levels
A type of chemical warfare technology

quiz.q: What process do bacteria at hydrothermal vents use to produce energy?
options: A process requiring constant sunlight exposure
Photosynthesis, using direct sunlight
Cellular respiration using oxygen from the surface only
Chemosynthesis

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Biotechnology: CRISPR and Gene Editing
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Science Life Systems strand: CRISPR is a gene-editing technology that allows scientists to make precise changes to DNA, with significant potential applications and ethical considerations in medicine and agriculture.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Biotechnology: CRISPR and Gene Editing

quiz.q: CRISPR is a technology used to ___.
options: Predict weather patterns
Measure the size of a cell
Study the movement of tectonic plates
Make precise changes to DNA

quiz.q: CRISPR has potential applications in fields such as ___.
options: Fields with no connection to biology
Medicine and agriculture
A single, unrelated area of study
Only entertainment technology

quiz.q: Why does gene editing technology like CRISPR raise ethical considerations?
options: It has the potential to significantly alter living organisms, raising questions about appropriate use
Gene editing has no ethical implications at all
CRISPR has no connection to living organisms
Ethical considerations are irrelevant to scientific research

quiz.q: Which is a potential application of CRISPR in agriculture?
options: An application with no connection to agriculture
A use unrelated to farming or crops
A technology that cannot be applied to plants
Developing crops with improved resistance to disease

quiz.q: Why is CRISPR considered a significant advancement in biotechnology?
options: It has no advantages over earlier gene-editing methods
It allows for much more precise and efficient gene editing than earlier methods
CRISPR cannot be used to edit genes at all
Gene editing technology has no scientific significance

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing Motif and Recurring Symbols in Fiction
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a motif is a recurring image, phrase, or idea that repeats throughout a text, reinforcing central themes and creating structural and thematic unity across a narrative.

quiz.q: What is a motif?
options: A recurring image, phrase, or idea repeated throughout a text
A single event that happens only once in a story
A type of punctuation mark
A formal citation style

quiz.q: What does a motif typically reinforce in a text?
options: The page numbering of a book
Central themes and structural unity
Random unrelated details
Grammar rules only

quiz.q: How does a motif differ from a one-time symbol?
options: A motif has no connection to meaning
A motif repeats across the text, while a single symbol may appear only once
A motif appears only in poetry, never in prose
A motif is always a literal object with no symbolic value

quiz.q: Which is an example of a motif in a novel?
options: The page count of the novel
Repeated references to birds or flight throughout the story
A single mention of rain in one chapter
The title page of the book

quiz.q: Why might a reader track a recurring motif while reading?
options: Motifs have no effect on interpretation
To identify grammatical errors only
To count how many words are in the chapter
To notice how the pattern deepens or shifts the meaning of the text over time

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus Preview: An Introduction to the Derivative as a Limit
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the derivative of a function at a point is defined as the limit of the average rate of change as the interval shrinks toward zero, giving the instantaneous rate of change and the slope of the tangent line.

quiz.q: How is the derivative of a function at a point defined?
options: As the sum of all function values
As a fixed number unrelated to the function
As the total area under the curve
As the limit of the average rate of change as the interval shrinks toward zero

quiz.q: What does the derivative represent geometrically?
options: The area enclosed by the curve
The slope of the tangent line at a point
The length of the curve
The y-intercept of the function

quiz.q: What earlier concept is the formal definition of the derivative built upon?
options: The limit
Basic addition
Simple counting
The Pythagorean Theorem

quiz.q: What does the derivative measure at a specific point?
options: The instantaneous rate of change of the function
The number of times a graph crosses the x-axis
The average value of the function over its entire domain
The total distance travelled by a graph

quiz.q: Why is a function generally required to be continuous at a point before a derivative can exist there?
options: Derivatives only exist for straight lines
Discontinuous functions always have derivatives everywhere
A break or jump at a point prevents a well-defined tangent line from being formed
Continuity has no relationship to derivatives at all

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Cell Biology: The Cytoskeleton -- Shape, Support, and Movement
subjects.summary: Students examine the three main cytoskeletal fibre types -- microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules -- and their roles in maintaining cell shape, enabling movement, and organizing organelle transport.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Cell Biology: The Cytoskeleton -- Shape, Support, and Movement

quiz.q: Which cytoskeletal component is the thickest and forms the tracks for organelle transport by motor proteins?
options: Intermediate filaments
Cell wall
Microfilaments
Microtubules

quiz.q: Microfilaments are composed mainly of which protein?
options: Tubulin
Collagen
Keratin
Actin

quiz.q: Which cytoskeletal fibres provide the greatest mechanical strength and help anchor the nucleus in place?
options: Flagella
Intermediate filaments
Microtubules
Microfilaments

quiz.q: During cell division, which cytoskeletal structure forms the spindle fibres that separate chromosomes?
options: Microfilaments
Intermediate filaments
Microtubules
Peroxisomes

quiz.q: Which of the following is a function of the cytoskeleton?
options: Synthesizing lipids
Maintaining cell shape and enabling intracellular movement
Producing ATP through respiration
Storing genetic information

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Cellular Respiration in Depth
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Biology strand: cellular respiration breaks down glucose in the presence of oxygen to release usable energy for cells, producing carbon dioxide and water as byproducts.

quiz.q: Cellular respiration breaks down ___ to release usable energy.
options: Water only
Glucose
Oxygen only
Carbon dioxide only

quiz.q: Cellular respiration typically requires ___.
options: Oxygen
No input substances at all
Only carbon dioxide, with no oxygen involved
Only sunlight, with no oxygen involved

quiz.q: Which are byproducts of cellular respiration?
options: Only sunlight, with no other byproducts
Oxygen and glucose
Carbon dioxide and water
Nitrogen and hydrogen

quiz.q: Why is cellular respiration essential for most living cells?
options: This process has no connection to cellular energy production
Cells never require energy to function
Cellular respiration has no role in providing energy
It provides the usable energy cells need to carry out their functions

quiz.q: How is cellular respiration related to photosynthesis?
options: Photosynthesis produces glucose and oxygen, which cellular respiration then uses
Only plants perform cellular respiration
Cellular respiration produces the glucose used in photosynthesis
The two processes have no connection to each other

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: The Ballad — Narrative Poetry and Oral Tradition
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a ballad is a narrative poem, often set to music, that tells a story through simple language, repetition, and a regular rhythm, rooted in an oral tradition of passing stories between generations.

quiz.q: What does a ballad primarily do?
options: Avoids any use of rhythm or repetition
Functions only as a formal legal document
Tells a story through verse, often set to music
Presents a list of unrelated facts

quiz.q: What tradition is the ballad form rooted in?
options: Legal contract writing
Modern digital publishing only
Oral storytelling passed between generations
Formal academic essay writing

quiz.q: Which literary technique is commonly used in ballads to aid memorization and musicality?
options: Random line lengths with no pattern
Repetition and regular rhythm
Complete absence of rhyme or rhythm
Only footnotes and citations

quiz.q: What kind of language does a ballad typically use?
options: Highly technical, scientific vocabulary only
Simple, direct language accessible to a wide audience
Language understood only by scholars
No language at all, only music

quiz.q: Why might a ballad be considered a bridge between poetry and music?
options: Ballads have no connection to music whatsoever
Music was invented after the ballad form disappeared
Ballads are always performed silently with no sound
Ballads were traditionally sung and passed down orally before being written

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to Vectors
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: a vector is a quantity that has both magnitude, or size, and direction, such as a force applied at a specific angle, often represented visually as an arrow.

quiz.q: What two things does a vector have?
options: Only a single number with no direction
Magnitude and direction
Only a colour
A concept unrelated to math

quiz.q: How is a vector often represented visually?
options: As an arrow
As a random squiggle with no meaning
A concept unrelated to vectors
As a single dot only

quiz.q: Does the length of a vector’s arrow typically represent its magnitude?
options: A concept unrelated to vectors
The colour of the arrow always shows magnitude instead
Yes
No, length has no connection to magnitude

quiz.q: Why might a vector be a more useful way to describe a force than just a single number?
options: A vector captures both how strong the force is and which direction it is applied
This concept has no connection to vectors
Vectors never actually describe any real-world quantity
A single number always fully describes a force with no need for direction

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a vector quantity, since it includes both size and direction?
options: The temperature of a room
The price of an item at a store
Wind blowing at 20 kilometres per hour toward the north
The number of students in a class

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Endocrine Disruptors and Hormonal Health
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: endocrine disruptors are chemical compounds that interfere with the normal function of the hormonal system by mimicking, blocking, or altering natural hormone signalling, with potential effects on growth, reproduction, and development.

quiz.q: What is an endocrine disruptor?
options: A type of vitamin required for healthy bones
A protein that has no interaction with the endocrine system
A chemical compound that interferes with normal hormone signalling
A hormone naturally produced by the pancreas

quiz.q: How might an endocrine disruptor affect the body?
options: By permanently increasing bone density only
By replacing all cells in the body instantly
By having no measurable biological effect
By mimicking, blocking, or altering natural hormone signals

quiz.q: Which body system do endocrine disruptors primarily target?
options: The digestive system exclusively
The hormonal (endocrine) system
The integumentary system only
The skeletal system only

quiz.q: What kinds of biological processes might be affected by exposure to endocrine disruptors?
options: Growth, reproduction, and development
Only the sense of taste
Only hair texture
Only eye colour

quiz.q: Why are scientists concerned about environmental sources of endocrine disruptors?
options: They only exist in a laboratory setting with no real-world presence
They immediately and completely dissolve with no lasting effect
Because they may accumulate in the environment and affect wildlife and human hormonal health over time
Endocrine disruptors have no environmental sources at all

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Vulcanization — Cross-Linking in Rubber Polymers
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: vulcanization is a chemical process in which sulfur atoms form cross-links between polymer chains in rubber, converting a soft, sticky material into a stronger, more elastic, and heat-resistant product.

quiz.q: What is vulcanization?
options: A chemical process that forms cross-links between polymer chains in rubber using sulfur
A physical process with no chemical reaction involved
A process that removes all polymer chains from rubber
A method of melting rubber into a liquid permanently

quiz.q: What element is commonly used to cross-link rubber polymer chains during vulcanization?
options: Chlorine
Helium
Sulfur
Oxygen

quiz.q: How does vulcanized rubber differ from untreated natural rubber?
options: It is softer and much stickier than untreated rubber
It is stronger, more elastic, and more heat-resistant
It loses all elasticity and becomes brittle
It becomes a liquid at room temperature

quiz.q: What structural change occurs to the polymer chains during vulcanization?
options: The polymer chains disappear entirely
The chains rearrange into a crystal lattice with no bonds
All polymer chains are broken into individual monomers
Cross-links form between separate polymer chains

quiz.q: Why is vulcanized rubber used in products like tires?
options: It cannot withstand any temperature change
It is far more fragile than untreated rubber
It has no practical advantage over untreated rubber
Its added strength and heat resistance make it more durable under stress

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Process Essay — Explaining How Something Works
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a process essay explains how to complete a task or how something works through a clear sequence of steps, relying on precise chronological order and transitional language to guide the reader.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a process essay?
options: To argue a single controversial opinion
To explain how to complete a task or how something works
To summarize a work of fiction
To describe a personal memory with no instructional purpose

quiz.q: What structural feature is essential to a process essay?
options: A rhyme scheme
A completely random order of ideas
No structure of any kind
A clear, chronological sequence of steps

quiz.q: What kind of language helps guide a reader through a process essay?
options: Language with no connection between steps
Only technical jargon with no explanation
Transitional language, such as first, next, and finally
Poetic imagery with no clear steps

quiz.q: Which of these topics would suit a process essay?
options: A personal reflection on a childhood memory
How to brew a cup of tea

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Measuring Biodiversity -- Richness and Diversity Indices
subjects.summary: Students distinguish species richness from species evenness as components of biodiversity, and see how ecologists use simple diversity indices to compare the variety and balance of species across different ecosystems.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Ecology: Measuring Biodiversity -- Richness and Diversity Indices

quiz.q: Species richness refers to:
options: The total number of different species in a community
The number of trophic levels present
The total biomass of an ecosystem
The relative abundance of each species

quiz.q: Two forests each have 5 tree species. Forest X has these species in nearly equal numbers, while Forest Y is 95% dominated by one species. Forest X has higher:
options: Species richness
Total biomass
Carrying capacity
Species evenness

quiz.q: A community with high species richness but very low evenness would most likely be:
options: Impossible to measure
Automatically classified as a monoculture
Considered equally diverse as a community with high richness and high evenness
Dominated by one or a few species even though many species are technically present

quiz.q: Which of the following would most directly increase the measured biodiversity of a wetland?
options: Adding several new native species without eliminating existing ones
Removing the top predator entirely
A drought that kills all amphibians
A new invasive species outcompeting and eliminating native species

quiz.q: Ecologists use diversity indices primarily to:
options: Measure the pH of soil
Calculate the exact age of an ecosystem
Predict earthquake activity
Compare the variety and balance of species between different communities

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Effervescence — The Chemistry of Antacid Tablets
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: effervescent antacid tablets combine a solid acid, such as citric acid, with a carbonate or bicarbonate base, so that when dissolved in water the two react to release carbon dioxide gas as visible bubbles while neutralizing stomach acid.

quiz.q: What two general classes of compounds are typically combined in an effervescent antacid tablet?
options: Two different metals with no acid or base present
A solid acid and a carbonate or bicarbonate base
Only pure water and salt
Two identical acids with no base

quiz.q: What gas is released as bubbles when an effervescent tablet dissolves in water?
options: Carbon dioxide
Pure oxygen
Nitrogen gas
Hydrogen gas

quiz.q: What is the main therapeutic purpose of an antacid tablet?
options: Replacing water lost through dehydration
Increasing the acidity of the stomach
Providing a source of dietary sugar
Neutralizing excess stomach acid

quiz.q: Which of these is a common solid acid used in effervescent tablets?
options: Pure carbon
Citric acid
Liquid mercury
Table salt

quiz.q: Why does the fizzing reaction only occur once the tablet is dissolved in water?
options: The tablet reacts the same way whether or not it is dissolved in water
Water allows the acid and base components to dissolve and react with each other
The dry tablet already contains free carbon dioxide gas
Water prevents any reaction from occurring at all

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Reading: Comparing Translations of a Text
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Language strand: comparing different translations of the same text can reveal how word choice, tone, and cultural context shape meaning, since no translation is a perfectly neutral copy of the original.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Reading: Comparing Translations of a Text

quiz.q: What can comparing different translations of the same text reveal?
options: Only the exact number of pages in each version
How word choice, tone, and cultural context shape meaning
Nothing useful about the original text
A concept unrelated to reading

quiz.q: Is a translation ever a perfectly neutral copy of the original text?
options: No
Translations never differ from one another in any way
Yes, every translation is always perfectly neutral
A concept unrelated to translation

quiz.q: Why might two translators choose different words for the same original sentence?
options: Translators always choose the exact same words with no variation
This concept has no connection to translation
Each translator may interpret tone, culture, or meaning slightly differently
Word choice never affects how a translation is understood

quiz.q: Why might comparing translations deepen a reader’s understanding of a classic work of literature?
options: This concept has no connection to reading comprehension
It can reveal different interpretive choices and highlight aspects of meaning that a single translation might miss
Comparing translations never reveals anything new about a text
Every translation of a classic work is always identical

quiz.q: Why might cultural context be an important factor for a translator to consider?
options: Cultural context never affects how a text should be translated
Every language shares identical cultural expressions with no differences
Certain words or expressions may carry meanings specific to a culture that do not directly translate
This concept has no relevance to reading comprehension

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to Logarithms
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: a logarithm is the inverse operation of exponentiation, answering the question of what exponent a given base must be raised to in order to produce a certain number.

quiz.q: What is a logarithm the inverse operation of?
options: Addition
Division only
A concept unrelated to math
Exponentiation

quiz.q: Does a logarithm answer what exponent a base must be raised to in order to reach a certain number?
options: No, logarithms have no connection to exponents
A concept unrelated to logarithms
Yes
Logarithms only ever apply to subtraction

quiz.q: What is the logarithm base 10 of 100?
Why might logarithms be useful for solving an equation where the unknown value is an exponent?
options: This concept has no connection to algebra
Logarithms never help with solving any type of equation
They allow you to isolate and solve directly for the exponent
Exponents can never be solved for using any mathematical method

quiz.q: Why are logarithms used to measure things like earthquake magnitude on the Richter scale?
options: Earthquake magnitude is never measured using any mathematical scale
Logarithms have no connection to measuring real-world phenomena
This concept has no relevance to math
They can compress an enormous range of values into a more manageable scale

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Allelopathy — Chemical Warfare Between Plants
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: allelopathy is a biological phenomenon in which a plant releases chemical compounds into the environment that inhibit the germination, growth, or survival of neighbouring plant species, reducing competition for resources.

quiz.q: What is allelopathy?
options: A disease that only affects animal cells
A type of pollination strategy involving insects
A process where two plants merge into a single organism
A phenomenon in which a plant releases chemicals that inhibit nearby plant species

quiz.q: What is the main ecological benefit of allelopathy for the plant releasing the chemicals?
options: A guaranteed increase in local animal populations
Increased competition from every neighbouring plant species
The complete elimination of the need for sunlight
Reduced competition for resources like light, water, and nutrients

quiz.q: What might an allelopathic chemical inhibit in a neighbouring plant?
options: The neighbouring plants ability to photosynthesize sunlight directly
Seed germination or root growth
The colour of the neighbouring plants flowers only
Nothing, since allelopathic chemicals have no biological effect

quiz.q: Where might allelopathic compounds be released from a plant?
options: Only after the entire plant has died with no other release point
From the surrounding soil with no involvement from the plant itself
From its roots, leaves, or decomposing plant material
Only from the flowers, and nowhere else

quiz.q: Why might allelopathy be considered a form of chemical competition among plants?
options: It allows a plant to indirectly suppress nearby competitors without direct physical contact
It only occurs between plants and animals, never between two plants
It always requires two plants to physically touch to have any effect
Allelopathy has no connection to competition between organisms

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Composting and Organic Decomposition
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: composting relies on microbial decomposition reactions that break down complex organic molecules such as cellulose and proteins into simpler compounds, releasing carbon dioxide, water, and heat while forming nutrient-rich humus.

quiz.q: What process drives the breakdown of organic material during composting?
options: A single non-biological chemical reaction with no microorganisms involved
Complete evaporation of all organic matter
Nuclear fission of the organic material
Microbial decomposition reactions

quiz.q: Which complex organic molecules are broken down during composting?
options: Only inorganic salts
Only noble gases
Only pure metals
Cellulose and proteins

quiz.q: What gas is commonly released during the decomposition process in composting?
options: Carbon dioxide
Chlorine gas
Neon gas
Pure hydrogen gas only

quiz.q: What nutrient-rich material is formed as a result of composting?
options: Synthetic plastic
Pure crystalline salt
Humus
Liquid mercury

quiz.q: Why does a compost pile often feel warm during active decomposition?
options: Compost piles have no chemical reactions occurring within them
Decomposition always absorbs heat from the surrounding environment
The warmth comes only from direct sunlight exposure
The microbial breakdown reactions release heat as a byproduct

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: Motif, Genre, Voice, and Persuasion
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: students revisit motif and recurring symbols, the ballad, the process essay, active and passive voice, the roman a clef, clickbait headlines, the personal narrative speech, narrative distance, and the encomium.

quiz.q: What is a motif?
options: A single event that happens only once in a story
A formal citation style
A type of punctuation mark
A recurring image, phrase, or idea repeated throughout a text

quiz.q: What does a ballad primarily do?
options: Tells a story through verse, often set to music
Avoids any use of rhythm or repetition
Functions only as a formal legal document
Presents a list of unrelated facts

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a process essay?
options: To explain how to complete a task or how something works
To argue a single controversial opinion
To describe a personal memory with no instructional purpose
To summarize a work of fiction

quiz.q: What is a roman a clef?
options: A type of formal legal document
A novel in which real people or events are thinly disguised as fiction
A novel with no connection to reality whatsoever
A poem written entirely in French

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of an encomium?
options: To formally praise a person, achievement, or quality
To provide a neutral, purely factual report
To criticize a public figure
To argue against a popular opinion

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Polynomial Long Division
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: polynomial long division is a method for dividing a polynomial by another polynomial of equal or lesser degree, following a process similar to long division with numbers.

quiz.q: What does polynomial long division do?
options: Adds a list of polynomials together
Divides a polynomial by another polynomial
A concept unrelated to algebra
Multiplies two polynomials together

quiz.q: Is polynomial long division similar in process to long division with numbers?
options: A concept unrelated to polynomial long division
No, the two processes share no similarities at all
Polynomial long division never involves any division at all
Yes

quiz.q: What do you call the polynomial left over after a division that does not divide evenly?
options: The coefficient
The product
A concept unrelated to polynomial division
The remainder

quiz.q: Why might polynomial long division be useful when factoring a polynomial?
options: This concept has no connection to algebra
It can help confirm whether a given expression is a factor and simplify the polynomial
Polynomial long division never helps with factoring in any way
Factoring and division are always completely unrelated processes

quiz.q: Why is it important to arrange terms in order of degree before starting polynomial long division?
options: This concept has no connection to polynomial long division
Working in order of degree keeps the process organized and prevents errors when combining terms
The order of terms never has any effect on the division process
Terms should always be arranged in a completely random order

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology Review: Cell Biology, Genetics, Physiology, and Ecology
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: students revisit the cytoskeleton, endocrine disruptors, polyploidy, the blood-brain barrier, hibernation and torpor, quorum sensing, the diving reflex, RNA interference, and allelopathy.

quiz.q: What is the cytoskeleton?
options: A structure found only in bacterial cells
A type of carbohydrate stored in the nucleus
A dynamic network of protein filaments within a cell
A rigid outer shell surrounding the cell membrane

quiz.q: What is an endocrine disruptor?
options: A chemical compound that interferes with normal hormone signalling
A protein that has no interaction with the endocrine system
A hormone naturally produced by the pancreas
A type of vitamin required for healthy bones

quiz.q: What is polyploidy?
options: A type of asexual reproduction with no genetic change
A condition where an organism has no chromosomes at all
A disease affecting only animal cells
A condition in which an organism has more than two complete sets of chromosomes

quiz.q: What is the blood-brain barrier?
options: A selectively permeable layer of tightly joined cells lining the brain capillaries
A type of muscle found only in the heart
A bone structure that surrounds the entire brain
A layer of skin on the outside of the skull

quiz.q: What is allelopathy?
options: A disease that only affects animal cells
A process where two plants merge into a single organism
A type of pollination strategy involving insects
A phenomenon in which a plant releases chemicals that inhibit nearby plant species

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry Review: Coordination Chemistry, Materials, and Applied Reactions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand review: students revisit chelation therapy, vulcanization, reverse osmosis, catalytic converters, adhesive chemistry, enthalpy of solution, leather tanning, antacid effervescence, and the chemistry of composting.

quiz.q: What is a chelating agent?
options: A molecule that binds tightly to metal ions through multiple coordinate bonds
An acid with no metal-binding ability
A type of radioactive isotope
A gas used only in refrigeration

quiz.q: What is vulcanization?
options: A method of melting rubber into a liquid permanently
A chemical process that forms cross-links between polymer chains in rubber using sulfur
A process that removes all polymer chains from rubber
A physical process with no chemical reaction involved

quiz.q: What does reverse osmosis use to purify water?
options: External pressure forcing water through a semi-permeable membrane
Freezing the water into solid ice
Adding large amounts of salt to the water
Boiling the water at extremely high temperatures

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a catalytic converter?
options: Storing fuel before it reaches the engine
Converting harmful exhaust gases into less harmful substances
Cooling the engine during operation
Increasing the amount of pollution released by a vehicle

quiz.q: What process drives the breakdown of organic material during composting?
options: A single non-biological chemical reaction with no microorganisms involved
Nuclear fission of the organic material
Complete evaporation of all organic matter
Microbial decomposition reactions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: The Ode — Form and Address to a Subject
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: an ode is a formal, often elevated lyric poem that directly addresses and celebrates a person, object, or abstract quality, traditionally using a structured stanza pattern to build sustained praise or reflection.

quiz.q: What does an ode typically do?
options: Functions only as a legal or contractual document
Avoids any direct address to its subject
Presents a purely factual news report with no emotional content
Directly addresses and celebrates a person, object, or abstract quality

quiz.q: What tone does an ode traditionally use?
options: A casual, joking tone with no serious content
A purely instructional, step-by-step tone
A tone of complete indifference to its subject
A formal, elevated tone of sustained praise or reflection

quiz.q: Which of these could be the subject of an ode?
options: Only grammar rules
Only geometric shapes, and nothing else
Only historical dates with no emotional content
A beloved object, achievement, or abstract idea, addressed directly

quiz.q: How does an ode typically address its subject?
options: Ignoring the subject entirely after the title
Speaking to it directly, often as if it could listen
Never mentioning the subject by name
Describing the subject only in the third person with no direct address

quiz.q: Why might a poet choose the ode form rather than a shorter lyric?
options: The ode form forbids any reflection on a single subject
Odes must always be shorter than a single sentence
Its structured stanza pattern supports sustained, developed reflection on a single subject
The ode form has no structure of any kind

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus Preview: The Power Rule for Derivatives
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the power rule states that the derivative of x raised to an exponent n is n times x raised to the exponent n minus 1, giving a quick algebraic shortcut for differentiating polynomial terms without returning to the limit definition each time.

quiz.q: What does the power rule provide?
options: A quick algebraic shortcut for differentiating polynomial terms
A rule for simplifying fractions only
A method for factoring quadratic equations
A way to calculate the area under any curve exactly

quiz.q: According to the power rule, what is the derivative of x to the power n?
options: The reciprocal of x raised to the power n
n plus x
x raised to the power n plus 1
n times x raised to the power n minus 1

quiz.q: What method does the power rule let you avoid repeating for every polynomial term?
options: Substituting random values into the function
Multiplying every term by zero
Returning to the limit definition of the derivative each time
Graphing the function by hand

quiz.q: What is the derivative of a constant term, according to the power rule family of results?
options: Infinity
One
The constant itself
Zero

quiz.q: How does the power rule relate to the earlier limit definition of the derivative?
options: It has no connection to the limit definition at all
It is a shortcut result that can itself be proven using the limit definition
The power rule was discovered before the concept of a limit existed
It replaces the need for limits in every branch of mathematics

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Genetics: Epistasis — Gene Interactions and Modified Ratios
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: epistasis occurs when the expression of one gene is masked or modified by the effect of a different, non-allelic gene, producing phenotypic ratios that depart from the classic patterns predicted by simple Mendelian inheritance.

quiz.q: What is epistasis?
options: A type of cell division unrelated to genetics
A process where a single gene has no effect on phenotype at all
When the expression of one gene is masked or modified by a different, non-allelic gene
A disease caused only by environmental factors

quiz.q: What kind of phenotypic ratios does epistasis often produce?
options: Ratios that depart from the classic patterns predicted by simple Mendelian inheritance
No measurable ratios of any kind
Ratios that depend only on environmental temperature
Ratios that are always identical to simple Mendelian predictions

quiz.q: How many genes are involved in a typical epistatic interaction?
options: Zero genes, since epistasis is purely environmental
Every gene in the entire genome simultaneously
Only a single gene acting alone
At least two different, non-allelic genes

quiz.q: Why might epistasis make predicting offspring phenotypes more complex than a single-gene cross?
options: Epistasis has no effect on phenotype prediction at all
Only environmental factors affect phenotype when epistasis is present
Epistasis always makes phenotype prediction simpler than a single-gene cross
One gene can hide or alter the phenotypic effect of another gene entirely

quiz.q: Which of these best describes an epistatic gene?
options: A gene that has no interaction with any other gene
A gene that only affects eye colour
A gene found exclusively in bacteria
A gene whose alleles can suppress or modify the phenotype produced by a different gene

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Population Ecology: Growth Models
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Biology strand: population ecology studies how populations change over time, using models such as exponential growth, which assumes unlimited resources, and logistic growth, which accounts for environmental limits.

quiz.q: Population ecology studies how ___ change over time.
options: Only individual organisms, with no connection to populations
Only non-living systems
A concept unrelated to biology
Populations of organisms

quiz.q: Exponential growth models assume ___.
options: Resources are always extremely limited
Unlimited resources are available
No population growth occurs at all
A concept unrelated to population size

quiz.q: Logistic growth models account for ___.
options: Environmental limits on population growth
Unlimited resources with no environmental constraints
A concept unrelated to population ecology
Only exponential increases with no limiting factors

quiz.q: Why might a population’s growth rate slow down as it approaches an environment’s carrying capacity?
options: Resource availability has no connection to population size
Limited resources, such as food and space, can restrict further population growth
Populations always continue growing exponentially with no limits
Carrying capacity has no effect on population growth rate

quiz.q: Why are population growth models useful in ecology?
options: They help predict and understand how populations might change under different conditions
Population changes can never be predicted or modeled
This topic has no connection to understanding ecosystems
These models have no scientific value

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: Utopian Fiction and the Ideal Society
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: utopian fiction imagines a society organized around an idealized vision of order, equality, or harmony, often serving as a foil to dystopian fiction by exploring what a perfected world might require and whether it is achievable.

quiz.q: What does utopian fiction typically imagine?
options: A society identical in every way to the authors own
An idealized society organized around order, equality, or harmony
A purely historical account with no imagined elements
A society with no organization of any kind

quiz.q: How does utopian fiction often relate to dystopian fiction?
options: Utopian fiction always depicts total societal collapse
The two genres are identical with no meaningful difference
It serves as a contrasting foil exploring an idealized rather than a failed society
Dystopian fiction always depicts a perfect society

quiz.q: What central question do many utopian narratives explore?
options: Whether novels should have chapters
Whether poetry should rhyme
Whether a truly perfected society is achievable and what it would require
Whether grammar rules should be abolished

quiz.q: Which of these might a utopian narrative depict?
options: A community structured to eliminate poverty, conflict, or inequality
A community with no structure or planning whatsoever
A community with no relationship to social organization at all
A community deliberately designed to maximize suffering

quiz.q: Why might an author use a utopian setting to offer social commentary?
options: Social commentary is impossible within a fictional setting
Utopian settings are always purely decorative with no thematic purpose
A utopian setting removes any possibility of social commentary
An idealized world lets the author highlight what is missing or flawed in real societies

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus Preview: Finding Equations of Tangent Lines Using Derivatives
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: once the derivative of a function is known, its value at a specific point gives the slope of the tangent line there, which combined with the point itself allows a full equation of the tangent line to be written.

quiz.q: What does the derivative of a function at a specific point give?
options: The maximum value of the function everywhere
The y-intercept of the function
The slope of the tangent line at that point
The total area under the entire curve

quiz.q: What two pieces of information are needed to write the equation of a tangent line?
options: Two unrelated points chosen at random
The area under the curve and its perimeter
The slope from the derivative and a point on the curve
Only the y-intercept, with no slope required

quiz.q: Why is finding a tangent line equation a natural application of derivatives?
options: Tangent lines have no relationship to derivatives at all
Finding a tangent line requires no knowledge of slope
Tangent lines can only be found using integration
It directly uses the derivatives geometric meaning as an instantaneous slope

quiz.q: If a functions derivative at x = 2 is 5, what does that tell you about the tangent line there?
options: The tangent line at that point is horizontal
The function has a maximum value of 5 everywhere
The tangent line at that point has a slope of 5
The tangent line passes through the origin only

quiz.q: What form is commonly used to write a tangent line equation once slope and a point are known?
options: Point-slope form
Pythagorean Theorem
Quadratic formula
Standard form of a circle

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Vestigial Structures as Evidence for Evolution
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: vestigial structures are anatomical features that have lost most or all of their original function through evolutionary history, persisting in reduced form as evidence of an organisms ancestry and shared descent with species in which the structure remains functional.

quiz.q: What are vestigial structures?
options: Anatomical features that have lost most or all of their original function over evolutionary history
Structures found only in single-celled organisms
Structures that appear only in embryos and never in adults of any species
New structures that have never existed in any ancestor

quiz.q: What do vestigial structures provide evidence for?
options: A brand-new function unrelated to any ancestral trait
An organisms ancestry and shared descent with other species
The complete absence of evolutionary change in a species
The idea that species never share common ancestors

quiz.q: Why might a vestigial structure persist even though it no longer serves its original function?
options: Natural selection always removes any structure with no function immediately
Vestigial structures always provide a major survival advantage
Vestigial structures are required for reproduction in every species
Reduced structures with little cost are not always strongly selected against

quiz.q: Which of these would be an example of a vestigial structure?
options: A fully functional wing used for powered flight
Small, non-functional hip bones in some whale species
A muscle used constantly for essential daily movement
A fully functional eye used for normal vision

quiz.q: How do vestigial structures differ from structures that were never present in an ancestral lineage?
options: Vestigial structures always appear only in the most recently evolved species
Structures never present in an ancestor are always larger than vestigial ones
There is no difference between the two categories
Vestigial structures were once functional in an ancestor before becoming reduced

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Saponification — The Chemistry of Soap Making
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: saponification is the hydrolysis reaction of a fat or oil with a strong base that breaks triglycerides into glycerol and fatty acid salts, the fatty acid salts being the soap molecules that can bind both grease and water to lift dirt away.

quiz.q: What is saponification?
options: A reaction that converts soap back into a fat or oil
A reaction that only occurs between two acids
The hydrolysis reaction of a fat or oil with a strong base to form soap
A purely physical process with no chemical reaction involved

quiz.q: What two products does saponification break a triglyceride into?
options: Carbon dioxide and water only
Glycerol and fatty acid salts
Oxygen gas and a metal oxide
Two identical fatty acid molecules with no glycerol

quiz.q: Which product of saponification acts as soap?
options: The strong base used in the reaction
Water released during the reaction
The fatty acid salts
The glycerol byproduct

quiz.q: Why can soap molecules lift grease away using water?
options: They repel water completely and bind only to grease
They convert grease directly into glycerol
They dissolve grease into a gas that evaporates instantly
They can bind both grease and water at the same time

quiz.q: What type of reactant is required alongside a fat or oil to carry out saponification?
options: A pure metal with no other compound
A strong base
A weak organic acid only
A noble gas

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Rhetorical Precis — Structured Summary and Analysis
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a rhetorical precis is a highly structured four-sentence summary that identifies a texts main claim, its supporting method, its stated purpose and audience, and the rhetorical strategies the author uses to achieve that purpose.

quiz.q: What is a rhetorical precis?
options: A purely emotional response to a text with no analysis
A lengthy, unstructured retelling of an entire text
A list of grammar corrections for a text
A highly structured, condensed summary that analyzes both content and rhetorical strategy

quiz.q: What does the first sentence of a rhetorical precis typically identify?
options: The page number of the final paragraph
The texts main claim and its author
A list of unrelated vocabulary words
The publishers address

quiz.q: Besides summarizing content, what else does a rhetorical precis analyze?
options: The number of paragraphs in the text
The font size used in the original publication
The rhetorical strategies the author uses to achieve their purpose
The colour of the books cover

quiz.q: Why is a rhetorical precis useful for close reading?
options: It forces a reader to distinguish what a text says from how and why it says it
It requires no analysis of the texts purpose
It eliminates the need to read the text closely at all
It focuses only on counting the number of sentences

quiz.q: What element does a rhetorical precis typically identify about a texts audience?
options: The audiences favourite colour
The exact number of readers a text has had
Nothing regarding audience is ever considered
The intended audience and the authors purpose in addressing them

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Introduction to Function Notation, Domain, and Range
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: function notation, such as f(x), represents the output of a function for a given input, while the domain is the set of possible inputs and the range is the set of possible outputs.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Introduction to Function Notation, Domain, and Range

quiz.q: What does function notation like f(x) represent?
options: A random number with no connection to the function
A concept unrelated to algebra
The output of a function for a given input
The name of a variable with no other meaning

quiz.q: What is the domain of a function?
options: A concept unrelated to functions
A single fixed number only
The set of possible outputs
The set of possible inputs

quiz.q: What is the range of a function?
options: The set of possible inputs
The set of possible outputs
A concept unrelated to functions
A single fixed number only

quiz.q: If f(x) = x + 2, what is f(3)?
Why is function notation useful for describing a relationship between two variables?
options: It clearly shows how an output value depends on a specific input value
This concept has no connection to algebra
Function notation never shows any relationship between variables
Inputs and outputs are always completely unrelated to each other

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Photosynthetic Pigments and Paper Chromatography
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: leaves contain multiple photosynthetic pigments, including chlorophyll a, chlorophyll b, and carotenoids, each absorbing different wavelengths of light, and paper chromatography separates these pigments by exploiting their differing solubility as they travel up a solvent-soaked strip.

quiz.q: Which of these is a photosynthetic pigment found in leaves?
options: Insulin
Chlorophyll a
Hemoglobin
Keratin

quiz.q: Why do leaves typically contain more than one type of photosynthetic pigment?
options: Extra pigments have no functional purpose in photosynthesis
Different pigments absorb different wavelengths of light, broadening the range used for photosynthesis
Multiple pigments exist only to change the colour of flowers
Leaves contain only a single pigment, never more than one

quiz.q: What does paper chromatography use to separate plant pigments?
options: An electrical current passed directly through the leaf
Differing pigment solubility as they travel up a solvent-soaked strip
A high-powered microscope with no solvent involved
A process that destroys all pigments before separation

quiz.q: Which pigment type often produces the yellow and orange colours seen in chromatography separations of leaf extract?
options: Keratin
Chlorophyll a exclusively
Melanin
Carotenoids

quiz.q: Why do different pigments end up at different positions on a chromatography strip?
options: They travel at different rates depending on their solubility in the solvent
Pigments are sorted by weight using a centrifuge instead
All pigments always travel at exactly the same rate
