Speaking that is read word-for-word from a prepared script
Speaking that avoids any organization whatsoever
Speaking that is organized and delivered without a fully scripted text

quiz.q: Why is staying composed important when answering an unexpected or challenging question?
options: Staying composed guarantees the question will not be asked again
Only written responses benefit from composure, not spoken ones
Composure has no effect on how an answer is received
It helps the speaker respond thoughtfully rather than defensively

quiz.q: What skill helps a speaker understand exactly what an audience member is really asking?
options: Active listening
Ignoring the audience members tone entirely
Answering before the question is fully asked
Speaking louder than the audience member

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Trigonometry: The Pythagorean Trigonometric Identity
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: the Pythagorean trigonometric identity states that sine squared plus cosine squared of an angle always equals one, a relationship derived directly from the Pythagorean Theorem applied to the unit circle.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Trigonometry: The Pythagorean Trigonometric Identity

quiz.q: What does the Pythagorean trigonometric identity state?
options: Sine minus cosine always equals one
Tangent squared always equals negative one
Sine plus cosine always equals zero
Sine squared plus cosine squared of an angle equals one

quiz.q: From what earlier concept is the Pythagorean trigonometric identity derived?
options: The quadratic formula
The Pythagorean Theorem applied to the unit circle
The binomial theorem
The distance formula only

quiz.q: If sine of an angle is 0, what must cosine squared equal, according to the identity?
Why is this identity considered fundamental in trigonometry?
options: It only works for angles greater than 360 degrees
It has no use beyond a single specific angle
It connects sine and cosine for any angle and supports many other identities
It contradicts the definitions of sine and cosine

quiz.q: The Pythagorean trigonometric identity applies to ___.
options: Only angles less than 10 degrees
Only angles measured in a right triangle
Only angles equal to exactly 90 degrees
Any angle, since it holds true for all real values

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Island Biogeography and Species-Area Relationships
subjects.summary: Students learn how island biogeography theory predicts species richness on an island based on the balance between immigration and extinction rates, and how island size and distance from the mainland shift that balance.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Ecology: Island Biogeography and Species-Area Relationships

quiz.q: According to island biogeography theory, larger islands tend to support more species mainly because they have:
options: More available habitat and resources, lowering extinction rates
Higher extinction rates
No competition among species
Lower immigration rates

quiz.q: Islands located closer to the mainland typically have higher species richness because they experience:
options: No immigration at all
Higher immigration rates
Lower immigration rates
Higher extinction rates only

quiz.q: Island biogeography theory predicts that species richness on an island reaches equilibrium when:
options: Every available niche is permanently filled by one species
Immigration completely stops
The rate of new species immigrating equals the rate of species going extinct
All species have gone extinct

quiz.q: Which island would be predicted to have the LOWEST species richness according to the theory?
options: A small island far from the mainland
A small island close to the mainland
A large island far from the mainland
A large island close to the mainland

quiz.q: Island biogeography principles are also useful for studying:
options: Only actual ocean islands
Habitat fragments surrounded by human development, which act like ecological islands
The chemical composition of rocks
Weather patterns unrelated to ecology

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Sound Waves and the Doppler Effect
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Physics strand: the Doppler effect describes the change in a sound wave’s perceived frequency when its source is moving relative to an observer, such as a siren sounding higher-pitched as it approaches.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Sound Waves and the Doppler Effect

quiz.q: The Doppler effect describes a change in a wave’s perceived ___ due to relative motion between source and observer.
options: A property unrelated to sound waves
Colour
Frequency
Only its speed of light

quiz.q: As a sound source moves toward an observer, the perceived pitch typically ___.
options: Remains completely unaffected by the motion
Becomes completely silent
Increases
Decreases

quiz.q: As a sound source moves away from an observer, the perceived pitch typically ___.
options: Increases
Remains completely unaffected by the motion
Becomes completely silent
Decreases

quiz.q: Which is a common real-world example of the Doppler effect?
options: A siren sounding higher-pitched as an ambulance approaches, then lower as it passes
A concept unrelated to sound waves
A sound that never changes in pitch under any circumstances
A stationary object producing a constantly increasing pitch

quiz.q: Why is the Doppler effect relevant beyond sound waves, such as in astronomy?
options: This concept has no connection to any other type of wave
The Doppler effect only applies to sound and has no other applications
Astronomy never makes use of wave-related phenomena
A similar shift can be observed in light waves, helping scientists study the motion of distant objects

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: Ode, Utopia, Rhetoric, and Media Literacy
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: students revisit the ode, utopian fiction, the rhetorical precis, modal verbs and certainty, the roman-fleuve, astroturfing, the lyric essay, the doppelganger motif, and handling audience questions.

quiz.q: What does an ode typically do?
options: Avoids any direct address to its subject
Presents a purely factual news report with no emotional content
Directly addresses and celebrates a person, object, or abstract quality
Functions only as a legal or contractual document

quiz.q: What does utopian fiction typically imagine?
options: A purely historical account with no imagined elements
A society identical in every way to the authors own
A society with no organization of any kind
An idealized society organized around order, equality, or harmony

quiz.q: What do modal verbs allow a writer to signal?
options: The physical length of a sentence
Varying degrees of certainty, obligation, or possibility
The number of syllables in a word
The exact tense of every verb in a sentence

quiz.q: What is astroturfing?
options: A formal government policy announcement
An organized campaign disguised as spontaneous grassroots public opinion
A type of academic citation style
A genuine, entirely spontaneous grassroots movement with no organization

quiz.q: What is a doppelganger in fiction?
options: A type of formal poem with a fixed rhyme scheme
A narrator who exists outside the story entirely
A double or mirror-self figure who closely resembles the protagonist
A minor character who appears only once with no significance

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Algebra: Solving Radical Equations
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: a radical equation contains a variable inside a radical, and solving one typically involves isolating the radical, then raising both sides of the equation to a matching power to remove it, followed by checking for extraneous solutions.

quiz.q: What defines a radical equation?
options: An equation in which a variable appears inside a radical, such as a square root
An equation that cannot be graphed
An equation with no variables of any kind
An equation that only involves whole number coefficients

quiz.q: What is a common first step in solving a radical equation?
options: Multiplying both sides by zero
Deleting the radical without performing any operation
Immediately squaring every term with no isolation first
Isolating the radical on one side of the equation

quiz.q: After isolating a square root, what operation removes it from the equation?
options: Dividing both sides by the variable
Taking the square root of both sides again
Squaring both sides of the equation
Adding one to both sides

quiz.q: Why must solutions to a radical equation always be checked in the original equation?
options: Squaring both sides never changes the set of valid solutions
Radical equations always have exactly one guaranteed solution
Checking solutions is never necessary once an equation is solved
Squaring both sides can introduce extraneous solutions that do not actually satisfy the original equation

quiz.q: If solving x = sqrt(x+2) produces a candidate solution of x=-1, why would this be rejected?
options: Negative numbers can never appear anywhere in a radical equation
Substituting -1 back into the original equation does not produce a true statement
The candidate solution must always be accepted without checking
The equation has no valid solutions under any circumstances

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology Review: Genetics, Physiology, and Ecology
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: students revisit epistasis, vestigial structures, photosynthetic pigments, chemoreception, countercurrent exchange, autoimmune disorders, detritivores, the renin-angiotensin system, and genomic imprinting.

quiz.q: What is epistasis?
options: A type of cell division unrelated to genetics
When the expression of one gene is masked or modified by a different, non-allelic gene
A disease caused only by environmental factors
A process where a single gene has no effect on phenotype at all

quiz.q: What are vestigial structures?
options: Structures that appear only in embryos and never in adults of any species
Anatomical features that have lost most or all of their original function over evolutionary history
New structures that have never existed in any ancestor
Structures found only in single-celled organisms

quiz.q: What is chemoreception?
options: The process of detecting sound waves using the ear
The sensory process of detecting dissolved or airborne chemical molecules
The process of detecting light using the retina
The process of detecting temperature changes in the skin only

quiz.q: What causes an autoimmune disorder?
options: A purely mechanical injury to a single organ
An excess of vitamin intake over a short period
A complete absence of any immune system activity
The immune system fails to distinguish the bodys own cells from foreign invaders

quiz.q: What is genomic imprinting?
options: A permanent mutation in the DNA sequence of a gene
An epigenetic phenomenon where certain genes are expressed differently depending on parental origin
A process that always silences every gene equally regardless of origin
A form of asexual reproduction with no parental contribution

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Electric Fields and Static Discharge
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Physics strand: an electric field surrounds a charged object and exerts a force on other charges within it, and static discharge occurs when built-up static electricity suddenly transfers between objects.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Electric Fields and Static Discharge

quiz.q: An electric field surrounds a charged object and exerts a force on ___.
options: Other charges within that field
Nothing, as electric fields exert no force
A concept unrelated to electricity
Only objects with no charge at all

quiz.q: Static discharge occurs when ___.
options: Built-up static electricity suddenly transfers between objects
A concept unrelated to static electricity
An object loses all electrical properties permanently
Electric charge is permanently trapped with no possible transfer

quiz.q: Which of these is a common everyday example of static discharge?
options: Feeling a small shock after touching a doorknob on a dry day
A situation with no connection to static electricity
A process unrelated to electric fields
An object that never builds up any electric charge

quiz.q: Why might friction, such as rubbing a balloon on hair, cause a build-up of static charge?
options: Electrons can never be transferred between materials through friction
Friction never has any effect on electric charge
Friction can transfer electrons between materials, leaving one object with excess charge
Static charge only occurs without any physical contact between objects

quiz.q: Why is understanding electric fields important in fields like electronics engineering?
options: It helps explain how charged components interact and influence one another in a circuit or device
Electric fields have no relevance to electronics or engineering
This concept only applies to naturally occurring static electricity, not engineered devices
Electric fields never influence how electronic components function

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Elegy and Occasional Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Language strand: an elegy is a reflective poem or piece of writing that mourns a loss, often a persons death, using formal, contemplative language to express grief and honour memory.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Writing: The Elegy and Occasional Writing

quiz.q: What is an elegy?
options: A reflective poem or piece of writing that mourns a loss
A type of business letter
A scientific report format
A humorous poem with no serious tone

quiz.q: What tone does an elegy typically use?
options: A tone with no emotional content
An aggressive and mocking tone
A purely comedic tone
A formal, contemplative tone expressing grief and reflection

quiz.q: What is an elegy commonly written to honour?
options: The memory of someone who has died
A recipe for a meal
A new invention
A sports victory

quiz.q: Occasional writing refers to writing composed for what purpose?
options: Only fictional stories with no real-world connection
A specific event or occasion, such as a memorial or celebration
No specific purpose at all
Only technical manuals

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose formal language in an elegy?
options: Formal language is never appropriate for this purpose
To make the subject seem unimportant
To confuse the reader intentionally
To convey the seriousness and depth of the loss being honoured

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: The Product Rule for Derivatives
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the product rule states that the derivative of a product of two functions equals the derivative of the first function times the second, plus the first function times the derivative of the second, letting you differentiate products without expanding them first.

quiz.q: What does the product rule let you differentiate?
options: A product of two functions, without expanding the product first
Only the sum of two functions
Only a single function with no multiplication involved
Only a function divided by a constant

quiz.q: According to the product rule, the derivative of f times g equals what?
options: The derivative of f times the derivative of g
f times g with no derivatives taken at all
The derivative of f times g, plus f times the derivative of g
The sum of f and g with no multiplication

quiz.q: Why is the product rule needed instead of just multiplying the derivatives of each factor?
options: Derivatives cannot be applied to any product of functions
The product rule is optional and never affects the result
Multiplying the individual derivatives always gives the correct answer
Multiplying the individual derivatives together does not give the correct derivative of the product

quiz.q: What must you identify before applying the product rule to an expression?
options: The two separate functions being multiplied together
The degree of the final derivative in advance
The exact numerical value of the function at one point only
The sum of all constants in the expression

quiz.q: How does the product rule relate to the earlier power rule?
options: The product rule replaces the power rule in every case
The product rule extends differentiation to products of functions, while the power rule handles a single power of x
The two rules are entirely unrelated and never used together
The power rule can only be used for products, never single terms

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Microbiology: Horizontal Gene Transfer in Bacteria
subjects.summary: Students compare the three natural mechanisms bacteria use to exchange genetic material without reproduction -- transformation, conjugation, and transduction -- and discuss their role in spreading traits like antibiotic resistance.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Microbiology: Horizontal Gene Transfer in Bacteria

quiz.q: In bacterial conjugation, genetic material is transferred:
options: By bacteria absorbing free DNA from their environment
Directly between two bacterial cells through a pilus
Through a virus that infects two different bacteria
Only during bacterial binary fission

quiz.q: Transformation refers to a bacterium's ability to:
options: Inject DNA into a virus
Divide asexually
Change its own genome spontaneously with no outside source
Take up free DNA fragments from its surrounding environment

quiz.q: In transduction, genetic material is transferred between bacteria by:
options: Binary fission
Diffusion through the cell wall
Direct cell-to-cell contact through a pilus
A bacteriophage (virus) that accidentally packages bacterial DNA

quiz.q: Horizontal gene transfer is a major concern in medicine because it can rapidly spread:
options: Viral DNA into human cells
Antibiotic resistance genes between different bacterial species
Mitochondrial DNA between organisms
Chromosomal mutations in humans

quiz.q: Which structure allows two bacterial cells to connect directly during conjugation?
options: Pilus
Ribosome
Flagellum
Capsule

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Solutions and Solubility: Concentration and Saturation
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Chemistry strand: a solution forms when a solute dissolves in a solvent, concentration describes the amount of solute relative to solvent, and a saturated solution has dissolved the maximum amount of solute possible at a given temperature.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Solutions and Solubility: Concentration and Saturation

quiz.q: A solution forms when a ___ dissolves in a solvent.
options: A substance that never mixes with a solvent
Solute
Solvent, dissolving into itself
A concept unrelated to chemistry

quiz.q: Concentration describes the amount of ___ relative to solvent in a solution.
options: Only the solvent, with no connection to solute
Temperature exclusively
A property unrelated to solutions
Solute

quiz.q: A saturated solution has dissolved ___.
options: No solute whatsoever
The maximum amount of solute possible at a given temperature
An unlimited amount of solute regardless of temperature
A concept unrelated to solubility

quiz.q: Why might increasing the temperature of a solvent, such as water, allow more solute to dissolve?
options: Temperature never affects how much solute can dissolve
This concept has no connection to solubility
Increasing temperature always decreases solubility for every solute
Higher temperatures often increase a solvent’s capacity to dissolve certain solutes

quiz.q: Which of these is an example of a solution encountered in everyday life?
options: Sand mixed with water that settles to the bottom
Oil floating on top of water with no mixing
Salt fully dissolved in water
A concept unrelated to solutions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Fairy Tale Retelling and Revisionist Fiction
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a fairy tale retelling takes a familiar traditional story and reworks its point of view, setting, or values, often to question the original tales assumptions about gender, power, or morality, turning a childhood tale into a vehicle for adult critique.

quiz.q: What does a fairy tale retelling typically do to a familiar traditional story?
options: Removes every character from the original tale
Converts the tale into a strictly factual historical record
Reworks its point of view, setting, or values
Repeats the original story word for word with no changes

quiz.q: What might a revisionist fairy tale question about the original story?
options: Its assumptions about gender, power, or morality
The number of pages in the original text
The publication date of the earliest printed version
The spelling of the original title only

quiz.q: Why might an author retell a story from a minor or villainous characters point of view?
options: Doing so always shortens the story to a single sentence
It guarantees the retelling will be identical to the original
To reveal a perspective the original tale left out or dismissed
Minor characters have no perspective worth exploring

quiz.q: What effect can a revisionist retelling have on a readers view of a familiar tale?
options: It can unsettle assumptions the reader took for granted in the original
It proves the original tale was factually inaccurate
It has no effect on how the reader interprets the original
It always makes the reader forget the original story entirely

quiz.q: What genre most commonly supplies source material for these retellings?
options: Legal contracts
Contemporary financial reports
Scientific lab manuals
Traditional fairy tales and folklore

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: The Quotient Rule for Derivatives
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the quotient rule gives the derivative of one function divided by another as the derivative of the numerator times the denominator minus the numerator times the derivative of the denominator, all divided by the denominator squared.

quiz.q: What does the quotient rule find the derivative of?
options: Only the product of two functions
Only the sum of two functions
Only a single constant term
One function divided by another function

quiz.q: What is the denominator of the result produced by the quotient rule?
options: The original denominator function, squared
The original numerator function, squared
The sum of the numerator and denominator
A constant equal to one

quiz.q: In the quotient rule, what is subtracted in the numerator of the result?
options: A constant with no relation to either function
The denominator function times itself
The numerator function times the derivative of the denominator
The derivative of the numerator times the derivative of the denominator

quiz.q: Why cannot you simply divide the derivative of the numerator by the derivative of the denominator?
options: That shortcut does not produce the correct derivative of a quotient
Division of derivatives is undefined in every case
That shortcut always produces the correct derivative of a quotient
The quotient rule forbids any use of division

quiz.q: When might the quotient rule be especially useful in Grade 11 Functions?
options: Only when no denominator is present at all
Only when differentiating a single constant
When differentiating a rational function expressed as one polynomial divided by another
Only for functions with no variables

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Seed Dormancy and Germination Triggers
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: seed dormancy is a temporary suspension of active growth that allows a seed to survive unfavourable conditions until specific environmental triggers, such as adequate moisture, suitable temperature, or exposure to light, signal that conditions are right for germination.

quiz.q: What is seed dormancy?
options: A permanent state that a seed can never leave
The complete death of a seed embryo
A temporary suspension of active growth that allows a seed to survive unfavourable conditions
Rapid growth that occurs immediately after a seed forms

quiz.q: Name one environmental trigger that can signal a dormant seed to germinate.
options: Total darkness with no light at any point
Freezing the seed permanently
Adequate moisture
A complete absence of any water

quiz.q: Why is seed dormancy advantageous for a plant species?
options: It prevents a seed from ever germinating under any circumstance
It guarantees every seed will germinate immediately regardless of conditions
It lets seeds survive unfavourable conditions until conditions improve
It has no survival advantage of any kind

quiz.q: What happens to a seed once the right combination of environmental triggers is present?
options: It immediately dies
It begins to germinate
It enters a deeper state of permanent dormancy
It reverses its development back to a single cell

quiz.q: How might exposure to light act as a germination trigger for certain seed species?
options: Light can signal that a seed is near the soil surface, a favourable position for a seedling to grow
Light has no relationship to germination in any species
Seeds cannot detect light in any way
Light always prevents germination in every seed species

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Friction, Air Resistance, and Terminal Velocity
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Physics strand: friction is a force that opposes motion between surfaces in contact, air resistance is a form of friction from air molecules, and terminal velocity occurs when a falling object’s speed becomes constant as air resistance balances gravity.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Friction, Air Resistance, and Terminal Velocity

quiz.q: Friction is best described as a force that ___.
options: A concept unrelated to physics
Has no effect on moving objects
Always increases an object’s speed
Opposes motion between surfaces in contact

quiz.q: Air resistance is a form of friction caused by ___.
options: A concept unrelated to friction
Gravity acting alone, with no connection to air
A vacuum with no molecules present at all
Air molecules interacting with a moving object

quiz.q: Terminal velocity occurs when a falling object’s speed becomes ___.
options: Constant, as air resistance balances the force of gravity
Continuously increasing with no upper limit
A concept unrelated to falling objects
Zero, as the object stops moving entirely

quiz.q: Why might a skydiver reach terminal velocity before opening a parachute?
options: This concept has no connection to falling objects
Air resistance has no effect on a skydiver’s speed
Air resistance eventually increases enough to balance the force of gravity pulling them downward
Gravity stops acting on the skydiver at a certain height

quiz.q: Why does a flat sheet of paper fall more slowly than a crumpled ball of the same paper?
options: The flat sheet has more surface area, increasing air resistance and slowing its fall
A crumpled ball always experiences greater air resistance than a flat sheet
Surface area has no effect on how air resistance acts on a falling object
This concept has no connection to friction or air resistance

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Conditional Sentences and Hypothetical Reasoning
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: conditional sentences pair an if-clause with a result clause to express real possibilities, hypothetical situations, or outcomes contrary to fact, and choosing the right conditional pattern lets a writer signal exactly how likely or how imaginary a scenario is.

quiz.q: What two parts make up a conditional sentence?
options: A subject and a verb with no clause structure at all
Two independent clauses joined only by a semicolon
A question followed by a one-word answer
An if-clause and a result clause

quiz.q: What does a conditional sentence about an outcome contrary to fact typically signal?
options: A simple statement of present fact
A hypothetical situation that did not actually happen
An event that is certain to happen tomorrow
A command directed at the reader

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose a conditional sentence over a direct statement?
options: To signal how likely or imaginary a scenario is rather than asserting it as fact
Direct statements are grammatically forbidden in academic writing
Conditional sentences always sound less formal than direct statements
Conditional sentences remove all meaning from a sentence

quiz.q: Which verb form commonly appears in the if-clause of a hypothetical past conditional?
options: A future tense verb form
The imperative mood only
A past perfect verb form
No verb at all

quiz.q: What kind of reasoning do conditional sentences allow a writer to express?
options: Reasoning expressed only through single-word exclamations
Reasoning limited only to historical facts
Reasoning about possible, hypothetical, or contrary-to-fact outcomes
Reasoning that cannot involve cause and effect

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: The Chain Rule for Composite Functions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the chain rule differentiates a composite function by multiplying the derivative of the outer function, evaluated at the inner function, by the derivative of the inner function, allowing nested functions to be differentiated layer by layer.

quiz.q: What kind of function does the chain rule differentiate?
options: A composite function, made of one function nested inside another
Only a function with no variables at all
Only a function with a single, unnested term
Only a constant function

quiz.q: What two derivatives does the chain rule multiply together?
options: The derivative of the outer function and the outer function itself
The derivative of the outer function and the derivative of the inner function
The sum of the inner and outer functions
Two unrelated constants with no connection to the function

quiz.q: What does the phrase differentiating layer by layer describe about the chain rule?
options: Removing all layers before differentiating anything
Working from the outermost function inward through each nested layer
Differentiating every layer at the exact same time with no order
Differentiating only the innermost layer and ignoring the rest

quiz.q: Why is the chain rule essential for a function like the square of a polynomial?
options: The inner polynomial can always be ignored during differentiation
The polynomial inside must be treated as the inner function nested inside the squaring operation
The chain rule only applies to trigonometric functions

quiz.q: How does the chain rule relate to the product and quotient rules?

The chain rule replaces the need for the product and quotient rules entirely

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Embryonic Development -- Cleavage to Differentiation
subjects.summary: Students trace early animal embryonic development, from the rapid cell divisions of cleavage through gastrulation and the formation of the three primary germ layers that give rise to all body tissues.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Biology: Embryonic Development -- Cleavage to Differentiation

quiz.q: The rapid series of cell divisions immediately following fertilization, which increases cell number without increasing overall embryo size, is called:

Cleavage
Ovulation

quiz.q: Gastrulation is the process during which the embryo:

Implants directly into the ovary

quiz.q: Which of the three germ layers gives rise to the skin and nervous system?

quiz.q: Cell differentiation during development occurs even though nearly all cells in the embryo contain:

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Enzymes and Biological Catalysts
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Biology strand: an enzyme is a biological catalyst, typically a protein, that speeds up chemical reactions in living organisms without being consumed in the process.

quiz.q: An enzyme is best described as ___.
options: A molecule that always slows down chemical reactions

A type of cell found only in plants
A concept unrelated to biology

quiz.q: Enzymes are typically composed of ___.

Pure carbon with no other elements

quiz.q: A defining feature of an enzyme is that it ___.

Is not consumed or permanently changed during the reaction it catalyzes

quiz.q: Why might an enzyme’s shape be important to its function?
options: Its shape allows it to bind specifically to a particular substrate molecule
This concept has no relevance to biological catalysts
An enzyme’s shape has no connection to its function

quiz.q: Why might extreme heat cause an enzyme to stop functioning properly?
options: Heat never has any effect on an enzyme’s structure or function
Enzymes always function more effectively at extremely high temperatures
High temperatures can change an enzyme’s shape, preventing it from binding to its substrate

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Independent Reading: Climate Fiction and Environmental Storytelling
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: climate fiction, often called cli-fi, imagines characters and societies confronting environmental change and its consequences, using narrative to make abstract scientific projections feel immediate, personal, and morally urgent.

quiz.q: What does climate fiction typically imagine?
options: Characters and societies confronting environmental change and its consequences
Purely historical events with no connection to climate
A setting entirely disconnected from any scientific concept
A world with no environmental concerns of any kind

quiz.q: What is another common name for climate fiction?
options: Epistolary fiction
Detective fiction
Hard-boiled fiction
Cli-fi

quiz.q: What effect can narrative have on abstract scientific projections about climate change?
options: It always makes scientific projections seem less believable
It removes any moral dimension from the topic
It can make the projections feel immediate, personal, and morally urgent
Narrative has no effect on how readers process scientific information

quiz.q: Why might an author set a climate fiction story in a near-future version of a real city?
options: Doing so guarantees the story cannot be read as fiction
Near-future settings remove all stakes from a narrative
Real cities cannot appear in works of fiction
To make the environmental consequences feel plausible and close to the readers own experience

quiz.q: What kind of urgency does climate fiction often aim to create in its readers?
options: An urgency limited strictly to questions of grammar
An urgency to memorize scientific formulas
A moral and emotional urgency about environmental change
No urgency of any kind, since the genre is purely decorative

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Financial Literacy: Inflation and the Time Value of Money
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: inflation gradually reduces the purchasing power of money over time, and the time value of money reflects the principle that a given amount of money today is generally worth more than the same amount received in the future.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Financial Literacy: Inflation and the Time Value of Money

quiz.q: What does inflation gradually reduce?
options: The physical size of paper currency
The number of digits in a bank account
The purchasing power of money over time
The total number of banks in a country

quiz.q: What does the time value of money principle state?
options: Money available today is generally worth more than the same amount received in the future
Money always loses all of its value the moment it is earned
Future money is always worth more than present money in every case
Time has no connection to the value of money whatsoever

quiz.q: Why is money received today generally considered more valuable than the same amount in the future?
options: It can be invested or saved to grow in value before that future date arrives
Future money always arrives with no possible delay or risk
There is no mathematical relationship between time and money
Money received today can never be saved or invested at all

quiz.q: If inflation rises faster than the interest earned on savings, what happens to the real value of those savings?
options: Inflation has no effect on the value of savings at all
The real purchasing power of the savings can decline over time
Savings automatically double in value regardless of inflation
The real purchasing power always increases no matter what

quiz.q: Understanding inflation and the time value of money is especially useful when planning for what kind of financial decision?
options: Deciding what colour to paint a room
Choosing a favourite school subject
Selecting a route to walk to school
Long-term savings and investment decisions

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Ecological Niches and Competitive Exclusion
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a species ecological niche describes its full role in an ecosystem, including the resources it uses and the conditions it tolerates, and the competitive exclusion principle holds that two species cannot indefinitely occupy the exact same niche in the same habitat without one outcompeting the other.

quiz.q: What does a species ecological niche describe?
options: Its full role in an ecosystem, including the resources it uses and conditions it tolerates
The exact number of offspring a species produces each year
Only the geographic location where a species was first discovered
Only the physical size of an individual organism

quiz.q: What does the competitive exclusion principle state?
options: Competition between species never affects their long-term survival
Two species can always occupy the exact same niche forever without conflict
Two species cannot indefinitely occupy the exact same niche in the same habitat
Only predators are ever subject to competitive exclusion

quiz.q: What typically happens when two species compete for the exact same niche in the same habitat?
options: Both species always thrive equally forever with no change
The habitat immediately becomes uninhabitable for both species
The two species instantly merge into a single species
One species eventually outcompetes and displaces the other

quiz.q: What resources might be included as part of a species niche?
options: Only the exact date the species was named by scientists
Only the colour of the species fur or feathers
Food sources, habitat space, and other resources the species depends on
Nothing related to resources at all

quiz.q: How might two similar species avoid competitive exclusion when living in the same area?
options: By becoming genetically identical to one another
By eliminating all other species from the habitat
Competitive exclusion cannot be avoided under any circumstance
By using slightly different resources or occupying slightly different niches

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Review: Solutions, Immune System, Circulatory/Respiratory, and Radioactivity
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science strand review: this lesson revisits solutions and solubility, the immune system, the circulatory and respiratory systems, and radioactivity and half-life from Days 61-69.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Review: Solutions, Immune System, Circulatory/Respiratory, and Radioactivity

quiz.q: A solution forms when a ___ dissolves in a solvent.
options: A substance that never mixes with a solvent
A concept unrelated to chemistry
Solvent, dissolving into itself
Solute

quiz.q: A pathogen is best described as ___.
options: A cell that always protects the body from disease
A concept unrelated to biology
A nutrient the body requires to survive
A microorganism, such as a bacterium or virus, that can cause disease

quiz.q: The circulatory system is primarily responsible for ___.
options: Producing hormones exclusively
Breaking down food for digestion
Transporting blood, oxygen, and nutrients throughout the body
A function unrelated to body systems

quiz.q: Radioactive decay occurs when ___.
options: A concept unrelated to atomic structure
A molecule dissolves completely in a solvent
An unstable atomic nucleus releases energy and particles over time
An atom becomes permanently stable with no further change

quiz.q: Why is it valuable to review chemistry, biology, and physics concepts like solutions, immunity, body systems, and radioactivity together?
options: These topics are entirely unrelated to each other
It helps connect and reinforce related science concepts learned across recent lessons
Review provides no benefit in science
Each topic must always be studied in isolation

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Political Cartoons and the Grammar of Visual Satire
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a political cartoon compresses commentary on a public issue into symbolic imagery, exaggerated caricature, and brief text, relying on a shared visual vocabulary of labels, symbols, and irony to make a persuasive argument in a single frame.

quiz.q: What does a political cartoon typically compress into a single frame?
options: Commentary on a public issue using symbolic imagery and caricature
A detailed scientific diagram with no commentary
A complete, unabridged transcript of a news broadcast
A purely decorative image with no argument at all

quiz.q: What technique does a political cartoonist often use to exaggerate a public figures features?
options: Strict photographic realism
Caricature
Blank, empty panels with no imagery
Verbatim quotation with no visual alteration

quiz.q: What shared visual vocabulary do political cartoons often rely on?
options: Complex mathematical notation
Musical notation
Legal citations
Labels, symbols, and irony

quiz.q: Why might a cartoonist label an object or figure directly within the image?
options: Labels are required by law on every published image
To make the symbolic meaning of the image unambiguous to the viewer
Labels always remove all meaning from a cartoon
Cartoonists label images only to credit the printer

quiz.q: What persuasive goal does a political cartoon typically pursue?
options: Avoiding any commentary on public issues whatsoever
Presenting a perfectly neutral, opinion-free record of events
Providing a complete academic bibliography
Making an argument about a public issue through a single striking image

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Algebra: Solving Exponential Equations
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: an exponential equation has the variable in the exponent, and it can be solved by rewriting both sides with a common base and setting the exponents equal, or by applying logarithms when a common base cannot easily be found.

quiz.q: What defines an exponential equation?
options: An equation in which the variable appears in the exponent
An equation that only involves whole number coefficients
An equation with no exponents of any kind
An equation that cannot be graphed

quiz.q: If both sides of an exponential equation are rewritten with equal bases, what can then be done?
options: The bases must be multiplied together first
Nothing further can be done to solve the equation
The exponents can be set equal to each other and solved directly
The equation becomes impossible to solve

quiz.q: When the bases of an exponential equation cannot easily be made equal, what tool is commonly used instead?
options: A protractor
The distributive property alone
Long division
Logarithms

quiz.q: Solve for x: 2^x = 8.
Why must the base of an exponential equation be positive and not equal to one?
options: Because negative numbers cannot appear anywhere in mathematics
So the exponential function is well defined and produces a consistent, predictable output for each exponent
So the equation always has infinitely many solutions
Because the base has no effect on the equations solutions

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Blood Types and the ABO/Rh Blood Group Systems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: the ABO blood group system classifies blood by the presence or absence of A and B antigens on red blood cells, while the Rh system adds a positive or negative marker, and mismatched transfusions can trigger a dangerous immune reaction against foreign antigens.

quiz.q: What does the ABO blood group system classify?
options: Blood based on the persons eye colour
Blood based on the presence or absence of A and B antigens on red blood cells
Blood based on its exact volume in the body
Blood based on the persons age at donation

quiz.q: What does the Rh system add to a blood type classification?
options: An exact percentage of water content
A colour code with no biological meaning
A numeric score from one to ten
A positive or negative marker

quiz.q: What can happen if a person receives a transfusion of a mismatched blood type?
options: A dangerous immune reaction against the foreign antigens
Immediate improvement in the recipients blood pressure only
No effect of any kind on the recipient
An automatic conversion of the donated blood to the recipients type

quiz.q: What are antigens, in the context of the ABO blood group system?
options: Molecules found only in bone marrow, never on red blood cells
A hormone that regulates blood sugar
A type of white blood cell responsible for digestion
Molecules on the surface of red blood cells that the immune system can recognize as foreign

quiz.q: Why is blood typing important before a transfusion is given?
options: Blood typing has no effect on the safety of a transfusion
Blood typing is only relevant for organ transplants, not transfusions
All blood types are always compatible with one another
To prevent an immune reaction caused by incompatible antigens

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Nanotechnology and Materials Science
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science Technology strand: nanotechnology involves manipulating matter at an extremely small scale, often at the level of individual atoms or molecules, to create materials with new or enhanced properties.

quiz.q: Nanotechnology involves manipulating matter at ___.
options: A scale only relevant to astronomical distances
A concept unrelated to materials science
A scale visible clearly to the naked eye with no magnification
An extremely small scale, often at the level of individual atoms or molecules

quiz.q: Materials engineered at the nanoscale can have properties that ___.
options: Are always identical to the same material at a larger scale
A concept unrelated to nanotechnology
Never change regardless of the scale being examined
Differ significantly from the same material at a larger scale

quiz.q: Which of these is a real-world application of nanotechnology?
options: A process that only applies to astronomical research
Coatings that make fabric resistant to stains and water
A technology that has never been applied outside of theory
An application unrelated to nanotechnology

quiz.q: Why might scientists be interested in developing new materials using nanotechnology?
options: Nanoscale materials can offer improved strength, conductivity, or other useful properties for various applications
This concept has no connection to materials science
Nanotechnology has no practical applications in any field
New materials developed through nanotechnology never offer any advantage

quiz.q: Why is precise control at the atomic or molecular level considered a defining feature of nanotechnology?
options: It allows scientists to engineer materials with specific, intentional properties not found in bulk materials
Precise control at this scale has no effect on a material’s properties
This concept has no relevance to nanotechnology
Materials can never be engineered with any intentional design at this scale

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: Vocal Delivery — Pace, Pitch, and Emphasis
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: effective vocal delivery uses pace, pitch, and emphasis to shape how an audience experiences a spoken message, since varying speaking rate, raising or lowering pitch, and stressing key words can communicate meaning that the words alone do not carry.

quiz.q: What three vocal elements does effective delivery typically vary?
options: Font size, colour, and margin width
Spelling, punctuation, and citation style
Pace, pitch, and emphasis
Word count, page number, and paragraph length

quiz.q: What can varying speaking pace communicate to an audience?
options: Only the exact time remaining in a speech
The speakers reading level
Nothing at all, since pace has no communicative value
A shift in urgency, importance, or emotional tone

quiz.q: Why might a speaker stress a particular word in a sentence?
options: To emphasize the most important idea in that sentence
Emphasis has no effect on how a listener interprets a sentence
Stressing a word always changes its dictionary spelling
Every word in a sentence must receive identical stress

quiz.q: What can a rise or fall in vocal pitch signal to a listener?
options: A question, a shift in emotion, or a change in emphasis
Nothing measurable at all
A change in the color of the speakers clothing
The exact number of pages in a written script

quiz.q: Why is vocal delivery considered part of oral communication skill, separate from word choice?
options: How something is said can shape meaning just as much as the words themselves
Word choice is the only element that ever affects meaning
Oral communication excludes any consideration of vocal delivery
Vocal delivery has no connection to how a message is understood

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Financial Literacy: Present Value and Future Value of Annuities
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: an annuity is a series of equal payments made at regular intervals, and its future value represents the total accumulated amount including interest, while its present value represents the equivalent lump sum today.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Financial Literacy: Present Value and Future Value of Annuities

quiz.q: What is an annuity in financial mathematics?
options: A type of insurance that covers only property damage
A single one-time payment with no future obligations
A loan that never requires repayment of any kind
A series of equal payments made at regular intervals over time

quiz.q: What does the future value of an annuity represent?
options: The exact number of payments made in a single year
The total accumulated value of all payments, including interest, at a future date
The value of a single payment made many years in the past
A value that ignores interest entirely

quiz.q: What does the present value of an annuity represent?
options: The total value of an annuity after every payment has stopped
A value that has no connection to future payments at all
The single lump-sum amount today that is equivalent to a series of future payments
The interest rate applied to a single payment only

quiz.q: Why does the future value of an annuity generally exceed the simple sum of its payments?
options: Because payments made later are always worth more than earlier ones with no interest involved
Because each payment earns interest over the time it remains invested
Because interest is never applied to any of the payments
Because the number of payments always decreases over time

quiz.q: Which financial product is a common real-world example of an annuity?
options: A single purchase made only once with no repeated payments
A textbook purchased for a single course
A retirement plan that pays a fixed amount at regular intervals
A coin collected as a one-time souvenir

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Innate Immunity -- The Body's First Line of Defense
subjects.summary: Students distinguish the body's innate, non-specific defences -- physical barriers, phagocytic cells, and the inflammatory response -- from the slower, targeted adaptive immune response, and explain why innate immunity acts first.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Biology: Innate Immunity -- The Body's First Line of Defense

quiz.q: Which of the following is an example of a physical barrier that is part of innate immunity?
options: Vaccination
Skin and mucous membranes
Memory T cells
Antibodies produced by B cells

quiz.q: Innate immunity is described as 'non-specific' because it:
options: Only activates after a second exposure to a pathogen
Responds in the same general way to a wide range of pathogens
Requires prior exposure to develop
Targets one particular pathogen only

quiz.q: During the inflammatory response, blood vessels near an injury site widen (vasodilation) mainly in order to:
options: Deliver more white blood cells and clotting factors to the site
Reduce blood flow to the area
Lower the local temperature
Prevent phagocytes from reaching the wound

quiz.q: Which cell type engulfs and digests invading pathogens as part of the innate immune response?
options: Memory cell
B lymphocyte
Plasma cell
Phagocyte (e.g., macrophage)

quiz.q: Compared to the adaptive immune response, the innate immune response:
options: Only occurs after vaccination
Acts within minutes to hours and does not require prior exposure
Produces long-lasting immunological memory
Is slower but highly specific to one pathogen

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Aerosols and Atmospheric Particulate Matter
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: atmospheric aerosols are tiny solid or liquid particles suspended in air, produced by both natural sources such as sea spray and human activities such as combustion, and fine particulate matter can scatter sunlight, seed cloud formation, and pose serious respiratory health risks.

quiz.q: What are atmospheric aerosols?
options: A single type of gas found only in laboratories
Large, visible chunks of solid rock
Tiny solid or liquid particles suspended in air
Pure gases with no solid or liquid particles present

quiz.q: Name one natural source of atmospheric aerosols.
options: Sea spray
Only synthetic laboratory chemicals
Only electronic devices
Only underground mining equipment

quiz.q: Name one human activity that produces atmospheric particulate matter.
options: Combustion
Photosynthesis in plants
Simple evaporation of pure water
Freezing of pure water into ice

quiz.q: What atmospheric effect can fine particulate matter have on sunlight and clouds?
options: It permanently blocks all sunlight from reaching the ground
It can scatter sunlight and seed cloud formation
It eliminates cloud formation entirely
It has no measurable effect on sunlight or clouds

quiz.q: What health risk is associated with fine particulate matter in the air?
options: No health risk of any kind to humans
A guaranteed cure for existing respiratory disease
Serious respiratory health risks
Improved lung function with prolonged exposure

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Reading: Analyzing In Medias Res and Narrative Beginnings
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Language strand: in medias res means beginning a narrative in the middle of the action rather than at the start of events, often followed later by a flashback that fills in the missing earlier background.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Reading: Analyzing In Medias Res and Narrative Beginnings

quiz.q: What does in medias res mean?
options: Ending a narrative before any action has occurred
Telling a story entirely through dialogue with no narration
Skipping the ending of a story entirely
Beginning a narrative in the middle of the action rather than at the start of events

quiz.q: What technique often supplies the missing earlier events after a story opens in medias res?
options: A table of contents listing every character
Flashback used to fill in earlier background information
A glossary placed at the end of the book
A footnote citing an unrelated source

quiz.q: Why might an author choose to open a story in medias res?
options: To immediately capture the readers attention with tension or action
To ensure the story has no identifiable setting
To make the story impossible for any reader to understand
To avoid including any characters in the story at all

quiz.q: A story that opens with a characters birth and proceeds strictly in chronological order is an example of what?
options: A story with no beginning at all
A classic example of in medias res
Not starting in medias res
A purely nonlinear narrative structure

quiz.q: What risk does an author take by opening a story in medias res?
options: The story can no longer contain any characters
Readers will always understand every detail immediately
Readers may feel confused until enough context is revealed
The story becomes impossible to write in any language

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Geometry: Graphing Sine and Cosine Functions (Amplitude and Period)
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: the graphs of sine and cosine functions are smooth, repeating waves whose amplitude describes their maximum height above the midline and whose period describes the horizontal length of one complete cycle.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Geometry: Graphing Sine and Cosine Functions (Amplitude and Period)

quiz.q: What does the amplitude of a sine or cosine graph describe?
options: The total horizontal length of the graph
The maximum height of the wave above (or below) its midline
The number of times the graph crosses the x-axis
The steepness of the graph at the origin only

quiz.q: What does the period of a sine or cosine function describe?
options: The number of amplitudes in a single wave
The y-intercept of the function
The horizontal length required to complete one full cycle of the wave
The maximum height reached by the graph

quiz.q: What is the period of the basic function y = sin(x), measured in radians?
options: 2 pi
Pi divided by two
4 pi
Pi

quiz.q: How does increasing the coefficient in front of sin(x) in y = a sin(x) affect the graph?
options: It shifts the entire graph horizontally
It increases the period, making the wave wider
It increases the amplitude, making the wave taller
It has no effect on the graph whatsoever

quiz.q: Why are sine and cosine graphs often described as periodic?
options: Their values never repeat under any circumstances
They only exist for negative input values
Their pattern of values repeats identically at regular horizontal intervals
They only produce a single output value for all inputs

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Antibody Structure and the Humoral Immune Response
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: antibodies are Y-shaped proteins produced by B cells that bind specifically to antigens on a pathogen, marking it for destruction, and this antibody-mediated defence is called the humoral immune response, distinct from the cell-mediated response carried out directly by T cells.

quiz.q: What shape are antibody proteins typically described as having?
options: Y-shaped
Perfectly spherical
Long and thread-like with no branching
Cube-shaped

quiz.q: What type of cell produces antibodies?
options: Skin cells
Muscle cells
B cells
Red blood cells

quiz.q: What do antibodies bind to specifically?
options: Nothing, since antibodies do not bind to anything
Antigens on a pathogen
Only molecules found in the persons own healthy tissue
Any random molecule in the bloodstream

quiz.q: What is the antibody-mediated immune defence called?
options: The purely mechanical immune response
The humoral immune response
The digestive immune response
The skeletal immune response

quiz.q: How does the humoral immune response differ from the cell-mediated response?
options: The cell-mediated response relies entirely on antibodies
The two responses are identical in every respect
The humoral response is carried out directly by T cells with no antibodies
The humoral response relies on antibodies, while the cell-mediated response is carried out directly by T cells

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Fire Retardant Chemistry and Flame-Resistant Materials
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: fire retardant chemicals slow or prevent combustion by interfering with the chemical chain reactions of burning, insulating a material from heat, or releasing water and non-flammable gases that dilute oxygen at the surface, and are applied to textiles, furniture, and building materials to improve fire safety.

quiz.q: What is the general purpose of a fire retardant chemical?
options: To slow or prevent combustion
To accelerate combustion as quickly as possible
To permanently change the colour of a material with no other effect
To eliminate all oxygen from the entire building

quiz.q: Name one mechanism by which fire retardants can slow combustion.
options: Increasing the amount of oxygen available at the surface
Removing all insulation from the material
Adding pure fuel directly to the flame
Interfering with the chemical chain reactions of burning

quiz.q: How can a fire retardant dilute oxygen at a materials surface during a fire?
options: By converting the material into a highly flammable gas
By releasing water and non-flammable gases
By removing all water from the surrounding environment
By releasing pure oxygen gas directly into the flame

quiz.q: Name one type of material fire retardants are commonly applied to.
options: Only liquids with no solid surface
Textiles
Only materials found exclusively underwater
Only substances that cannot burn under any circumstance

quiz.q: Why might a building code require fire retardant treatment on certain furniture?
options: To improve fire safety by slowing the spread of flames
Fire retardants have no connection to building fire safety
Fire retardant treatment always makes furniture more flammable
Building codes never address furniture materials

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The White Paper — Persuasive Technical Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a white paper presents a detailed, evidence-based argument about a technical, policy, or business problem, combining research and data with a clear recommendation, aimed at persuading an informed reader to adopt a particular solution.

quiz.q: What does a white paper typically present?
options: A short poem with no argument at all
A purely fictional narrative with invented characters
A detailed, evidence-based argument about a technical, policy, or business problem
A single-sentence advertising slogan

quiz.q: What combination does a white paper rely on to build its argument?
options: Random opinions with no supporting research
Images alone with no written analysis
Rhyme and meter with no supporting evidence
Research and data combined with a clear recommendation

quiz.q: Who is the typical intended reader of a white paper?
options: A reader who never makes any decisions
A young child with no background in the subject
An informed reader considering a technical, policy, or business decision
An audience expecting only entertainment

quiz.q: What is the persuasive goal of a white paper?
options: To entertain the reader with an invented story
To summarize unrelated topics with no central argument
To persuade the reader to adopt a particular solution or recommendation
To avoid taking any position on the problem discussed

quiz.q: How does a white paper typically differ from a purely narrative essay?
options: A white paper always uses rhymed verse throughout
It relies on technical evidence and a formal recommendation rather than storytelling
A white paper never includes any data or evidence
A white paper is defined by having no clear topic

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Trigonometry: Graphing the Tangent Function and Its Asymptotes
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: the graph of the tangent function repeats every pi radians and has vertical asymptotes wherever cosine equals zero, since tangent is defined as sine divided by cosine and becomes undefined at those points.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Trigonometry: Graphing the Tangent Function and Its Asymptotes

quiz.q: What is the period of the basic tangent function y = tan(x)?
options: Pi
Pi divided by two
4 pi
2 pi

quiz.q: Where do vertical asymptotes occur on the graph of y = tan(x)?
options: Wherever cosine of x equals zero
Wherever sine of x equals zero
At every integer value of x with no exceptions
Tangent graphs never contain any asymptotes

quiz.q: Why is the tangent function undefined at its asymptotes?
options: Tangent is undefined everywhere, not just at specific points
Because sine and cosine are always equal to each other at those points
Because tangent equals sine divided by cosine, and division by zero is undefined
Because tangent is defined only for negative angles

quiz.q: How does the graph of tangent differ visually from the graphs of sine and cosine?
options: Tangent has vertical asymptotes and an unbounded range, while sine and cosine are continuous and bounded between -1 and 1
Sine and cosine both have vertical asymptotes, unlike tangent
Tangent has a smaller period than both sine and cosine combined
Tangent, sine, and cosine all look exactly identical when graphed

quiz.q: What is the general shape of one branch of the tangent graph between two consecutive asymptotes?
options: A decreasing curve that never crosses the x-axis
An increasing curve that passes through zero and approaches positive and negative infinity at its edges
A closed loop that returns exactly to its starting point
A perfectly flat horizontal line with no curvature at all

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Bioindicator Species and Water Quality Assessment
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a bioindicator species is an organism whose presence, absence, or abundance reflects the health of its environment, and aquatic biologists often survey sensitive invertebrates in a stream to assess water quality without relying solely on chemical testing.

quiz.q: What is a bioindicator species?
options: A species that has no relationship to environmental conditions
An organism whose presence, absence, or abundance reflects the health of its environment
A species that only exists in fossil records
A species found only in laboratory settings

quiz.q: What might aquatic biologists survey in a stream to assess water quality?
options: Sensitive invertebrates
Only the temperature of the air above the stream
Only the width of the stream channel
Only the colour of the streambed rocks

quiz.q: Why are sensitive invertebrates useful as bioindicators of water quality?
options: Invertebrates never live in streams under any conditions
They have no sensitivity to pollution of any kind
Their presence or absence reflects pollution levels and habitat health over time
Their numbers are always constant regardless of water quality

quiz.q: What advantage does using a bioindicator species offer over chemical testing alone?
options: Chemical testing is always completely unnecessary once a bioindicator is found
Bioindicators can only be used in laboratory tanks, never in the field
Bioindicators provide no information that chemical testing cannot already provide
It can reflect the cumulative, long-term health of an ecosystem rather than a single moment in time

quiz.q: What might a sudden decline in a sensitive bioindicator species suggest about a stream?
options: No meaningful information about the stream at all
An increase in water temperature only, with no other implication
A decline in water quality or an increase in pollution
An improvement in water quality with no other cause needed

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Invisible Ink and Redox Indicators
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: many invisible inks rely on colourless organic compounds that become visible after a chemical change, such as an acid-base reaction revealed with an indicator or an oxidation reaction triggered by heat, illustrating how redox and acid-base chemistry can be used to hide and reveal a written message.

quiz.q: What property do many invisible ink compounds share before they are revealed?
options: They are metallic solids with no organic component
They glow permanently under any lighting condition
They are bright, highly visible pigments
They are colourless organic compounds

quiz.q: What can trigger an invisible ink message to become visible through oxidation?
options: Complete darkness with no light or heat applied
Freezing the paper solid
Submerging the paper in a vacuum
Heat

quiz.q: What type of chemical reaction can an indicator reveal in certain invisible inks?
options: A reaction with no chemical basis at all
A nuclear fission reaction
A purely physical change with no chemistry involved
An acid-base reaction

quiz.q: What does this use of invisible ink illustrate about redox and acid-base chemistry?
options: That these chemical changes can be used to hide and reveal a written message
That chemical reactions can never produce a visible colour change
That redox and acid-base chemistry have no practical applications
That invisible ink relies entirely on nuclear reactions

quiz.q: Why does heating certain invisible ink compounds reveal the hidden message?
options: Heat can trigger an oxidation reaction that produces a visible coloured compound
Heat has no chemical effect on the ink compound
Heat destroys the paper entirely, revealing nothing
Heat converts the ink into a completely different, unrelated substance

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: The Concrete Poem — Visual Form and Meaning
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a concrete poem arranges its words, letters, and spacing on the page so that the poems visual shape reinforces or embodies its subject, making the physical layout of the text an active part of the poems meaning rather than a neutral container for it.

quiz.q: What does a concrete poem arrange to reinforce its subject?
options: Only its title, with no attention to the body text
Its words, letters, and spacing on the page
Only its rhyme scheme, with no visual arrangement
Only its punctuation marks, arranged alphabetically

quiz.q: What role does the physical layout play in a concrete poem?
options: It is a neutral container with no effect on meaning
Layout has no relationship to a poems subject in any form
It becomes an active part of the poems meaning
Layout is chosen entirely at random by a printer

quiz.q: What might a concrete poem about a tree look like on the page?
options: It would always be printed as a plain, unbroken paragraph
It would contain no words related to trees at all
It would be identical in shape to every other poem
Its lines could be shaped to visually resemble a tree

quiz.q: Why might a poet choose the concrete poem form over a conventional stanza structure?
options: Visual shape can never add meaning to a poem
The visual shape can add a layer of meaning that words alone would not convey
Concrete poems are required to follow strict conventional stanzas
Conventional stanza structure is forbidden in all poetry

quiz.q: What makes a poem count as concrete rather than purely conventional?
options: It is defined solely by its length in lines
The visual arrangement of text is deliberately shaped to embody the subject
It is written entirely in a foreign language
It contains no visual arrangement of any kind

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Geometry: The Dot Product and the Angle Between Vectors
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the dot product of two vectors is found by multiplying corresponding components and summing the results, and it relates directly to the angle between the vectors, since a dot product of zero indicates that the two vectors are perpendicular.

quiz.q: How is the dot product of two vectors calculated?
options: By multiplying corresponding components and summing the results
By multiplying only the first components of each vector
By subtracting corresponding components and summing the results
By dividing one vector by the other component-wise

quiz.q: What does a dot product of zero indicate about two vectors?
options: The two vectors are perpendicular
The two vectors are identical in every component
One of the vectors must have zero magnitude
The two vectors point in exactly the same direction

quiz.q: What geometric quantity does the dot product help calculate between two vectors?
options: The number of dimensions in the coordinate system
The exact length of a completely unrelated third vector
The area of a circle with the same radius as one vector
The angle between the two vectors

quiz.q: What type of quantity does a dot product produce, a scalar or a vector?
options: A matrix of numbers
A vector with the same direction as the first input
A vector perpendicular to both input vectors
A scalar

quiz.q: How does the dot product differ from the cross product introduced earlier in the vectors strand?
options: The dot product is undefined for any pair of vectors
The dot product and the cross product always produce identical results
The cross product only applies to two-dimensional vectors
The dot product produces a scalar, while the cross product produces a vector perpendicular to both inputs

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Human Biology: Synaptic Transmission and Neurotransmitters
subjects.summary: Students follow a nerve signal across the synaptic cleft, from the release of neurotransmitter from the presynaptic axon terminal to receptor binding and signal termination on the postsynaptic cell.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Human Biology: Synaptic Transmission and Neurotransmitters

quiz.q: When an action potential reaches the axon terminal, it triggers the release of neurotransmitter from:
options: The postsynaptic membrane
Synaptic vesicles in the presynaptic neuron
The cell body of the receiving neuron
The myelin sheath

quiz.q: Neurotransmitter molecules cross the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the:
options: Nucleus of the sending neuron
Presynaptic membrane
Myelin sheath
Postsynaptic membrane

quiz.q: Which of the following correctly ends a signal at a synapse?
options: The axon terminal dissolving
Neurotransmitter accumulating permanently in the synaptic cleft
The postsynaptic neuron dividing
Neurotransmitter being broken down by enzymes or reabsorbed by the presynaptic neuron

quiz.q: Acetylcholine is an example of a:
options: Neurotransmitter
Structural protein
Enzyme cofactor
Hormone

quiz.q: An inhibitory neurotransmitter, when it binds its receptor, typically makes the postsynaptic neuron:
options: Release its own neurotransmitter in return
Less likely to fire an action potential
More likely to fire an action potential
Immediately die

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Science: Epigenetics: How Environment Affects Gene Expression
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Science strand: epigenetics studies how environmental factors, such as diet or stress, can influence whether certain genes are turned on or off, without changing the underlying DNA sequence.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Science: Epigenetics: How Environment Affects Gene Expression

quiz.q: What does epigenetics study?
options: How environmental factors influence whether genes are turned on or off
A concept unrelated to biology
How genes are physically removed from an organism
How DNA sequences are permanently rewritten

quiz.q: Name one environmental factor that might influence gene expression, such as diet.
options: A favourite colour
Diet
A random guess with no scientific basis
A concept unrelated to epigenetics

quiz.q: Does epigenetics involve changing the underlying DNA sequence itself?
options: No
Epigenetics has no connection to genes at all
A concept unrelated to epigenetics
Yes, it always changes the DNA sequence

quiz.q: Why might scientists be interested in how stress affects gene expression?
options: Gene expression is never affected by any outside factor
This concept has no relevance to science
Stress has no connection to gene expression
Understanding these effects could reveal connections between environment and health outcomes

quiz.q: Why is epigenetics considered a relatively new and evolving area of scientific study?
options: Gene expression was fully explained centuries ago
Epigenetics has already been completely understood with nothing left to discover
Scientists are still working to understand the full range of factors that can influence gene expression
This concept has no relevance to science

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: Fixed Forms, Revision, and Persuasive Voice
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: students revisit the sestina, fairy tale retellings, conditional sentences, climate fiction, political cartoons, vocal delivery, the palimpsest, the white paper, and the concrete poem.

quiz.q: What defines a sestina?
options: A poem written entirely in prose
A single rhymed couplet repeated indefinitely
A poem with no fixed length or repeated words
A fixed 39-line poem that repeats six end-words in a rotating pattern across six stanzas plus an envoi

quiz.q: What does a fairy tale retelling typically do to a familiar traditional story?
options: Converts the tale into a strictly factual historical record
Repeats the original story word for word with no changes
Removes every character from the original tale
Reworks its point of view, setting, or values

quiz.q: What does climate fiction typically imagine?
options: A world with no environmental concerns of any kind
Purely historical events with no connection to climate
Characters and societies confronting environmental change and its consequences
A setting entirely disconnected from any scientific concept

quiz.q: What does a political cartoon typically compress into a single frame?
options: A detailed scientific diagram with no commentary
Commentary on a public issue using symbolic imagery and caricature
A complete, unabridged transcript of a news broadcast
A purely decorative image with no argument at all

quiz.q: What does a concrete poem arrange to reinforce its subject?
options: Only its title, with no attention to the body text
Only its punctuation marks, arranged alphabetically
Its words, letters, and spacing on the page
Only its rhyme scheme, with no visual arrangement

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Probability: An Introduction to Geometric Probability
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: geometric probability calculates the likelihood of an outcome using the ratio of a favourable area, length, or region to the total possible area, length, or region, rather than counting individual discrete outcomes.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Probability: An Introduction to Geometric Probability

quiz.q: What does geometric probability compare?
options: The exact number of coins flipped in an experiment
The colour of a randomly chosen shape
The ratio of a favourable area, length, or region to the total possible area, length, or region
The number of dice rolled in a single game

quiz.q: How does geometric probability differ from counting discrete outcomes, such as rolling a die?
options: It can only be used with a standard six-sided die
It always produces a probability greater than one
It uses continuous measurements like area or length instead of counting separate outcomes
It never involves any kind of ratio

quiz.q: Which situation could be modeled using geometric probability?
options: The chance that a randomly thrown dart lands within a specific region of a target
The chance of drawing a specific card from a deck
The chance of flipping heads on a single coin
The chance of rolling a six on a single die

quiz.q: In geometric probability, what happens to the calculated probability if the favourable region takes up half of the total region?
options: The probability is one half
The probability cannot be calculated
The probability is always zero
The probability is always one
