quiz.q: Why is geometric probability useful in situations that counting alone cannot easily solve?
options: It removes the need to ever calculate a ratio
It cannot be applied to any real-world situation
It only applies to situations involving whole numbers
It allows probability to be calculated for continuous outcomes, such as a location within an area, rather than only separate, countable outcomes

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology Review: Gene Transfer, Development, and Immunity
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: students revisit horizontal gene transfer, seed dormancy, cell signaling, ecological niches, ABO and Rh blood types, embryonic development, antibody structure, bioindicator species, and prions.

quiz.q: What is horizontal gene transfer?
options: The complete destruction of genetic material within a cell
A process that never occurs in bacteria
The movement of genetic material between organisms of the same generation, rather than from parent to offspring
The transfer of genetic material only from parent to offspring

quiz.q: What is a ligand in the context of cell signaling?
options: A type of carbohydrate stored for energy
A signaling molecule that binds to a specific receptor
A structural protein found only in the cell wall
An enzyme that breaks down DNA exclusively

quiz.q: What does a species ecological niche describe?
options: Only the geographic location where a species was first discovered
Only the physical size of an individual organism
Its full role in an ecosystem, including the resources it uses and conditions it tolerates
The exact number of offspring a species produces each year

quiz.q: What happens during cleavage in early embryonic development?
options: Rapid cell division partitions the fertilized egg into many smaller cells
The embryo stops dividing entirely for an extended period
Specialized organs form immediately without any cell division
The fertilized egg is destroyed and replaced

quiz.q: What is a prion made of?
options: A carbohydrate molecule with no protein at all
A complete virus particle with RNA
Misfolded protein, with no genetic material of its own
DNA exclusively, with no protein component

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Science: The Physics of Superconductors
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Science strand: a superconductor is a material that can conduct electricity with zero resistance when cooled to extremely low temperatures, allowing electric current to flow without losing energy.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Science: The Physics of Superconductors

quiz.q: What is a superconductor?
options: A concept unrelated to physics
A material that conducts electricity with zero resistance at low temperatures
A material that only works at very high temperatures
A material that always blocks electricity completely

quiz.q: Does a superconductor need to be cooled to extremely low temperatures to work?
options: Temperature has no connection to superconductivity
Yes
No, superconductors work best at room temperature only
A concept unrelated to superconductors

quiz.q: Does electric current flow through a superconductor without losing energy?
options: Superconductors never actually conduct any electricity
A concept unrelated to superconductors
Yes
No, superconductors always lose a large amount of energy

quiz.q: Why might superconductors be useful for technologies like maglev trains?
options: Maglev trains never use any superconducting technology
They can create powerful magnetic fields efficiently, without energy loss from resistance
Superconductors have no connection to magnetic technology
This concept has no relevance to science

quiz.q: Why is the requirement for extremely low temperatures a current challenge for using superconductors widely?
options: Cooling materials to such low temperatures can be expensive and difficult to maintain
Cooling has no connection to how superconductors are used
This concept has no relevance to physics
Superconductors work at any temperature with no special cooling needed

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Emphatic and Cleft Sentences
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Language strand: an emphatic sentence uses structures such as the auxiliary verb do to stress a point, while a cleft sentence divides a single idea into two clauses, often beginning with it or what, to highlight one particular piece of information.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Grammar: Emphatic and Cleft Sentences

quiz.q: What is the purpose of an emphatic sentence?
options: To remove all emphasis from every part of a sentence
To stress or emphasize a particular point, often using an auxiliary verb such as do
To combine two unrelated ideas with no connection at all
To eliminate the need for a main verb in a sentence

quiz.q: Which sentence is an example of emphatic structure using the auxiliary verb do?
options: Finishing my homework, I ate dinner.
I finished my homework before dinner.
I did finish my homework before dinner.
Homework, I finished, before dinner.

quiz.q: What is a cleft sentence?
options: A sentence divided into two clauses, often beginning with it or what, to highlight a specific piece of information
A sentence that contains no verbs of any kind
A type of sentence found only in poetry, never in prose
A sentence that must always begin with a question word

quiz.q: Which sentence is an example of a cleft sentence?
options: It was Maria who solved the difficult problem.
The difficult problem was solved.
Maria solved the difficult problem.
Solving the difficult problem, Maria smiled.

quiz.q: Why might a writer choose a cleft sentence structure instead of a simple, direct sentence?
options: To draw special attention to one particular piece of information within the sentence
Cleft sentences are grammatically incorrect in every context
Cleft sentences always make a sentence less clear to the reader
A cleft sentence removes the subject from a sentence entirely

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: Related Rates Problems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a related rates problem uses the chain rule to connect the rates of change of two or more quantities that are linked by an equation, letting you find how fast one quantity is changing at a given instant from the known rate of change of another.

quiz.q: What technique do related rates problems rely on to connect changing quantities?
options: The quadratic formula
The chain rule
The Pythagorean Theorem alone with no calculus
A method that ignores any equation linking the quantities

quiz.q: What must two or more quantities in a related rates problem share?
options: A shared unit of measurement and nothing else
Identical numerical values at every instant
An equation that links them together
No relationship of any kind

quiz.q: What can a related rates problem let you find once one rate is known?
options: How fast a linked quantity is changing at a given instant
The total distance traveled over an entire day
The colour of the object being measured
The exact value of a completely unrelated constant

quiz.q: Why is differentiating both sides of an equation with respect to time useful in a related rates problem?
options: Differentiating with respect to time has no effect on the equation
It removes all variables from the equation entirely
It reveals how the rates of change of the linked quantities are related to each other
It changes the equation into an unrelated geometric formula

quiz.q: Which of these is a classic example of a related rates problem?
options: Finding the average of a list of unrelated numbers
Finding the total surface area of a fixed, unchanging cube
Finding how fast the radius of a balloon changes as it is inflated at a known rate
Finding the exact colour of a balloon

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Wetland Ecosystems and Ecosystem Services
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: wetlands are ecosystems saturated with water for at least part of the year, and they provide critical ecosystem services such as filtering pollutants, storing floodwater, and supporting high levels of biodiversity, making them among the most productive habitats on Earth.

quiz.q: What defines a wetland ecosystem?
options: An ecosystem that never contains any water at all
An ecosystem found only at extremely high altitudes
An ecosystem defined solely by its average temperature
An ecosystem saturated with water for at least part of the year

quiz.q: Name one ecosystem service wetlands provide.
options: Eliminating biodiversity from the surrounding region
Producing large amounts of desert sand
Filtering pollutants from water
Preventing all plant growth in the area

quiz.q: How do wetlands help reduce flood damage?
options: By evaporating all rainfall before it can accumulate
By storing floodwater and slowing its release
By having no effect on water flow whatsoever
By immediately releasing all stored water at once

quiz.q: Why are wetlands considered among the most productive habitats on Earth?
options: They are always larger in area than any other habitat type
They support unusually high levels of biodiversity relative to their area
Productivity has no relationship to biodiversity in a wetland
They support no living organisms of any kind

quiz.q: What might happen to nearby communities if a wetland is drained or destroyed?
options: Increased flood risk and reduced natural water filtration
An automatic improvement in local water quality
Guaranteed protection from all future flooding
No change of any kind to surrounding water systems

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Electronegativity and Bond Polarity
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: electronegativity measures how strongly an atom attracts shared electrons in a covalent bond, and a large difference in electronegativity between two bonded atoms produces a polar bond with partial positive and negative charges, while a small difference produces a nonpolar bond.

quiz.q: What does electronegativity measure?
options: How strongly an atom attracts shared electrons in a covalent bond
The exact number of neutrons in an atom
The colour an element appears in visible light
The total mass of an atoms nucleus

quiz.q: What forms when there is a large electronegativity difference between two bonded atoms?
options: A bond with no charge distribution of any kind
A purely metallic bond with free-flowing electrons
A bond that instantly breaks apart
A polar bond with partial positive and negative charges

quiz.q: What kind of bond forms when two bonded atoms have similar electronegativity?
options: An extremely polar ionic bond
A bond with no shared electrons at all
A bond that cannot exist under any conditions
A nonpolar bond

quiz.q: What do the partial charges in a polar bond represent?
options: A complete transfer of an entire electron from one atom to the other
An uneven sharing of electron density between the two atoms
An equal sharing of electron density with no imbalance
A charge that has no connection to electron distribution

quiz.q: Why is electronegativity difference useful for predicting a bonds character?
options: It determines the physical colour of a compound exclusively
It indicates whether electrons are shared evenly or pulled toward one atom
It only applies to bonds between identical atoms
It has no relationship to how electrons are shared in a bond

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Elliptical Constructions and Implied Words
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Language strand: an elliptical construction omits a word or phrase that can be clearly understood from context, allowing a sentence to avoid needless repetition while still remaining fully comprehensible to the reader.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Grammar: Elliptical Constructions and Implied Words

quiz.q: What is an elliptical construction?
options: A sentence that repeats the same word or phrase multiple times for emphasis
A sentence structure in which a word or phrase is omitted because it can be understood from context
A grammatical rule that forbids the omission of any word under any circumstances
A punctuation mark used only to separate two independent clauses

quiz.q: Why do writers use elliptical constructions?
options: Because every sentence in formal writing must contain an omission
To avoid needless repetition while keeping the sentence clear
To make a sentence as repetitive and confusing as possible
To remove all verbs from a sentence entirely

quiz.q: Which sentence contains an elliptical construction?
options: Maria studied French, and Carlos studied Spanish, and both enjoyed it.
Maria and Carlos both studied French together every day.
Maria studied French, and Carlos, Spanish.
Maria studied French. Carlos studied Spanish. Both enjoyed it.

quiz.q: What must be true for an omitted word in an elliptical construction to be acceptable?
options: The omitted word must always be a noun and nothing else
The omitted word must never appear anywhere else in the sentence
The omitted word must be replaced with a comma in every case
The omitted word must be clearly recoverable from the surrounding context

quiz.q: How does an elliptical construction differ from an incomplete sentence fragment?
options: An elliptical construction omits words that are still understood by the reader, while a fragment leaves a sentence incomplete and unclear
A fragment always contains more information than an elliptical construction
Elliptical constructions are never grammatically acceptable in any context
An elliptical construction and a sentence fragment are exactly the same thing

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: Concavity, Inflection Points, and the Second Derivative
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the second derivative of a function reveals its concavity, with a positive second derivative indicating the graph curves upward and a negative second derivative indicating it curves downward, and an inflection point marks where concavity switches from one to the other.

quiz.q: What does the second derivative of a function reveal?
options: The colour of the functions graph
Its concavity
The total number of terms in the function
The exact y-intercept of the function

quiz.q: What does a positive second derivative indicate about a graph?
options: The graph has no defined shape at all
The graph is a perfectly straight line
The graph curves upward
The graph curves downward

quiz.q: What does a negative second derivative indicate about a graph?
options: The graph curves upward
The graph repeats itself infinitely
The graph has no second derivative at all
The graph curves downward

quiz.q: What is an inflection point?
options: The single highest point on the entire graph
A point where the graph crosses the y-axis exclusively
A point where concavity switches from upward to downward or downward to upward
A point where the function is undefined in every case

quiz.q: Why is concavity useful information beyond just knowing where a function increases or decreases?
options: Concavity only applies to functions with no derivative
It describes how the rate of change itself is changing, revealing the shape of the curve
Concavity provides no additional information about a functions shape
Concavity replaces the need to know where a function increases or decreases

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Restriction Enzymes and Recombinant DNA Technology
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: restriction enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sequences, allowing scientists to splice a gene of interest into a plasmid vector and insert the resulting recombinant DNA into a host cell, a foundational technique behind much of modern genetic engineering.

quiz.q: What do restriction enzymes do to DNA?
options: Convert DNA directly into a protein with no intermediate steps
Permanently destroy all DNA they contact
Cut it at specific recognition sequences
Have no effect on DNA of any kind

quiz.q: What is a plasmid vector used for in recombinant DNA technology?
options: Measuring the exact temperature of a reaction
Destroying a host cells entire genome
Producing energy for the host cell exclusively
Carrying a gene of interest into a host cell

quiz.q: What is recombinant DNA?
options: DNA with no genetic information of any kind
DNA that has never been altered in any way
DNA formed by combining genetic material from different sources
A type of DNA found only in viruses

quiz.q: Why are restriction enzymes considered a foundational tool of genetic engineering?
options: They function identically to antibodies in the immune system
They allow precise cutting and splicing of DNA at known sequences
They have no practical application in genetic engineering
They can only be used to destroy DNA, never to modify it usefully

quiz.q: What must happen to a gene of interest before it can be inserted into a host cell using this technique?
options: It must first be converted into a completely different gene
Nothing, since genes can be inserted with no preparation at all
It must be removed from all cellular contexts permanently
It must be spliced into a vector such as a plasmid

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Dyes and Pigments — Azo Compounds and Colour Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: azo compounds contain a nitrogen-nitrogen double bond linking two aromatic rings, and this extended conjugated system absorbs specific wavelengths of visible light, making azo compounds one of the most widely used classes of synthetic dye in textiles and food colouring.

quiz.q: What functional group defines an azo compound?
options: A single carbon-hydrogen bond with no nitrogen present
A nitrogen-nitrogen double bond linking two aromatic rings
A bond found only in noble gases
A pure metal-metal bond

quiz.q: What structural feature of azo compounds allows them to absorb visible light?
options: Their extremely small overall molecular size
Their extended conjugated system
A rigid, non-conjugated single bond structure
Their complete lack of any bonding electrons

quiz.q: What common application are azo compounds widely used for?
options: Producing pure oxygen gas
Insulating electrical wiring
Synthetic dyes in textiles and food colouring
Building structural steel beams

quiz.q: Why does the conjugated system in an azo dye affect the colour observed?
options: It determines which wavelengths of visible light are absorbed
It only affects the compounds melting point, never its colour
It converts the compound into a colourless gas
Conjugation has no relationship to colour in any compound

quiz.q: What links the two aromatic rings in a typical azo compound?
options: A nitrogen-nitrogen double bond
A chain of carbon atoms with no nitrogen at all
A metallic bridge between the two rings
A single oxygen atom with no other bonds

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Correlative Conjunctions and Balanced Sentence Structure
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: correlative conjunctions such as either-or, neither-nor, and not only-but also work in pairs to link balanced grammatical elements, and keeping the paired elements parallel in structure gives a sentence rhythm and clarity that a single conjunction cannot achieve alone.

quiz.q: What is distinctive about correlative conjunctions?
options: They can only be used at the very start of a paragraph
They work in pairs to link balanced grammatical elements
They never appear more than once in an entire essay
They eliminate the need for any punctuation whatsoever

quiz.q: Give an example of a correlative conjunction pair.
options: Either and or
Red and blue
Before and after, used only as prepositions
Quickly and slowly

quiz.q: What must the elements joined by a correlative conjunction pair maintain?
options: Parallel grammatical structure
No grammatical relationship at all
Identical spelling in every joined word
Completely different grammatical structures

quiz.q: What effect can correctly balanced correlative conjunctions have on a sentence?
options: They always make a sentence harder to understand
They are grammatically forbidden in formal writing
They give the sentence rhythm and clarity
They remove all meaning from a sentence

quiz.q: What might happen if the two elements joined by a correlative conjunction pair are not grammatically parallel?
options: The sentence becomes impossible to punctuate
The sentence can sound awkward or unbalanced
Nothing changes, since parallel structure is never required
The sentence automatically becomes more sophisticated

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: Implicit Differentiation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: implicit differentiation finds the derivative of a relation in which y is not isolated on one side of the equation, by differentiating both sides with respect to x and applying the chain rule whenever a term involving y appears.

quiz.q: When is implicit differentiation needed?
options: When y is not isolated on one side of an equation
Only when a function has no variables at all
Only when an equation contains no y term whatsoever
When a function is already fully solved for y

quiz.q: What rule must be applied whenever a term involving y is differentiated with respect to x?
options: The chain rule
No rule is needed when differentiating a term involving y
The Pythagorean Theorem
A rule that applies only to constants

quiz.q: What does implicit differentiation ultimately find?
options: The exact numerical value of x only
The area enclosed by a curve
The derivative of a relation between x and y
The colour of a graphed curve

quiz.q: Why cannot every equation involving x and y be solved for y before differentiating?
options: Some relations cannot be rearranged into a simple function of x alone
Implicit differentiation is only used when y does not exist
Solving for y is never possible under any circumstance
Every equation can always be solved for y with no difficulty

quiz.q: What is a classic example of a curve that requires implicit differentiation?
options: A circle defined by x squared plus y squared equals a constant
A function with no y term present anywhere
A straight horizontal line with a constant y-value
A single point plotted with no equation at all

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Gel Electrophoresis and DNA Fingerprinting
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments by size as an electric current pulls negatively charged DNA through a porous gel, with smaller fragments migrating farther, producing a banding pattern unique enough to individuals to be used in DNA fingerprinting.

quiz.q: What property of DNA fragments does gel electrophoresis separate by?
options: Colour
Taste
Size
Exact age of the sample

quiz.q: What pulls DNA fragments through the gel during electrophoresis?
options: A stream of pressurized air
Gravity alone, with no external force applied
An electric current
A strong magnetic field with no electric current

quiz.q: Which fragments migrate farther through the gel, smaller or larger ones?
options: Smaller fragments
Both migrate an identical distance in every case
Neither size of fragment ever migrates at all
Larger fragments

quiz.q: What does gel electrophoresis produce that can be used to identify an individual?
options: A unique banding pattern
A permanent chemical bond between all samples tested
A single unchanging colour with no pattern
An audible sound unique to each sample

quiz.q: Why is DNA able to migrate through a gel under an electric current?
options: DNA has no ability to move under an electric current
DNA is positively charged and repelled by both electrodes
DNA carries no charge and is pushed by air pressure instead
DNA is negatively charged and moves toward the positive electrode

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Science: Vaccines and Immunology
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science strand: immunology studies how the immune system protects the body from pathogens, and vaccines work by training the immune system to recognize specific pathogens before an actual infection occurs.

quiz.q: What does immunology study?
options: A concept unrelated to biology
How plants convert sunlight into food
How rocks form over long periods of time
How the immune system protects the body from pathogens

quiz.q: What do vaccines train the immune system to recognize?
options: Specific pathogens
A concept unrelated to vaccines
Nothing at all related to disease
Only harmless substances with no medical purpose

quiz.q: Do vaccines typically work by preparing the immune system before an actual infection occurs?
options: No, vaccines only work after a person is already infected
A concept unrelated to vaccines
Timing has no connection to how vaccines work
Yes

quiz.q: Why might a vaccine include a small, harmless piece of a pathogen rather than a full, dangerous version?
options: This concept has no connection to immunology
Vaccines always include the full, dangerous version of a pathogen
It allows the immune system to learn and build a defense safely, without causing the actual illness
A harmless piece of a pathogen provides no useful immune response

quiz.q: Why is widespread vaccination in a community sometimes linked to protecting people through herd immunity?
options: Vaccinating a community never has any effect on how a disease spreads
This concept has no relevance to science
Herd immunity has no connection to vaccination at all
When enough people are immune, a disease has a harder time spreading, protecting those who cannot be vaccinated

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Drama: The Soliloquy and Interior Thought on Stage
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a soliloquy is a dramatic speech in which a character alone on stage speaks their private thoughts aloud, giving the audience direct access to motives, doubts, or plans that other characters in the play cannot hear.

quiz.q: What is a soliloquy?
options: A conversation between two characters with no audience present
A stage direction printed only in the margins of a script
A song performed by an entire chorus of characters
A dramatic speech in which a character alone on stage speaks private thoughts aloud

quiz.q: Who can hear the words of a true soliloquy within the world of the play?
options: Every character on stage at that moment
Only the playwright, never the audience
No other character, only the audience
A single silent character standing offstage

quiz.q: What does a soliloquy give the audience direct access to?
options: A list of props used later in the play
The exact date the play was first performed
The names of every actor in the cast
A characters motives, doubts, or plans

quiz.q: Why might a playwright use a soliloquy rather than dialogue to reveal a characters plan?
options: It lets the audience understand private thoughts no other character could realistically hear
A soliloquy must always be spoken by more than one character
Soliloquies are required to contain no meaningful information
Dialogue is always a more private form of speech than a soliloquy

quiz.q: What must be true of a characters position on stage for a speech to count as a soliloquy?
options: The character must be surrounded by the entire cast
The character must be reading directly from a printed script
The character must be alone, with no other characters present to hear
The character must be offstage and unseen by the audience

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Statistics: An Introduction to Percentiles and Quartiles
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: a percentile indicates the percentage of data values in a set that fall below a given value, and quartiles divide an ordered data set into four equal parts, with the second quartile equal to the median.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Statistics: An Introduction to Percentiles and Quartiles

quiz.q: What does a percentile indicate?
options: The percentage of data values in a set that fall below a given value
The exact number of data points in a set
The largest value in a data set
The colour used in a graph of the data

quiz.q: How many equal parts do quartiles divide an ordered data set into?
options: Two
One hundred
Four
Ten

quiz.q: Which quartile is equal to the median of a data set?
options: The second quartile
The first quartile
The fourth quartile
The third quartile

quiz.q: If a students test score is at the 90th percentile, what does that mean?
options: The student is ninety years old
The student scored in the bottom ten percent of the class
The student answered exactly ninety percent of the questions correctly
The students score is higher than about ninety percent of other scores in the set

quiz.q: Why are percentiles and quartiles useful for interpreting a large data set?
options: They can only be used with data sets smaller than ten values
They eliminate the need to ever collect data
They summarize how a specific value compares to the overall spread of the data
They always describe exactly the same information as the mean

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Evolution: Phylogenetics and the Construction of Cladograms
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: phylogenetics reconstructs the evolutionary relationships among species based on shared characteristics, and a cladogram is a branching diagram that represents these relationships, with each branch point marking a common ancestor shared by all species descending from it.

quiz.q: What does phylogenetics reconstruct?
options: A list of every mutation in a single genome
The evolutionary relationships among species
The precise geographic coordinates of a species habitat
The exact diet of a single individual organism

quiz.q: What is a cladogram?
options: A branching diagram representing evolutionary relationships among species
A map showing only modern political borders
A photograph of a single fossil specimen
A table listing the average weight of several species

quiz.q: What does each branch point on a cladogram represent?
options: A point with no biological significance at all
The exact birth date of an individual organism
A location where a species went permanently extinct
A common ancestor shared by all descending species

quiz.q: What kind of evidence is used to build a cladogram?
options: The alphabetical order of species names
Random guesses with no supporting evidence
Shared characteristics among species
Only the colour of each species fur or scales

quiz.q: Why might two species appear close together on a cladogram?
options: They share a more recent common ancestor than species placed farther apart
They live in the exact same city or town
They were both discovered in the same calendar year
Placement on a cladogram is entirely random

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Bleach and Oxidizing Household Cleaners
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: household bleach works as an oxidizing agent, breaking apart the conjugated pigment molecules responsible for stains and killing microorganisms by disrupting proteins and cell membranes through the same oxidation reactions that give bleach its cleaning and disinfecting power.

quiz.q: What type of chemical agent is household bleach?
options: An oxidizing agent
A completely inert substance with no reactivity
A reducing agent with no oxidizing ability
A pure acid with no oxidizing properties

quiz.q: How does bleach remove stains at the molecular level?
options: By breaking apart the conjugated pigment molecules responsible for the stain colour
By adding new pigment molecules to the fabric
By dissolving the fabric itself completely
By physically scrubbing the stain away with no chemical reaction

quiz.q: How does bleach act as a disinfectant?
options: By disrupting proteins and cell membranes through oxidation
By providing nutrients that microorganisms need to thrive
By freezing microorganisms at room temperature
By having no effect on microorganisms whatsoever

quiz.q: What single type of reaction explains both bleachs stain removal and disinfecting action?
options: Oxidation reactions
Photosynthesis reactions
Nuclear fission reactions
Simple physical dissolution with no chemical change

quiz.q: Why might mixing bleach with certain other cleaning products be dangerous?
options: Mixing bleach with other cleaners always makes cleaning safer
Bleach cannot react with any other household chemical
Mixing chemicals always eliminates any safety risk
Reactions between bleach and other chemicals can release hazardous gases

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Satirical News and the Line Between Parody and Misinformation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: satirical news outlets use exaggeration and irony to mock real events for comic or critical effect, but when a satirical headline is shared without its original context, readers may mistake parody for genuine reporting, raising questions about how a text signals its own satirical intent.

quiz.q: What technique do satirical news outlets rely on to mock real events?
options: Random, unrelated numerical data
Exaggeration and irony
Strict, unembellished factual reporting only
Complete silence on any current event

quiz.q: What can happen when a satirical headline is shared without its original context?
options: Nothing changes, since context never affects interpretation
The headline automatically becomes illegal to share
Readers may mistake the parody for genuine reporting
Readers always immediately recognize it as satire

quiz.q: What question does the spread of decontextualized satire raise for media literacy?
options: Whether satire has ever existed as a literary form
How a text signals its own satirical intent
Whether satire should be banned from all media entirely
Whether headlines should always be exactly one word long

quiz.q: Why might a satirical article be mistaken for real news?
options: Real news and satire are always printed in different fonts
Its exaggeration may not be obvious once removed from its original satirical source
Satirical articles always include a disclaimer in every possible context
Readers can never be confused by any form of media

quiz.q: What purpose does satirical news typically serve beyond humour?
options: Providing only entertainment with no commentary of any kind
Replacing the need for factual news entirely
Avoiding any connection to real-world events
Offering comic or critical commentary on real events

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Sequences and Series: Recursive versus Explicit Formulas
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Math strand: a recursive formula defines each term of a sequence in relation to one or more previous terms, while an explicit formula calculates any term directly using its position in the sequence, offering two different but related ways to describe the same pattern.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Sequences and Series: Recursive versus Explicit Formulas

quiz.q: What does a recursive formula use to define a term in a sequence?
options: One or more previous terms in the sequence
Only the position number of the term, with no reference to any other term
A recursive formula never refers to any other term in the sequence
The final term of the sequence only

quiz.q: What does an explicit formula allow you to calculate directly?
options: Only the very first term of a sequence
The sum of every term in an infinite sequence only
Any term in a sequence, using its position number
An explicit formula cannot be used to calculate any term directly

quiz.q: What is a disadvantage of using a recursive formula to find a term far along in a sequence?
options: It typically requires calculating every preceding term first, which can be time-consuming
A recursive formula always calculates a distant term instantly with no prior terms needed
There is no disadvantage to using a recursive formula for any term
Recursive formulas can only be used to find the first term of a sequence

quiz.q: Which type of formula would be more efficient for finding the 100th term of a sequence directly?
options: Both formulas require exactly the same amount of calculation in every case
Neither type of formula can be used to find a specific term
A recursive formula
An explicit formula

quiz.q: How do recursive and explicit formulas relate to each other when describing the same sequence?
options: Explicit and recursive formulas never produce the same set of terms
Recursive and explicit formulas always describe two completely unrelated sequences
They can describe the same underlying pattern using two different approaches, one based on previous terms and one based on position
A sequence can only ever be described using a recursive formula

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biochemistry: Cellular Respiration and ATP Production
subjects.summary: Students trace the three main stages of aerobic cellular respiration -- glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain -- and see how each stage contributes to the overall production of ATP.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Biochemistry: Cellular Respiration and ATP Production

quiz.q: Where in the cell does glycolysis take place?
options: Inner mitochondrial membrane
Mitochondrial matrix
Nucleus
Cytoplasm (cytosol)

quiz.q: The electron transport chain is located in the:
options: Inner mitochondrial membrane
Nucleus
Cytoplasm
Golgi apparatus

quiz.q: Which stage of cellular respiration produces the most ATP molecules?
options: The Krebs cycle
Glycolysis
The electron transport chain
Fermentation

quiz.q: In the electron transport chain, oxygen serves as the:
options: Source of carbon for glucose
Initial electron donor
Enzyme that starts glycolysis
Final electron acceptor, combining with electrons and H+ to form water

quiz.q: If oxygen is unavailable, a cell can no longer complete which stage of aerobic respiration?
options: The electron transport chain
Neither stage is affected
Glycolysis only
Only the Krebs cycle continues normally

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Thiols and the Chemistry of Skunk Spray
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: thiols are organic compounds containing a sulfur-hydrogen functional group, and their sulfur atoms give many thiols an intensely unpleasant odour detectable by the human nose at extremely low concentrations, which is why the thiol-based compounds in skunk spray are so difficult to remove.

quiz.q: What functional group defines a thiol?
options: A sulfur-hydrogen group
A pure carbon-carbon triple bond
A group containing only hydrogen and oxygen
A nitrogen-oxygen double bond

quiz.q: What property of many thiols makes them so noticeable to the human nose?
options: A complete lack of any odour whatsoever
An intensely unpleasant odour detectable at extremely low concentrations
A pleasant, sweet fragrance detectable only at high concentrations
An odour that only animals, never humans, can detect

quiz.q: What element gives thiols their characteristic strong odour?
options: Sodium
Helium
Calcium
Sulfur

quiz.q: Why is skunk spray so difficult to eliminate once it contacts skin or fabric?
options: Skunk spray evaporates completely within a few seconds
Skunk spray contains no chemical compounds capable of producing an odour
Its thiol-based compounds are detectable by smell at extremely low concentrations
Thiols are always odourless once exposed to air

quiz.q: What type of compound, based on its functional group, is responsible for skunk spray odour?
options: A noble gas
A pure metal
A thiol
An ionic salt with no organic component

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: Nonverbal Communication and Body Language in Presentations
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: nonverbal communication, including posture, gesture, eye contact, and facial expression, shapes how an audience receives a spoken message just as much as the words themselves, and a speaker whose body language contradicts their words can undermine the credibility of an otherwise strong presentation.

quiz.q: Name one element of nonverbal communication in a presentation.
options: The exact word count of the speech
Eye contact
The font used on any accompanying slides
The publication date of the source material

quiz.q: How much can nonverbal communication shape an audiences reception of a message?
options: Only slightly less than the colour of the speakers shoes
Nonverbal communication has no effect on how a message is received
As much as the words themselves
Nonverbal communication can only ever weaken a message

quiz.q: What can happen if a speakers body language contradicts their spoken words?
options: It can undermine the credibility of the presentation
It always makes the presentation more persuasive
It automatically improves the audiences understanding
It has no effect on how the audience perceives the speaker

quiz.q: Why might a speaker practice maintaining eye contact during a presentation?
options: To build a stronger connection with and credibility with the audience
Maintaining eye contact is forbidden in formal presentations
Eye contact always distracts an audience from the message
Eye contact has no relationship to audience connection

quiz.q: What kind of signal does posture send to an audience during a speech?
options: A nonverbal signal about the speakers confidence and engagement
A signal that only affects the speakers own hearing
No signal of any kind, since posture is irrelevant to communication
A signal about the exact temperature of the room

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Math Review: Probability, Number Theory, and Statistics (Days 171-179)
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand review: students revisit skewness and distribution shape, triangular numbers, the isoperimetric problem, synthetic division, and the Birthday Paradox.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Math Review: Probability, Number Theory, and Statistics (Days 171-179)

quiz.q: What does skewness describe about a data distribution?
options: Its asymmetry, or how unevenly the data is spread
The colour used to display a graph
The units used to measure the data
The exact number of data points collected

quiz.q: What is a triangular number?
options: A number that is always divisible by three
A number that can only be an even number
A number with exactly three digits
A number formed by summing consecutive whole numbers starting from one

quiz.q: What does the isoperimetric problem ask?
options: How to convert a shape into a straight line
How to calculate the volume of a sphere
Which shape encloses the greatest area for a given perimeter
Which shape has the smallest possible perimeter for any area

quiz.q: What does synthetic division provide a shortcut for?
options: Dividing a polynomial by a linear expression
Multiplying two polynomials together
Finding the square root of a number
Graphing a quadratic function

quiz.q: What does the Birthday Paradox describe?
options: A proof that no two people can share a birthday
A surprisingly high probability that two people in a group share a birthday
A rule for calculating everyones exact birthday
A method for predicting future birthdays

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Physiology: Muscle Contraction and the Sliding Filament Theory
subjects.summary: Students learn the sliding filament theory of muscle contraction, in which actin and myosin filaments within a sarcomere slide past one another, powered by ATP and triggered by the release of calcium ions.

Build new actin filaments

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Amphoteric Substances — Acting as Both Acid and Base
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: an amphoteric substance can act as either an acid or a base depending on what it reacts with, donating a proton to a stronger base or accepting a proton from a stronger acid, with water and aluminum hydroxide serving as classic examples of this dual behaviour.

quiz.q: What defines an amphoteric substance?
options: It has no acidic or basic properties of any kind

quiz.q: What does an amphoteric substance do when it reacts with a stronger acid?
options: Remains completely unreactive
Accepts a proton, acting as a base
Converts the acid into a solid precipitate immediately
Donates a proton, acting as an acid

quiz.q: Name a classic example of an amphoteric substance.
options: Water
A pure noble gas
A strand of DNA

quiz.q: Why is aluminum hydroxide considered amphoteric?
options: It can only ever react as a base, never as an acid

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Cover Letter and Professional Correspondence
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a cover letter introduces a job or program applicant to a reader who has not yet seen their full application, using a concise, tailored argument to connect the applicants specific experience to the specific opportunity rather than repeating a resume in sentence form.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a cover letter?
options: To list every job the applicant has ever held in exhaustive detail
To replace the need for a resume entirely
To provide a full transcript of academic grades
To introduce an applicant to a reader who has not yet seen their full application

quiz.q: What should a strong cover letter connect?
options: Nothing in particular, since content does not matter

The reader to a completely unrelated organization

quiz.q: What mistake does an effective cover letter avoid?
options: Mentioning the applicants relevant experience at all
Addressing the specific opportunity being applied for
Using complete sentences throughout the letter
Simply repeating the resume in sentence form

quiz.q: Why should a cover letter be tailored to a specific opportunity rather than written generically?
options: Generic letters are always more persuasive than tailored ones
Cover letters are never read by the people who receive them

quiz.q: What tone is generally expected in professional correspondence like a cover letter?
options: Entirely humorous with no serious content

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Financial Mathematics: Tax Brackets and Marginal versus Average Tax Rate
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a progressive tax system applies increasing tax rates to successive brackets of income, so the marginal tax rate taxes only the portion of income within the highest bracket reached, while the average tax rate is the total tax paid divided by total income, and the two rates are rarely equal.

quiz.q: What does a progressive tax system apply to successive brackets of income?
options: Increasing tax rates
Decreasing tax rates as income rises
No tax whatsoever, regardless of income
A single fixed tax rate with no brackets at all

quiz.q: What does the marginal tax rate apply to?
options: A rate that has no connection to income brackets
Only income earned before the age of eighteen
Only the portion of income within the highest bracket reached
The entire income at a single flat rate

quiz.q: How is the average tax rate calculated?
options: Total income divided by the number of tax brackets
The lowest possible tax bracket rate alone
The highest marginal rate multiplied by two
Total tax paid divided by total income

quiz.q: Why are the marginal and average tax rates rarely equal in a progressive system?
options: All portions of income are always taxed at the exact same rate
Marginal and average tax rates are mathematically identical by definition
The average tax rate is always higher than the marginal rate
Only the top portion of income is taxed at the marginal rate, while lower portions are taxed at lower rates

quiz.q: What kind of tax system increases its rate as income rises?
options: A system that only applies to corporations
A system with no defined structure at all

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Human Biology: The Menstrual Cycle and Hormonal Regulation

quiz.q: What regulates the menstrual cycle?

A fixed, unchanging hormone level with no variation
The digestive system exclusively
A shifting balance of hormones

Insulin

options: Fertilization, which always occurs automatically
Implantation, which happens before ovulation
Ovulation
Menstruation, occurring at the very start of the cycle

quiz.q: What happens to the uterine lining across the menstrual cycle?
options: It builds up only once in a persons lifetime
It builds up and then sheds if pregnancy does not occur
It remains completely unchanged throughout the entire cycle
It is permanently removed after a single cycle

quiz.q: What is the overall biological purpose of the hormonal changes across the menstrual cycle?
options: Producing energy for muscular movement exclusively

Controlling the digestive system with no reproductive role

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Rocket Propellants and Oxidizer Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a rocket propellant system pairs a fuel with an oxidizer that supplies the oxygen needed for combustion even in the vacuum of space, and the choice of fuel-oxidizer combination determines the thrust, efficiency, and storage challenges of a given rocket design.

quiz.q: What does an oxidizer supply in a rocket propellant system?

A structural support for the rocket body
The oxygen needed for combustion

quiz.q: Why must a rocket carry its own oxidizer rather than relying on the atmosphere?

Rockets must be able to combust fuel even in the vacuum of space

quiz.q: What determines the thrust and efficiency of a given rocket design?
options: The colour of the rockets exterior paint
The exact number of windows on the rocket
The choice of fuel-oxidizer combination

quiz.q: What two components make up a rocket propellant system?
options: A fuel and an oxidizer
A single inert gas with no fuel at all

options: Some oxidizers and fuels are highly reactive or require extreme storage conditions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: Sound Devices — Alliteration, Assonance, and Onomatopoeia

A poem with no sound devices at all

The repetition of initial consonant sounds

quiz.q: What is assonance?

The repetition of an identical rhyme at the end of every line

quiz.q: What is onomatopoeia?

subjects.subject: Functions

subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: solving an optimization problem with calculus involves writing a quantity to be maximized or minimized as a function of a single variable, then finding where its derivative equals zero to locate the critical points that produce the largest or smallest possible value.

quiz.q: What does an optimization problem ask you to find?

The maximum or minimum value of a quantity
The colour of a graphed function
The exact midpoint of an unrelated data set

subjects.subject: Biology

subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: twin studies compare identical twins, who share nearly all their genes, to fraternal twins, who share about half, allowing researchers to estimate how much of a given trait is explained by genetics versus environment in the ongoing nature-nurture debate.

subjects.subject: Chemistry

subjects.subject: English

It has no effect on how a reader interprets any choice

quiz.q: Why might an author plant a subtle early hint that only makes sense after a later event?
options: Subtle hints always confuse readers with no later payoff
To reward attentive readers and add coherence to the narrative in hindsight
Foreshadowing removes the need for any later event to occur
Early hints are required to reveal the ending immediately

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Statistics: An Introduction to Variance
subjects.summary: Grade 8 Math strand: variance measures how far a set of data values are spread out from their mean by averaging the squared differences between each value and the mean, giving more weight to values that are farther away.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Statistics: An Introduction to Variance

quiz.q: What does variance measure about a data set?
options: The total number of values in the data set
The exact largest value in the data set
The order in which data was collected
How far the data values are spread out from the mean

quiz.q: How is variance calculated from a data set?
options: By counting how many values are above zero
By multiplying every value by two
By adding all the values together only
By averaging the squared differences between each value and the mean

quiz.q: Why are the differences from the mean squared when calculating variance?
options: Squaring makes every difference equal to zero
Squaring always produces a negative number
Squaring removes the need for a mean
Squaring prevents negative and positive differences from cancelling out and emphasizes larger gaps

quiz.q: What does a very small variance suggest about a data set?
options: The values are clustered closely around the mean
The mean cannot be calculated
The data set has no numerical values
The values are spread across a huge range

quiz.q: Why is variance a useful measure alongside the mean when describing a data set?
options: It shows how consistent or spread out the data is, which the mean alone cannot show
It always equals the mean in every data set
It replaces the need to ever calculate a mean
It can only be used with exactly two data points

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Plant Biology: Transpiration and the Cohesion-Tension Theory
subjects.summary: Students learn how the cohesion-tension theory explains the upward movement of water through xylem, driven by transpiration pulling on a continuous water column held together by hydrogen bonding between water molecules.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Plant Biology: Transpiration and the Cohesion-Tension Theory

quiz.q: According to the cohesion-tension theory, water moves upward through the xylem primarily because of:
options: Photosynthesis directly generating water flow
Gravity pulling water down from the roots
Evaporation (transpiration) from leaves creating tension that pulls a continuous water column upward
Active pumping by root cells

quiz.q: 'Cohesion' in the context of water transport refers to:
options: Minerals dissolving in water
Water molecules sticking to the xylem walls
Water molecules being attracted to each other via hydrogen bonds
Water evaporating from stomata

quiz.q: Which structures on a leaf's surface open and close to regulate water loss through transpiration?
options: Lenticels
Chloroplasts
Root hairs
Stomata

quiz.q: On a hot, dry, windy day, transpiration rate typically:
options: Increases, pulling water upward faster
Stays exactly the same
Stops entirely
Decreases significantly

quiz.q: 'Adhesion' contributes to water transport in the xylem by describing the attraction between:
options: Water molecules and each other
Carbon dioxide and water
Water molecules and the walls of the xylem vessels
Two separate xylem vessels

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Non-Stick Cookware and Fluoropolymer Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: nonstick cookware coatings rely on fluoropolymers, long carbon-chain molecules bonded to fluorine atoms whose strong carbon-fluorine bonds resist chemical reaction and create an extremely low-friction surface that food will not readily stick to or react with.

quiz.q: What class of material do nonstick cookware coatings rely on?
options: Uncoated ceramic with no polymer content
Fluoropolymers
Pure silver metal
A layer of table salt crystals

quiz.q: What element is bonded to the carbon chain in a fluoropolymer?
options: Sodium
Helium
Argon
Fluorine

quiz.q: Why do fluoropolymers resist chemical reaction?
options: They react instantly with any substance they contact
They contain no chemical bonds of any kind
Their bonds break apart at room temperature
Their carbon-fluorine bonds are very strong

quiz.q: What surface property makes a fluoropolymer coating useful for cookware?
options: A surface with no measurable properties at all
A surface that dissolves completely when heated
An extremely rough, high-friction surface
An extremely low-friction surface that food will not readily stick to

quiz.q: What kind of bond gives a fluoropolymer its chemical stability?
options: A bond that exists only in theory
An unstable, easily broken ionic bond
The carbon-fluorine bond
A weak hydrogen bond only

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: Poetic Craft, Narrative Devices, and Professional Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: students revisit the aubade, the picaresque novel, correlative conjunctions, the soliloquy, satirical news and misinformation, nonverbal communication, the cover letter, sound devices, and foreshadowing and dramatic irony.

quiz.q: What does an aubade typically mourn?
options: The coming separation of lovers as dawn arrives
A victory in battle celebrated at noon
The death of a monarch decades earlier
A harvest festival held in autumn

quiz.q: What is distinctive about correlative conjunctions?
options: They can only be used at the very start of a paragraph
They eliminate the need for any punctuation whatsoever
They work in pairs to link balanced grammatical elements
They never appear more than once in an entire essay

quiz.q: What technique do satirical news outlets rely on to mock real events?
options: Strict, unembellished factual reporting only
Exaggeration and irony
Complete silence on any current event
Random, unrelated numerical data

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a cover letter?
options: To introduce an applicant to a reader who has not yet seen their full application
To replace the need for a resume entirely
To provide a full transcript of academic grades
To list every job the applicant has ever held in exhaustive detail

quiz.q: What does foreshadowing do?
options: Removes all sense of anticipation from a narrative
Has no connection to later events in a story
Reveals the entire ending in the very first sentence
Plants early hints of events that will happen later in a narrative

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Domain and Range in Interval and Set Notation
subjects.summary: Students determine the domain and range of polynomial, radical, and rational functions and express restrictions using interval notation and set notation.

quiz.q: What is the domain of f(x) = √(x - 3)?

quiz.q: What is the domain of g(x) = 1/(x + 5)?
options: all real numbers except x = 5
all real numbers except x = -5
all real numbers

quiz.q: Which notation correctly represents "all real numbers greater than or equal to 2"?

options: all real numbers
x ≤ -3 or x ≥ 3

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology Review: Biotechnology, Physiology, and Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: students revisit wetland ecosystems, restriction enzymes and recombinant DNA, gel electrophoresis, phylogenetics and cladograms, C3/C4/CAM photosynthesis, DNA repair mechanisms, the menstrual cycle, twin studies, and allometric scaling.

quiz.q: What defines a wetland ecosystem?
options: An ecosystem that never contains any water at all
An ecosystem saturated with water for at least part of the year
An ecosystem defined solely by its average temperature
An ecosystem found only at extremely high altitudes

quiz.q: What property of DNA fragments does gel electrophoresis separate by?
options: Size
Colour
Taste
Exact age of the sample

quiz.q: How do C3 plants fix carbon dioxide?
options: By opening their stomata only at night
By avoiding the Calvin cycle entirely
Directly through the standard Calvin cycle
By absorbing carbon dioxide through their roots only

quiz.q: What regulates the menstrual cycle?
options: A process with no hormonal involvement at all
A shifting balance of hormones
The digestive system exclusively
A fixed, unchanging hormone level with no variation

quiz.q: What does allometric scaling describe?
options: A relationship that applies only to plants, never animals
The number of offspring an animal produces annually
The exact colour pattern of an animals fur
How an organisms metabolic rate relates to its body mass

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry Review: Polarity, Household Chemistry, and Acid-Base Extensions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand review: students revisit electronegativity and bond polarity, azo dyes, vapor pressure and Raoults law, bleach and oxidizing cleaners, thiols and skunk spray, amphoteric substances, rocket propellants, solvent polarity, and fluoropolymer chemistry.

quiz.q: What does electronegativity measure?
options: The exact number of neutrons in an atom
The total mass of an atoms nucleus
How strongly an atom attracts shared electrons in a covalent bond
The colour an element appears in visible light

quiz.q: What is vapor pressure?
options: The pressure exerted only by a solid at absolute zero
The pressure exerted by a substances vapour in equilibrium with its liquid phase
A pressure that exists only in outer space
The total pressure of an entire closed room

quiz.q: What functional group defines a thiol?
options: A nitrogen-oxygen double bond
A pure carbon-carbon triple bond
A group containing only hydrogen and oxygen
A sulfur-hydrogen group

quiz.q: What does an oxidizer supply in a rocket propellant system?
options: A structural support for the rocket body
The oxygen needed for combustion
A coolant with no chemical reactivity
A source of pure nitrogen gas only

quiz.q: What class of material do nonstick cookware coatings rely on?
options: Pure silver metal
A layer of table salt crystals
Uncoated ceramic with no polymer content
Fluoropolymers

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: The Haiku and Tanka — Compression and Natural Imagery
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a haiku is a compressed three-line poetic form built around a fixed syllable pattern and a single vivid image drawn from nature, while a tanka extends the same tradition to five lines and adds a personal or emotional turn after the natural image has been established.

quiz.q: What structural feature defines a haiku?
options: A rhymed couplet describing an urban skyline
A twelve-line form with no fixed structure at all
A compressed three-line form built around a single natural image
A form that forbids any reference to nature

quiz.q: How many lines does a tanka typically have?
options: Two lines
Five lines
A tanka has no fixed number of lines at all
Fourteen lines

quiz.q: What often follows the natural image in a tanka that a haiku does not usually include?
options: A formal legal argument
A second, unrelated natural image with no connection to the first
A personal or emotional turn
A list of historical dates

quiz.q: Why might a poet choose the compressed form of a haiku to describe a single moment?
options: Haiku are required to describe multiple unrelated moments at once
A longer form always captures a moment more effectively than a short one
The brevity forces the poet to distill the moment to its most essential image
Compression removes all imagery from a poem

quiz.q: What poetic tradition do both the haiku and the tanka descend from?
options: A tradition with no connection to nature imagery
A Japanese poetic tradition centered on natural imagery
An ancient Roman tradition of epic verse
A tradition that forbids any fixed syllable pattern

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: Higher-Order Derivatives and Rates of Change of Rates of Change
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a higher-order derivative is found by differentiating a function more than once, so the third derivative measures how the rate of change of the rate of change is itself changing, and higher-order derivatives reveal increasingly subtle features of a functions behaviour beyond slope and concavity.

quiz.q: How is a higher-order derivative found?
options: By graphing the function with no further calculation
By integrating a function a single time
By differentiating a function more than once
By setting the function equal to zero and solving

quiz.q: What does the third derivative of a function measure?
options: The total area under the original curve
How the rate of change of the rate of change is itself changing
The exact y-intercept of the original function
A quantity with no relationship to the original function

quiz.q: What do higher-order derivatives reveal beyond slope and concavity?
options: Nothing beyond what the first derivative already shows
Increasingly subtle features of a functions behaviour
Only the colour of the functions graph
The exact domain of the original function

quiz.q: What is another name for the second derivative of a position function in physics?
options: Displacement
Acceleration
Momentum, with no connection to the second derivative
Velocity

quiz.q: Why might an engineer care about the third derivative of a position function, sometimes called jerk?
options: It replaces the need to know velocity or acceleration entirely
It measures only the total distance travelled
It measures how abruptly acceleration itself is changing, which affects comfort and mechanical stress
The third derivative has no physical meaning of any kind

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Grassland and Savanna Ecosystems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: grassland and savanna ecosystems are dominated by grasses with scattered trees or none at all, shaped by seasonal rainfall, periodic fire, and grazing pressure that together prevent woody plants from overtaking the landscape and maintain the open structure characteristic of these biomes.

quiz.q: What plant type dominates grassland and savanna ecosystems?
options: Coniferous trees exclusively
Grasses
Coral and other marine organisms
Mosses and lichens exclusively

quiz.q: Name one factor that helps maintain the open structure of a savanna.
options: Total absence of any rainfall year-round
Complete absence of any grazing animals
Permanent ice cover
Periodic fire

quiz.q: What role does grazing pressure play in a grassland ecosystem?
options: It has no effect on the balance between grasses and trees
It helps prevent woody plants from overtaking the landscape
It eliminates all grasses from the ecosystem entirely
It guarantees that trees will always dominate the landscape

quiz.q: What pattern of rainfall typically shapes a savanna ecosystem?
options: Constant, unvarying rainfall every day of the year
Rainfall that occurs only as snow
A complete absence of rainfall in every season
A seasonal pattern with distinct wet and dry periods

quiz.q: Why do scattered trees rather than dense forest typically characterize a savanna?
options: Savannas receive more rainfall than any rainforest
Grazing animals always promote dense forest growth
Fire, grazing, and seasonal drought limit the growth of woody plants
Trees are entirely absent from every savanna on Earth

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Caffeine and Alkaloid Extraction Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: caffeine is a naturally occurring alkaloid, a nitrogen-containing organic compound, and its extraction from coffee beans or tea leaves typically relies on differences in solubility between polar water and a nonpolar solvent to separate caffeine from the other plant compounds surrounding it.

quiz.q: What class of organic compound is caffeine?
options: An alkaloid
A noble gas
An ionic salt with no carbon present
A pure metal

quiz.q: What element, in addition to carbon, defines an alkaloid such as caffeine?
options: Nitrogen
Pure sodium metal
Helium
Argon

quiz.q: What property difference is often exploited to extract caffeine from plant material?
options: Differences in colour alone, with no chemical basis
Differences in electrical conductivity of solid metals
Differences in solubility between a polar and a nonpolar solvent
Differences in radioactive decay rate

quiz.q: Why is a nonpolar solvent often useful in caffeine extraction?
options: It dissolves every compound in the plant material equally
It reacts explosively with caffeine and destroys it
It has no ability to dissolve any organic compound
It can selectively dissolve caffeine while leaving many polar plant compounds behind

quiz.q: What kind of source is caffeine naturally extracted from?
options: Distilled water with no plant material present
Coffee beans or tea leaves
Pure quartz crystal
A sample of inert noble gas

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Verbals — Gerunds, Participles, and Infinitives in Complex Sentences
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a verbal is a verb form that functions as another part of speech, so a gerund acts as a noun, a participle acts as an adjective, and an infinitive can act as a noun, adjective, or adverb, letting a writer pack additional action into a sentence without adding a full clause.

quiz.q: What is a verbal?
options: A noun that has been converted into a proper adjective
A punctuation mark used only in dialogue
A verb form that functions as another part of speech
A verb that can never appear in a sentence

quiz.q: What part of speech does a gerund function as?
options: A conjunction
A noun
A preposition
An interjection with no grammatical function

quiz.q: What part of speech does a participle typically function as?
options: An adjective
A coordinating conjunction
A pronoun
A verbal with no descriptive function at all

quiz.q: What roles can an infinitive play in a sentence?
options: Only a preposition, never anything else
A noun, an adjective, or an adverb
No grammatical role of any kind
Only a proper noun

quiz.q: Why might a writer use a verbal phrase instead of a full clause?
options: Verbals always make a sentence longer and less clear
A verbal phrase always changes the tense of the entire sentence
Verbals are forbidden in formal academic writing
To pack additional action into a sentence without adding a separate clause

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: Curve Sketching Using the First and Second Derivative Tests
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: curve sketching combines the first derivative test, which locates local maxima and minima by tracking where a function changes from increasing to decreasing or back, with the second derivative test, which confirms concavity, to build an accurate picture of a functions shape without plotting every point.

quiz.q: What does the first derivative test locate?
options: The colour of a functions graph
The total area under a curve
The exact y-intercept of a function
Local maxima and minima

quiz.q: What does the first derivative test track to identify a local maximum or minimum?
options: Where a function changes from increasing to decreasing or back
Where a function remains completely constant forever
Where the y-intercept crosses the x-axis
Where a function is undefined at every point

quiz.q: What does the second derivative test confirm about a critical point?
options: Its concavity
The exact numerical value of the function at that point
The total number of terms in the function
The colour of the point on a graph

quiz.q: Why is curve sketching useful compared to plotting every point on a graph?
options: Curve sketching removes the need to know anything about a function
It builds an accurate picture of a functions shape using key features rather than exhaustive plotting
Plotting every point is always faster than curve sketching
Curve sketching only works for functions with no derivative

quiz.q: What combination of tools does curve sketching typically rely on?
options: The first and second derivative tests together
A single derivative test used in isolation with no other information
A test that ignores concavity entirely
Only a ruler and no calculus at all

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Physiology: The Liver — Detoxification and Metabolic Functions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: the liver filters blood arriving from the digestive tract, breaking down or neutralizing toxins and metabolic waste products, storing glucose as glycogen, and producing bile that aids in the digestion and absorption of dietary fats, making it central to both detoxification and metabolism.

Immediately discards it without any filtration

Has no effect on blood arriving from digestion

Bone marrow
Glycogen
Pure oxygen gas

quiz.q: What substance does the liver produce to aid in fat digestion?
options: Bile
A substance with no role in digestion
Stomach acid exclusively
Insulin exclusively

quiz.q: Why is the liver considered central to detoxification?
options: It only processes water, with no role in toxin removal
It has no ability to interact with toxins of any kind
It breaks down or neutralizes toxins and metabolic waste products
Detoxification occurs exclusively in the lungs, not the liver

quiz.q: What happens to bile after the liver produces it?
options: It converts directly into glucose for storage
It has no connection to the digestive process
It aids in the digestion and absorption of dietary fats

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Chewing Gum — Polymer Base and Flavour Release
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: chewing gum consists of an insoluble polymer base that remains chewable because it does not dissolve in saliva, combined with soluble sugars, flavour compounds, and softeners that dissolve and diffuse out during chewing, which is why sweetness and flavour fade well before the gum itself breaks down.

quiz.q: Why does the base of chewing gum remain chewable rather than dissolving?

The polymer base is insoluble in saliva
Chewing gum contains no polymer of any kind
The polymer base dissolves instantly in saliva

options: They have no interaction with saliva whatsoever
They dissolve and diffuse out of the gum
They convert into an insoluble solid
They become permanently locked inside the polymer base

quiz.q: Why does the flavour of chewing gum fade before the gum itself breaks down?
options: Chewing gum releases no flavour compounds at any point
Flavour compounds and the polymer base leave the gum at the exact same rate
The soluble flavour compounds leave the gum well before the insoluble polymer base does
The polymer base dissolves first, before any flavour is released

quiz.q: What type of material forms the base of chewing gum?
options: A sample of liquid mercury
A block of solid metal
A pure ionic salt
An insoluble polymer

quiz.q: What role do softeners play in a chewing gum formulation?
options: They have no functional role in the gum formulation
They dissolve the polymer base completely within seconds
They cause the polymer base to become instantly rigid
They help keep the polymer base pliable and chewable

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Family Saga Novel Across Generations
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a family saga novel traces a family across multiple generations, following how inherited wealth, trauma, tradition, or ambition are passed down and reshaped by each successive generation, using the family itself as a lens for exploring broader historical and social change.

quiz.q: What does a family saga novel typically trace?
options: A single character across a single afternoon
A single generation with no reference to the past or future
A family across multiple generations
A nation with no reference to any individual family

quiz.q: What might a family saga novel show being passed down across generations?
options: Only the exact same physical house, with no other inheritance
A single unchanging opinion shared by every character
Nothing at all, since generations are treated as unconnected

quiz.q: What does a family saga novel often use the family as a lens for exploring?
options: Broader historical and social change
A subject that has no connection to history or society
A single isolated event with no wider significance
A topic entirely unrelated to any family member

quiz.q: Why might a family saga novel shift focus between different generations?

A family saga must remain fixed on a single generation only
To show how patterns, conflicts, or values are reshaped over time

quiz.q: What structural feature distinguishes a family saga from a novel focused on a single protagonist?
options: A complete absence of any named characters
A refusal to include any family relationships at all
A structure limited to a single day of events

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Financial Mathematics: Simple Interest and Calculating Total Amount

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Genetics: Nondisjunction and Aneuploidy
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: nondisjunction occurs when chromosomes fail to separate properly during meiosis, producing gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes, and when such a gamete is fertilized, the resulting condition, called aneuploidy, can lead to a chromosome count that differs from the typical number for the species.

A process with no connection to chromosome number at all
A perfectly normal separation of chromosomes during meiosis

options: Gametes with no chromosomes at all
Gametes that are genetically identical to the parent cell
An abnormal number of chromosomes
A perfectly normal, typical chromosome number in every case

quiz.q: What is aneuploidy?
options: A condition in which a chromosome count differs from the typical number for the species
A condition in which every chromosome count is identical across all species
A condition that has no relationship to chromosome number
A condition found only in single-celled organisms

quiz.q: When does nondisjunction occur in the cell cycle?
options: During meiosis, when chromosomes are meant to separate
During a process unrelated to cell division
Only after fertilization has already occurred
Only in cells that never divide at all

quiz.q: How can a gamete affected by nondisjunction lead to aneuploidy in offspring?

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Water Electrolysis and Hydrogen as a Fuel Source
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: electrolysis of water uses an electric current to split water molecules into hydrogen gas at the cathode and oxygen gas at the anode, and the hydrogen produced can later be recombined with oxygen in a fuel cell to release energy, making water electrolysis a route to storing electrical energy as chemical fuel.

quiz.q: What does electrolysis of water use to split water molecules?

An electric current

quiz.q: What gas is produced at the cathode during water electrolysis?
options: Chlorine gas exclusively
Nitrogen gas
Oxygen gas
Hydrogen gas

quiz.q: What gas is produced at the anode during water electrolysis?
options: Argon gas exclusively
Oxygen gas
Helium gas
Hydrogen gas

quiz.q: How can hydrogen produced by electrolysis later release energy?
options: By converting directly into a solid metal
By being permanently stored with no further chemical use
Hydrogen produced this way cannot release any energy
By recombining with oxygen in a fuel cell

quiz.q: Why is water electrolysis considered a way to store electrical energy?
options: It destroys electrical energy with no useful product remaining
It converts water directly into electricity with no intermediate step
It converts electrical energy into chemical energy stored in hydrogen fuel

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: Photo Manipulation and the Ethics of the Digital Image
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: digital editing tools make it possible to alter a photograph in ways that are difficult for a viewer to detect, from removing an object to reshaping a persons body, raising ethical questions about how much manipulation a viewer should expect and when an altered image crosses from enhancement into deception.

quiz.q: What do digital editing tools make possible with a photograph?
