Only converting a photograph into black and white
Nothing at all, since digital photographs cannot be altered

options: Printing the photograph on paper

Placing the photograph in a frame

quiz.q: What ethical question does photo manipulation raise?
options: Whether photographs should always be printed in black and white
When an altered image crosses from enhancement into deception

Whether cameras should be banned from all public spaces

quiz.q: Why might undetectable photo manipulation be more ethically concerning than obvious manipulation?

subjects.subject: Functions

the interest rate
the principal amount

Compound interest is only applied once
Compound interest is calculated on the principal plus previously earned interest

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Photosynthesis -- Light Reactions and the Calvin Cycle
subjects.summary: Students distinguish the light-dependent reactions, which occur in the thylakoid membrane and produce ATP and NADPH, from the light-independent Calvin cycle in the stroma, which uses those products to fix carbon dioxide into sugar.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Biology: Photosynthesis -- Light Reactions and the Calvin Cycle

quiz.q: The light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place in the:
options: Mitochondrial matrix
Thylakoid membrane
Stroma
Cell wall

quiz.q: Which two energy-carrying molecules are produced by the light-dependent reactions and used to power the Calvin cycle?
options: ATP and NADPH
DNA and RNA
Carbon dioxide and water
Glucose and oxygen

quiz.q: During the Calvin cycle, carbon dioxide is 'fixed' by combining it with a five-carbon molecule called:
options: Glucose
RuBP (ribulose bisphosphate)
ATP
Pyruvate

quiz.q: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from the splitting of:
options: Water molecules
ATP molecules
Glucose molecules
Carbon dioxide molecules

quiz.q: Unlike the light-dependent reactions, the Calvin cycle can proceed:
options: Only in the presence of oxygen
Only inside the mitochondria
Only in complete darkness with no other requirements
Without light directly, as long as ATP and NADPH are available

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Tattoo Ink and Pigment Permanence in Skin
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: tattoo ink consists of insoluble pigment particles suspended in a carrier liquid, and once injected into the dermis these particles are too large for the bodys immune cells to fully remove, allowing the pigment to remain visible beneath the skin for years or decades.

quiz.q: What are the pigment particles in tattoo ink suspended in?
options: A sample of pure gas
Nothing, since tattoo ink contains no carrier at all
A block of solid metal
A carrier liquid

quiz.q: Why does tattoo pigment remain visible in skin for years or decades?
options: The pigment particles are smaller than a single atom
The pigment particles are too large for immune cells to fully remove
Immune cells have no interaction with tattoo pigment at all
The pigment particles dissolve completely within a few days

quiz.q: Where in the skin is tattoo ink typically deposited?
options: Muscle tissue beneath the skin, never the skin itself
A layer entirely outside the body
The dermis
The outermost layer of dead skin cells only

quiz.q: What property of tattoo pigment particles makes them resist dissolving in the body?
options: Their tendency to evaporate rapidly at body temperature
Their complete lack of any physical structure
Their extremely high solubility in water
Their insolubility

quiz.q: What role do the bodys immune cells play in relation to tattoo pigment?
options: They have no interaction whatsoever with foreign particles in the skin
They convert the pigment into a different colour entirely
They completely and instantly remove all tattoo pigment
They attempt to remove the pigment but cannot fully clear particles that are too large

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Oral Communication: The Panel Discussion and Group Facilitation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a panel discussion brings together several speakers with different perspectives on a shared topic, guided by a moderator who manages turn-taking, keeps the conversation focused, and draws out disagreement or nuance rather than letting a single voice dominate the exchange.

quiz.q: What does a panel discussion bring together?
options: A single speaker addressing an empty room
A group of speakers who all share an identical opinion
Several speakers with different perspectives on a shared topic
A written document with no spoken component

quiz.q: What role does a moderator play in a panel discussion?
options: Managing turn-taking and keeping the conversation focused
Reading a prepared script with no interaction from panelists
Preventing every panelist from speaking at any point
Speaking for the entire length of the discussion with no other speakers

quiz.q: What might a skilled moderator draw out of a panel discussion?
options: A discussion with no connection to the original topic
Disagreement or nuance among the panelists
A single repeated answer from every speaker
Complete silence from every panelist present

quiz.q: Why is turn-taking important in a panel discussion?
options: Turn-taking has no effect on how a discussion unfolds
It prevents a single voice from dominating the exchange
Panel discussions are more effective when only one person ever speaks
Turn-taking always eliminates any useful discussion

quiz.q: What distinguishes a panel discussion from a single formal speech?
options: A formal speech always involves several speakers responding to each other
There is no meaningful difference between the two formats
A panel discussion always involves exactly one speaker
Multiple speakers with differing perspectives interact under a moderators guidance

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Sequences: Arithmetic Sequences — General Term and Sum Formulas
subjects.summary: Students use the general term formula tₙ = a + (n-1)d and the sum formula Sₙ = n/2(2a + (n-1)d) to analyze and solve problems involving arithmetic sequences.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Sequences: Arithmetic Sequences — General Term and Sum Formulas

quiz.q: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 4, 7, 10, 13, ...?
In the formula tₙ = a + (n-1)d, what does d represent?
options: the common difference
the sum of the sequence
the first term
the number of terms

quiz.q: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of an arithmetic sequence with first term 5 and common difference 2?
An arithmetic sequence has t₁ = 12 and t₅ = 32. What is the common difference?
Which of the following sequences is arithmetic?

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Evolution: Sexual Selection and Mate Choice
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: sexual selection favours traits that increase an individuals success at attracting mates or competing with rivals for access to them, which can produce elaborate features such as bright plumage or large antlers even when those traits provide no direct survival advantage or actively hinder it.

quiz.q: What does sexual selection favour?
options: Traits that increase success at attracting mates or competing for access to them
Only traits that improve an individuals ability to digest food
Traits that have no connection to mating success at all
Traits that always reduce an individuals chance of reproducing

quiz.q: Give an example of a trait that sexual selection can produce.
options: A trait with no connection to mate attraction
Bright plumage
A trait found equally in every species on Earth
A complete absence of any colouration

quiz.q: Can a trait favoured by sexual selection provide no direct survival advantage?
options: Sexual selection only ever removes existing traits, never adds new ones
No, every trait favoured by sexual selection always improves survival
Sexual selection never produces any trait of any kind
Yes, some traits favoured by sexual selection provide no survival advantage or even hinder survival

quiz.q: What might large antlers help an individual do in the context of sexual selection?
options: Regulate body temperature exclusively
Avoid all forms of predation entirely
Digest food more efficiently
Compete with rivals for access to mates

quiz.q: How does sexual selection differ from natural selection based purely on survival?
options: Sexual selection and natural selection always produce identical outcomes
Sexual selection has no connection to reproduction of any kind
Natural selection only ever concerns mate attraction, not survival
Sexual selection can favour traits that aid reproduction even at some cost to survival

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Science: Chemical Bonding: Metallic Bonds and Alloys
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science strand: a metallic bond forms when metal atoms share a sea of freely moving electrons, giving metals properties like conductivity and malleability, and an alloy is a mixture of two or more metals with enhanced properties.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Science: Chemical Bonding: Metallic Bonds and Alloys

quiz.q: What forms a metallic bond?
options: Metal atoms sharing a sea of freely moving electrons
A metal atom completely losing all of its electrons permanently
Two nonmetal atoms sharing a single electron pair
A concept unrelated to chemistry

quiz.q: Do metallic bonds help explain why metals conduct electricity well?
options: Yes
No, metallic bonds have no connection to electrical conductivity
A concept unrelated to metallic bonding
Metals never conduct electricity under any circumstances

quiz.q: What is an alloy?
options: A mixture of two or more metals with enhanced properties
A concept unrelated to metallic bonding
A type of gas found in the atmosphere
A single, pure metal element with no mixture at all

quiz.q: Why might steel, an alloy of iron and carbon, be stronger than pure iron alone?
options: This concept has no connection to chemistry
Steel and pure iron always have exactly the same physical properties
Alloys are always weaker than the pure metals used to create them
Adding carbon can disrupt the arrangement of metal atoms, making it harder for layers to slide past each other

quiz.q: Why is the malleability of metals, allowing them to be shaped without breaking, explained by the structure of metallic bonding?
options: This concept has no relevance to science
Metals are never able to be shaped or bent under any circumstances
The freely moving electrons allow metal atoms to shift position relative to each other without breaking the overall bond
Malleability has no connection to how metallic bonds are structured

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Proposal Argument — Identifying a Problem and Proposing a Solution
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a proposal argument identifies a specific problem, establishes why it matters to the intended audience, and then argues for a concrete, feasible solution, anticipating objections and explaining why the proposed course of action is more workable than the alternatives.

quiz.q: What does a proposal argument begin by identifying?
options: A specific problem
A list of random statistics with no context
An unrelated historical event
A solution with no stated problem behind it

quiz.q: What must a proposal argument establish about the problem it identifies?
options: That the problem does not actually exist
That the audience should ignore the problem entirely
Why it matters to the intended audience
That the problem cannot be solved under any circumstance

quiz.q: What does a proposal argument ultimately argue for?
options: A concrete, feasible solution
The permanent continuation of the problem
A solution with no practical steps of any kind
A solution deliberately kept vague and undefined

quiz.q: What should an effective proposal argument anticipate?
options: Objections to the proposed solution
Nothing at all, since objections are irrelevant
A total absence of any possible counterargument
Only objections raised by the writer themselves

quiz.q: Why might a proposal argument compare its solution to alternatives?
options: Comparing solutions is forbidden in a proposal argument
A proposal argument must never mention any other possible solution
Alternatives are always identical to the proposed solution
To explain why the proposed course of action is more workable than other options

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Geometry: The Equation of a Sphere in Three Dimensions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the equation of a sphere in three dimensions extends the equation of a circle by relating the coordinates of every point on the surface to a fixed centre point and a constant radius, so that the sum of the squared differences in each coordinate direction equals the square of the radius.

quiz.q: What does the equation of a sphere in three dimensions extend?
options: The equation of a circle
The equation of a straight line
The equation of a single point with no radius
An equation with no geometric meaning at all

quiz.q: What two quantities define a sphere in three-dimensional space?
options: A single coordinate with no radius involved
A radius with no defined centre point
A fixed centre point and a constant radius
Two unrelated points with no centre defined

quiz.q: What does the sum of the squared coordinate differences equal in the equation of a sphere?
options: The diameter of an unrelated circle
The radius itself, with no squaring involved
Zero, in every possible case
The square of the radius

quiz.q: How many coordinates does a point on the surface of a sphere in three dimensions require?
options: One
Three
Four
Two

quiz.q: Why is the equation of a sphere considered a natural extension of the equation of a circle?
options: A sphere and a circle share no mathematical relationship of any kind
A circle is defined using four dimensions rather than two
It applies the same distance relationship to points in three dimensions instead of two
The equation of a sphere ignores distance entirely

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Plant Biology: Mycorrhizal Associations and Nutrient Exchange
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a mycorrhizal association is a mutualistic partnership between a fungus and a plants roots, in which the fungus extends the roots effective surface area to absorb water and minerals such as phosphorus, while the plant supplies the fungus with sugars produced through photosynthesis.

quiz.q: What kind of relationship is a mycorrhizal association?
options: A purely parasitic relationship that harms the plant
A mutualistic partnership between a fungus and a plants roots
A relationship that occurs only between two plants, with no fungus involved
A relationship in which neither organism benefits

quiz.q: What does the fungus in a mycorrhizal association help the plant absorb?
options: Only oxygen produced by the plant itself
Water and minerals such as phosphorus
Only carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
Nothing, since the fungus provides no benefit to the plant

quiz.q: What does the plant supply to the fungus in this partnership?
options: Nothing, since the plant provides no benefit to the fungus
Water absorbed directly from the fungus
Sugars produced through photosynthesis
Minerals extracted from deep bedrock

quiz.q: How does the fungus increase the effectiveness of the plants root system?
options: By preventing the roots from absorbing any water at all
By shrinking the roots surface area to a fraction of its original size
By replacing the roots entirely with fungal tissue
By extending the roots effective surface area

quiz.q: Why is a mycorrhizal association considered mutualistic rather than one-sided?
options: Both the fungus and the plant receive a benefit from the exchange
Only the fungus benefits, while the plant receives nothing
Only the plant benefits, while the fungus receives nothing
Neither organism benefits in any way from the association

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Chocolate — Tempering and Cocoa Butter Crystal Forms
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: cocoa butter can solidify into several different crystal forms, and tempering chocolate involves carefully controlling temperature to encourage the formation of a single stable crystal form that gives finished chocolate its glossy surface, firm snap, and resistance to melting at room temperature.

quiz.q: What can cocoa butter solidify into?
options: A gas at room temperature
A liquid that never solidifies under any conditions
A single crystal form with no variation possible
Several different crystal forms

quiz.q: What does tempering chocolate involve?
options: Randomly heating and cooling chocolate with no control at all
Removing all cocoa butter from the chocolate
Adding water to the chocolate mixture
Carefully controlling temperature to encourage a stable crystal form

quiz.q: What visual quality does properly tempered chocolate typically have?
options: A surface that is always opaque white
No visible surface at all, since it remains a liquid
A dull, cloudy surface with no shine
A glossy surface

quiz.q: What textural quality does the stable crystal form give tempered chocolate?
options: A texture that never solidifies at any temperature
A texture identical to liquid honey
A firm snap
A texture with no measurable firmness

quiz.q: Why does poorly tempered chocolate often develop a dull, streaky surface?
options: Poorly tempered chocolate always looks identical to properly tempered chocolate
Unstable cocoa butter crystal forms create an uneven surface structure
Cocoa butter crystal form has no effect on chocolates appearance
A dull surface only occurs when no cocoa butter is present

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: Blank Verse and the Rhythm of Iambic Pentameter
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: blank verse is unrhymed poetry written in iambic pentameter, a rhythm of five unstressed-stressed syllable pairs per line, and its flexible structure, free of a rhyme scheme but still metrically patterned, has made it a favoured form for dramatic and narrative verse in English for centuries.

quiz.q: What defines blank verse?
options: Poetry written entirely in prose with no meter
Rhymed poetry with no fixed meter at all
Unrhymed poetry written in iambic pentameter
A form that forbids any use of rhythm

quiz.q: What rhythmic pattern does iambic pentameter follow?
options: A single stressed syllable repeated infinitely with no variation
Three stressed-unstressed pairs per line
Five unstressed-stressed syllable pairs per line
Ten unrelated syllables with no stress pattern at all

quiz.q: What does blank verse lack that many other poetic forms include?
options: Any use of syllables at all
A defined number of lines per stanza
A rhyme scheme
Any rhythmic pattern whatsoever

quiz.q: Why has blank verse been a favoured form for dramatic and narrative verse in English?
options: Rhyme is required for any dramatic verse, making blank verse unusable
Its flexible, metrically patterned structure suits extended storytelling without the constraint of rhyme
Blank verse has no metrical pattern to guide its rhythm
Blank verse forbids any storytelling of any kind

quiz.q: What remains constant in blank verse even though rhyme is absent?
options: The exact same words repeated in every line
A consistent metrical pattern
A strict requirement that every line rhyme with the next
Nothing at all remains constant

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Complex Numbers: Complex Conjugates and Their Properties
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the complex conjugate of a number reverses the sign of its imaginary part while leaving the real part unchanged, and multiplying a complex number by its conjugate always produces a real, non-negative result, a property used to simplify expressions and to divide by a complex number.

quiz.q: What does the complex conjugate of a number do to its imaginary part?
options: Converts it into a real number with no imaginary component remaining defined
Doubles it in magnitude
Removes it entirely, leaving only zero
Reverses its sign

quiz.q: What happens to the real part of a complex number when its conjugate is taken?
options: It is reversed in sign
It remains unchanged
It is removed entirely
It is doubled

quiz.q: What kind of result does multiplying a complex number by its conjugate always produce?
options: A result that is always exactly zero
An imaginary result with no real component
A negative real number in every case
A real, non-negative result

quiz.q: What common use does multiplying by a conjugate serve in working with complex numbers?
options: Eliminating the real part of a complex number entirely
Multiplying two real numbers together
Dividing by a complex number
Converting a real number into an imaginary one

quiz.q: If a complex number is written as a plus bi, what is its conjugate?
options: negative a plus bi
a plus bi, unchanged
a minus bi
negative a minus bi

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Human Biology: Sleep Architecture and the Stages of Sleep
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: sleep architecture refers to the cyclical pattern of distinct sleep stages a person moves through each night, alternating between non-REM stages of progressively deeper sleep and REM sleep, during which the brain is highly active and most vivid dreaming occurs, with each full cycle repeating several times per night.

quiz.q: What does sleep architecture refer to?
options: A pattern that occurs only once in a persons lifetime
A single unchanging state that lasts the entire night
The physical structure of the bedroom where a person sleeps
The cyclical pattern of distinct sleep stages a person moves through each night

quiz.q: What are the two broad categories of sleep stages mentioned?
options: Deep sleep and daytime wakefulness
Non-REM and REM sleep
Only non-REM sleep, with no other category
Only REM sleep, with no other category

quiz.q: During which stage does most vivid dreaming occur?
options: A stage that does not exist in human sleep
Every stage equally, with no difference between them
The deepest stage of non-REM sleep
REM sleep

quiz.q: What characterizes brain activity during REM sleep?
options: It is completely inactive, with no measurable brain activity
It matches waking activity exactly with no distinction
It is highly active
It ceases entirely until the person wakes up

quiz.q: How many times does a full sleep cycle typically repeat in one night?
options: A number that has no relationship to a full nights sleep
Zero times, since sleep is not cyclical
Exactly once, with no repetition
Several times

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Triboelectric Charging and the Chemistry of Static Electricity
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: triboelectric charging occurs when two different materials are rubbed together and electrons transfer from the surface of one material to the other, leaving one material with a net negative charge and the other with a net positive charge, an imbalance that later discharges as static electricity.

quiz.q: What happens when two different materials are rubbed together in triboelectric charging?
options: Protons transfer freely between the two materials
Electrons transfer from the surface of one material to the other
The two materials instantly fuse into a single substance
No charge transfer of any kind occurs

quiz.q: What charge does the material that loses electrons end up with?
options: No charge at all
A net positive charge
A charge that is always exactly neutral
A net negative charge

quiz.q: What charge does the material that gains electrons end up with?
options: A net positive charge
No charge at all
A net negative charge
A charge equal to the positive material

quiz.q: What eventually happens to the charge imbalance created by triboelectric charging?
options: It remains permanently locked in place with no discharge ever occurring
It discharges as static electricity
It converts directly into a different chemical element
It has no observable effect of any kind

quiz.q: What is required for triboelectric charging to occur between two materials?
options: The two different materials must be rubbed together
The materials must never come into contact with each other
The materials must be submerged in water before contact
The two materials must be completely identical to each other

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Drama: Stage Directions and the Language of the Performance Text
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: stage directions are the playwrights instructions describing setting, movement, tone, or gesture that accompany the dialogue of a play, guiding how a script should be staged and performed while remaining, unlike the dialogue itself, unspoken by the actors on stage.

quiz.q: What do stage directions describe?
options: Setting, movement, tone, or gesture
The biography of the playwright
Only the exact ticket price of a performance
A summary of the entire plot written after the play ends

quiz.q: Who writes the stage directions in a play?
options: The playwright
An actor improvising without any script
A director who never reads the original script
The audience, after watching a performance

quiz.q: What is true of stage directions in relation to the dialogue actors speak aloud?
options: Stage directions replace all dialogue in a play
Stage directions are typically unspoken by the actors on stage
Stage directions and dialogue are identical in every play
Stage directions are always spoken aloud exactly like dialogue

quiz.q: What do stage directions guide?
options: The seating chart of the audience
The financial budget of a theatrical production
The colour of the theatre curtains exclusively
How a script should be staged and performed

quiz.q: Why might a playwright include detailed stage directions rather than leaving staging entirely open?
options: Stage directions are forbidden in professional playwriting
Detailed stage directions always prevent a play from ever being performed
Leaving staging open always produces an identical result to detailed directions
To communicate a specific vision for how a scene should look and feel when performed

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Sequences: Geometric Sequences — General Term and Sum Formulas
subjects.summary: Students use the general term formula tₙ = a·r^(n-1) and the geometric series sum formula to solve problems involving constant ratios, including growth and finance contexts.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Sequences: Geometric Sequences — General Term and Sum Formulas

quiz.q: What is the 6th term of the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, ...?
In the formula tₙ = a·r^(n-1), what does r represent?
options: the sum of all terms
the number of terms
the first term
the common ratio

quiz.q: What is the common ratio of the geometric sequence 80, 20, 5, 1.25, ...?
What is the sum of the first 5 terms of the geometric sequence 2, 6, 18, 54, ...?
A ball dropped from 4 m reaches 60% of its previous height on each bounce. What height does it reach on the 4th bounce?

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biochemistry: Protein Structure — Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, and Quaternary Levels
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a proteins primary structure is its linear sequence of amino acids, its secondary structure consists of local folding patterns such as alpha helices and beta sheets, its tertiary structure is the overall three-dimensional shape of a single folded chain, and its quaternary structure describes how multiple folded chains assemble together.

quiz.q: What is a proteins primary structure?
options: A pattern found only in secondary structure
A structure that exists only in quaternary proteins
Its overall three-dimensional shape
Its linear sequence of amino acids

quiz.q: Name a folding pattern found in a proteins secondary structure.
options: A structure found only at the primary level
A pattern that never occurs in any protein
A single straight line with no folding at all
The alpha helix

quiz.q: What does a proteins tertiary structure describe?
options: The overall three-dimensional shape of a single folded chain
The linear sequence of amino acids only
The assembly of multiple separate protein chains
A structure that applies only to DNA, not protein

quiz.q: What does a proteins quaternary structure describe?
options: A folding pattern found only within a single amino acid
A structure that never involves more than one chain
How multiple folded chains assemble together
The sequence of amino acids in a single chain

quiz.q: Why is understanding all four levels of protein structure important for understanding protein function?
options: A proteins final shape at every level determines how it interacts with other molecules
All four levels of structure are always identical for every protein
Protein structure has no connection to protein function of any kind
Only the primary structure has any relevance to how a protein functions

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Molecular Gastronomy — Spherification and Gel Chemistry in Cooking
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: spherification is a molecular gastronomy technique in which a liquid containing sodium alginate is dropped into a calcium chloride bath, triggering a chemical reaction that forms a thin gel membrane around the droplet and produces a sphere with a liquid centre and a delicate solid outer shell.

quiz.q: What ingredient in the liquid is essential for spherification?
options: Pure table salt with no other chemical role
Distilled water with no dissolved compound present
A solid metal shaving
Sodium alginate

quiz.q: What solution is the sodium alginate liquid dropped into during spherification?
options: A container of liquid nitrogen with no chemical reaction
A calcium chloride bath
A bath of vegetable oil with no reactive component
A bath of pure distilled water with no dissolved ions

quiz.q: What forms around the droplet as a result of the reaction in spherification?
options: A solid metal coating
A thin gel membrane
No structural change occurs at all
A layer of ice regardless of temperature

quiz.q: What is the resulting structure of a sphere produced by this technique?
options: A flat, two-dimensional shape with no sphere formed
A liquid centre surrounded by a delicate solid outer shell
A sphere that is entirely gas-filled
A completely solid sphere with no liquid centre at all

quiz.q: What type of chemical process is responsible for forming the gel membrane in spherification?
options: A purely physical process with no chemical reaction involved
A reaction that requires no calcium of any kind
A nuclear reaction between two isotopes
A reaction between sodium alginate and calcium ions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Serial Novel and Publication in Instalments
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a serial novel is published in regular instalments rather than as a single complete volume, a format that shaped nineteenth-century fiction by encouraging cliffhangers and episodic pacing designed to keep readers subscribing to the next instalment rather than losing interest between releases.

quiz.q: How is a serial novel published?
options: Only once, as a single complete volume with no instalments
Exclusively as an audio recording with no written text
Anonymously, with no authors name ever attached
In regular instalments rather than as a single complete volume

quiz.q: What pacing technique did serial publication encourage in nineteenth-century fiction?
options: Cliffhangers and episodic pacing
A single unbroken scene with no change in pacing at all
An immediate resolution of every plot point in the first instalment
A refusal to include any tension or suspense

quiz.q: Why might a serial novel be structured around cliffhangers?
options: To keep readers subscribing to the next instalment
To ensure readers stop reading immediately after the first instalment
Cliffhangers were strictly forbidden in serial fiction
Cliffhangers have no effect on reader interest of any kind

quiz.q: What risk did a serial novel face between the release of each instalment?
options: Losing reader interest before the next instalment appeared
Losing the ability to be printed in any format
Gaining an infinite number of new readers automatically
Facing no risk at all, since interest was always guaranteed

quiz.q: How does the serial format differ from a novel released as a single complete volume?
options: It divides the story into regular instalments spaced out over time
There is no meaningful difference between the two formats
A serial novel is always shorter than a single-volume novel
A single complete volume is always released in instalments as well

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Solving Exponential Equations Using Common Bases
subjects.summary: Students solve exponential equations by rewriting both sides with a common base and equating exponents, laying the groundwork for logarithmic methods.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Functions: Solving Exponential Equations Using Common Bases

quiz.q: Solve for x: 2^x = 32
Solve for x: 3^(x+1) = 81
Solve for x: 9^x = 27
Solve for x: 4^(2x) = 8^(x+1)
Solve for x: (1/2)^x = 16

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Evolution: Genetic Bottlenecks and the Loss of Genetic Diversity
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a genetic bottleneck occurs when a population is sharply reduced in size by an event such as a natural disaster or disease outbreak, and the surviving individuals carry only a fraction of the original populations genetic diversity, leaving the recovered population more vulnerable to future environmental change.

quiz.q: What is a genetic bottleneck?
options: A steady, gradual increase in population size over centuries
A sharp reduction in population size that reduces genetic diversity
A process that has no connection to population size at all
An event that always increases genetic diversity

quiz.q: Give an example of an event that can cause a genetic bottleneck.
options: A steady, unchanging environment with no disruption
A period of unusually abundant food supply
An increase in the populations total genetic diversity
A natural disaster

quiz.q: What do surviving individuals after a bottleneck carry, compared to the original population?
options: More genetic diversity than the original population
The exact same amount of genetic diversity as before
Only a fraction of the original genetic diversity
No genetic material at all

quiz.q: Why does a population that has gone through a bottleneck become more vulnerable to future environmental change?
options: Reduced genetic diversity limits the range of traits available for natural selection to act on
A bottleneck always increases a populations resilience to change
Reduced genetic diversity always makes a population immune to environmental change
Genetic diversity has no connection to a populations ability to adapt

quiz.q: How does a genetic bottleneck differ from ordinary genetic drift in a stable population?
options: A genetic bottleneck and genetic drift are entirely unrelated concepts
Genetic drift only occurs in populations that never change in size
A bottleneck involves a sudden, sharp reduction in population size rather than gradual random change
A bottleneck always increases population size dramatically

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Science: Cell Transport: Diffusion and Osmosis
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science strand: diffusion is the movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to lower concentration, and osmosis is the diffusion of water specifically across a semi-permeable membrane.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Science: Cell Transport: Diffusion and Osmosis

quiz.q: What is diffusion?
options: A process that only occurs inside solid rocks
The movement of particles from an area of higher concentration to lower concentration
A concept unrelated to biology
The movement of particles from lower to higher concentration only

quiz.q: Is osmosis specifically the diffusion of water across a semi-permeable membrane?
options: Yes
Osmosis only ever involves the movement of oxygen gas
No, osmosis never involves the movement of water

subjects.subject: English

subjects.subject: Functions

subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the derivative of the natural exponential function equals the function itself, while the derivative of the natural logarithm of x equals one divided by x, and these two results extend differentiation beyond polynomial functions into functions that model growth, decay, and many real-world processes.

subjects.subject: Chemistry

subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a Lewis structure represents the arrangement of valence electrons around bonded atoms using dots for lone pairs and lines for shared bonds, and calculating the formal charge on each atom helps chemists judge which of several possible Lewis structures is the most reasonable representation of a molecule.
