Page number, since numbering shapes meaning

quiz.q: Why might the same written passage sound different when read aloud by two different speakers?
options: Each speaker brings a distinct prosody through their own pacing, stress, and intonation choices
Spoken performance always sounds identical no matter who reads it
Only the words on the page matter, with no role for the speaker
Reading aloud removes all possible variation in meaning

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Financial Mathematics: Real versus Nominal Interest Rates and Inflation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a nominal interest rate is the stated rate on an investment or loan before accounting for inflation, while the real interest rate adjusts that stated rate to reflect actual purchasing power, so that a nominal rate that looks attractive can still represent a loss in real terms if inflation rises faster than the nominal rate itself.

quiz.q: What is a nominal interest rate?
options: A rate that has no connection to money at all
The stated rate on an investment or loan before accounting for inflation
A rate that applies only to loans, never investments
A rate that already accounts fully for inflation

quiz.q: What does the real interest rate adjust for?
options: Actual purchasing power, accounting for inflation
The colour of the currency used
The exact number of years remaining on a loan
A factor with no connection to inflation

quiz.q: What can happen to a nominal interest rate that looks attractive if inflation rises faster than that rate?
options: It can still represent a loss in real terms
Inflation has no effect on the value of a nominal rate
It always guarantees a real gain regardless of inflation
The nominal rate automatically adjusts itself to cancel out inflation

quiz.q: Why is distinguishing between nominal and real interest rates useful for an investor?
options: Nominal and real rates are always numerically identical
The distinction has no practical use for any investor
It shows whether an investment actually increases purchasing power after inflation is considered
Real interest rates apply only to loans, never to investments

quiz.q: What relationship connects the nominal rate, the real rate, and inflation?
options: The real rate is always higher than the nominal rate
The real rate approximates the nominal rate minus the inflation rate
The nominal rate is always lower than the real rate
Inflation has no mathematical relationship to either rate

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Predator-Prey Coevolution and the Evolutionary Arms Race
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: predator-prey coevolution occurs when adaptations that improve a predators ability to capture prey exert selective pressure that favours prey with better defences, and those improved defences in turn favour predators with better hunting adaptations, producing an ongoing evolutionary arms race in which neither side gains a lasting advantage.

quiz.q: What is predator-prey coevolution?
options: A process in which only the prey ever changes over time
A reciprocal evolutionary process in which predator and prey adaptations drive one another
A process with no connection to natural selection at all
A process in which only the predator ever changes over time

quiz.q: What does an improved predator adaptation exert on a prey population?
options: Selective pressure favouring prey with better defences
Pressure that always eliminates the prey population entirely
No pressure of any kind on the prey population
Pressure that has no connection to evolution

quiz.q: What happens to predator adaptations after prey develop improved defences?
options: Predators immediately go extinct once prey improve their defences
Selective pressure then favours predators with better hunting adaptations
Predator adaptations have no relationship to prey defences
Predators stop evolving entirely once prey improve their defences

quiz.q: What term describes the ongoing cycle of reciprocal adaptation between predator and prey?
options: An evolutionary arms race
A process limited strictly to a single generation
A one-time event with no ongoing cycle
A relationship with no long-term evolutionary pattern

quiz.q: Why does neither predator nor prey typically gain a lasting advantage in this arms race?
options: Predators always gain a permanent advantage over prey
Prey always gain a permanent advantage over predators
Neither species is capable of adapting at all
Each improvement in one species tends to be matched over time by a counter-improvement in the other

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: The Human Ear and the Physics of Hearing
subjects.summary: Grade 9 Science strand: the ear captures sound waves and converts their vibrations into electrical signals through structures like the eardrum and cochlea, which the brain then interprets as sound.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: The Human Ear and the Physics of Hearing

quiz.q: What does the ear capture and convert into signals?
options: Chemical signals
Magnetic fields
Sound waves
Light waves

quiz.q: What structure vibrates when sound waves first enter the ear?
options: The retina
The cochlea alone
The optic nerve
The eardrum

quiz.q: What part of the inner ear helps convert vibrations into electrical signals?
options: The trachea
The cochlea
The epidermis
The pupil

quiz.q: How does the brain use the electrical signals sent from the ear?
options: It interprets them as sound
It uses them only to control digestion
It converts them into images
It ignores them completely

quiz.q: Studying the physics of sound and hearing connects biology to which field of physics?
options: Thermodynamics (the study of heat)
Astronomy (the study of space)
Acoustics (the study of sound)
Optics (the study of light)

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Media Literacy: The Filter Bubble and the Algorithmic Echo Chamber
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a filter bubble forms when a personalized recommendation algorithm repeatedly shows a user content that matches their existing preferences, gradually narrowing the range of viewpoints they encounter until opposing perspectives become rare, a dynamic that can reinforce existing beliefs and reduce exposure to alternative ideas.

quiz.q: What causes a filter bubble to form?
options: An algorithm designed specifically to show only opposing viewpoints
A personalized recommendation algorithm repeatedly showing content that matches existing preferences
A single unchanging list of content shown to every user identically
A random selection process with no personalization involved

quiz.q: What happens to the range of viewpoints a user encounters inside a filter bubble?
options: It remains exactly the same no matter how long the user engages with the platform
It always includes an equal balance of every possible viewpoint
It expands infinitely with no limit at all
It gradually narrows until opposing perspectives become rare

quiz.q: What is a filter bubble also commonly compared to?
options: An algorithmic echo chamber
A public library with no personalization at all
A printed newspaper with no algorithm involved
A source that guarantees full exposure to every viewpoint

quiz.q: What effect can a filter bubble have on existing beliefs?
options: It has no measurable effect on a users beliefs at all
It guarantees that a user will change their beliefs completely
It always weakens existing beliefs by exposing users to every viewpoint
It can reinforce existing beliefs by limiting exposure to alternative ideas

quiz.q: Why might understanding filter bubbles be important for evaluating information encountered online?
options: Filter bubbles only affect printed media, never online platforms
Understanding filter bubbles guarantees a reader will never encounter biased content again
Recognizing a filter bubble helps a reader seek out perspectives the algorithm might otherwise hide
Filter bubbles have no relevance to evaluating information at all

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Geometry: The Intersection of a Line and a Plane in Three Dimensions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: finding where a line intersects a plane in three dimensions involves substituting the parametric equations of the line into the equation of the plane and solving for the parameter, and depending on the result the line may cross the plane at exactly one point, lie entirely within it, or run parallel to it with no intersection at all.

quiz.q: What equations are substituted into a planes equation to find where a line intersects it?
options: The equation of an unrelated circle
The parametric equations of the line
A single fixed coordinate with no equation involved
The equation of a second, unrelated plane

quiz.q: What is solved for after substituting the lines equations into the planes equation?
options: The slope of the plane
The parameter
The colour of the intersection point
The radius of the plane

quiz.q: What is one possible outcome when a line meets a plane in three dimensions?
options: The line always lies exactly on top of every other line
The line always intersects the plane at an infinite number of unrelated points with no pattern
The line crosses the plane at exactly one point
The line always passes through every point in space

quiz.q: What does it mean if a line lies entirely within a plane?
options: Every point on the line also satisfies the equation of the plane
No point on the line ever satisfies the equation of the plane
The line must be perpendicular to the plane at every point
The line and plane share no relationship at all

quiz.q: What does it mean if a line runs parallel to a plane with no intersection?
options: The line and plane are identical to each other
The line meets the plane at every possible point
The line never meets the plane at any point
The line always meets the plane at exactly one point

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Antibiotic Mechanisms — Disrupting the Bacterial Cell Wall
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: many antibiotics such as penicillin work by interfering with the enzymes bacteria use to build their rigid cell wall, so that as the bacterium grows and attempts to divide, the weakened wall cannot withstand internal pressure and the cell ruptures, a mechanism that exploits a structural feature human cells do not share.

quiz.q: What structure do antibiotics such as penicillin typically target?
options: The bacterial cell wall
A structure that does not exist in bacteria
The bacterial nucleus, which bacteria do not actually possess
The human nucleus

quiz.q: What do these antibiotics interfere with in order to disrupt the cell wall?
options: The DNA sequence of a human cell
The enzymes bacteria use to build their cell wall
A structure found only in viruses
An enzyme with no connection to the cell wall

quiz.q: What happens to a bacterium once its cell wall is weakened by such an antibiotic?
options: It becomes permanently immune to any further antibiotic exposure
It develops a stronger cell wall than before
It immediately converts into a different species of bacteria
It ruptures under internal pressure as it attempts to grow and divide

quiz.q: Why can antibiotics that target the bacterial cell wall be selective for bacteria over human cells?
options: Human cells and bacterial cells share an identical cell wall structure
Human cells do not have the same rigid cell wall structure that bacteria depend on
Antibiotics affect every type of cell equally, with no selectivity
Human cells lack any structure that could be affected by antibiotics

quiz.q: What happens during bacterial growth and division that makes a weakened cell wall especially dangerous to the bacterium?
options: The bacterium becomes completely immune to internal pressure changes
Internal pressure disappears entirely once the wall is weakened
Growth and division stop having any effect on internal pressure
Internal pressure builds and the compromised wall cannot contain it

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Chemical Sensors — How pH and Gas Sensors Work
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a chemical sensor converts the presence or concentration of a target substance into a measurable signal, so a pH sensor typically measures the voltage generated across a special glass membrane sensitive to hydrogen ion concentration, while a gas sensor may rely on a chemical reaction at its surface that changes electrical resistance in the presence of a specific gas.

quiz.q: What does a chemical sensor convert the presence of a target substance into?
options: A completely random and unrelated output
A signal that has no connection to concentration
A measurable signal
A substance that cannot be detected at all

quiz.q: What does a typical pH sensor measure to determine hydrogen ion concentration?
options: The exact colour of the surrounding air
The mass of the solution being tested
The temperature of the solution alone, with no other measurement
A voltage generated across a special glass membrane

quiz.q: What might change in a gas sensor when a specific gas is present at its surface?
options: Its physical size, which never changes in any sensor
The colour of the surrounding room
Its electrical resistance
The sensor immediately stops functioning altogether

quiz.q: What triggers the response of a gas sensor that relies on surface chemistry?
options: A purely mechanical process with no chemistry involved
A reaction that occurs only in the absence of any gas
A chemical reaction occurring at the sensor surface
A process with no chemical reaction involved at all

quiz.q: Why is converting a chemical property into an electrical signal useful for a sensor?
options: Converting chemical properties into signals prevents any measurement from occurring
Electrical signals cannot be measured or interpreted in any practical way
It allows the concentration of a substance to be measured quickly and read electronically
Electrical signals have no connection to chemical concentration

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Campus Novel and the World of Higher Education
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a campus novel is set within the enclosed world of a college or university, often using the tension between intellectual ambition and personal or institutional politics to satirize academic life, following students or faculty as they navigate rivalry, status, and the pressure to succeed within that self-contained community.

quiz.q: Where is a campus novel typically set?
options: In a courtroom with no academic setting involved
Entirely within a single family household
Within the enclosed world of a college or university
On a remote island with no institution present

quiz.q: What tension does a campus novel often use to satirize academic life?
options: A tension found only in fairy tales, never in realistic fiction
The tension between intellectual ambition and personal or institutional politics
A tension that has no connection to intellectual life at all
The tension between two unrelated nations at war

quiz.q: Who might a campus novel typically follow as its central characters?
options: Only characters with no connection to any school
Exclusively young children in elementary school
Characters who never interact with any academic institution
Students or faculty

quiz.q: What pressures do characters in a campus novel often navigate?
options: Rivalry, status, and the pressure to succeed
Pressures entirely unrelated to their academic environment
A complete absence of any conflict or pressure
Only physical, non-academic challenges

quiz.q: Why is the campus setting well suited to satire in this genre?
options: Its self-contained community concentrates ambition, hierarchy, and politics in one setting
A campus setting removes all possibility of conflict or ambition
Satire requires a setting with no defined community at all
A university setting has no connection to hierarchy or politics

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Composition of Functions
subjects.summary: Students evaluate and simplify composite functions f(g(x)) and g(f(x)) and determine the domain of a composite function.

quiz.q: If f(x) = x + 3 and g(x) = 2x, what is f(g(2))?
If f(x) = x² and g(x) = x - 1, what is (f∘g)(x)?
options: x² - 2x
x² - 1

quiz.q: If f(x) = √x and g(x) = x + 4, what is the domain of (f∘g)(x)?
options: all real numbers

quiz.q: If f(x) = 2x - 1 and g(x) = x + 5, what is g(f(3))?
Which expression correctly represents "g composed with f, evaluated at x"?
options: f(x)·g(x)
g(f(x))
f(x) + g(x)
f(g(x))

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Genomic Libraries and DNA Cloning Techniques
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a genomic library is a collection of DNA fragments from an organisms entire genome, each fragment inserted into a separate vector such as a plasmid and introduced into host bacteria, so that as the bacteria multiply they produce many identical copies of each fragment, preserving the complete genome in a form that researchers can search and retrieve piece by piece.

quiz.q: What is a genomic library?
options: A single unbroken strand of DNA with no fragments at all
A collection containing no DNA of any kind
A physical building that stores printed books about genetics
A collection of DNA fragments from an organisms entire genome

quiz.q: What is each DNA fragment inserted into when a genomic library is constructed?
options: A structure with no connection to DNA insertion
A separate vector such as a plasmid
A single shared vector containing every fragment at once
A fragment of RNA rather than any vector

quiz.q: What organism is commonly used to multiply the inserted DNA fragments?
options: A fully grown human being
A plant with no bacterial component involved
An organism incapable of reproduction
Host bacteria

quiz.q: What happens to each DNA fragment as the host bacteria multiply?
options: The fragment is destroyed completely
The fragment converts into a completely different gene
No copies of the fragment are ever produced
Many identical copies of the fragment are produced

quiz.q: Why is a genomic library useful to researchers?
options: It has no practical research application of any kind
It preserves the complete genome in a form that can be searched and retrieved piece by piece
It only stores information about a single gene, never a complete genome
It destroys all genetic information rather than preserving it

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Enzymes as Biological Catalysts Compared to Industrial Catalysts
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up specific reactions inside living cells by lowering activation energy through a precisely shaped active site, and comparing them with industrial catalysts such as those used in the Haber process highlights how enzymes achieve remarkable specificity and efficiency at the mild temperatures and pressures found in living organisms.

quiz.q: What are enzymes classified as?
options: A substance with no effect on reaction rate
Biological catalysts
Structural proteins with no catalytic role
A type of inorganic mineral

quiz.q: What do enzymes lower in order to speed up a reaction?
options: Activation energy
The total mass of the reactants
The temperature of the surrounding environment permanently
The number of atoms present in a reactant

quiz.q: What structural feature of an enzyme allows it to act on a specific reactant?
options: Its precisely shaped active site
A random shape that changes with every reaction
A feature that applies equally to every possible reactant with no selectivity
An active site identical in every enzyme

quiz.q: What condition do enzymes typically operate under, compared to many industrial catalysts?
options: Mild temperatures and pressures found in living organisms
A complete vacuum with no surrounding conditions at all
Conditions with no defined temperature or pressure
Extremely high temperatures and pressures identical to industrial reactors

quiz.q: What quality do enzymes demonstrate that is often highlighted when comparing them to industrial catalysts such as those in the Haber process?
options: Remarkable specificity and efficiency
An inability to catalyze any reaction at all
A requirement for extremely high pressure to function
A complete lack of specificity for any reaction

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Poetry: The Limerick and the Comic Verse Tradition
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a limerick is a five-line comic poem with a distinctive AABBA rhyme scheme and a bouncing anapestic rhythm, traditionally building toward a punchline or absurd twist in its final line, making it a compact form well suited to wordplay, exaggeration, and light satire.

quiz.q: How many lines does a limerick have?
options: Three
Five
Fourteen
Eight

quiz.q: What rhyme scheme is characteristic of a limerick?
options: AAAA
ABAB
A rhyme scheme that is never fixed in a limerick
AABBA

quiz.q: What kind of rhythm does a limerick traditionally use?
options: A rhythm identical to free verse
A bouncing anapestic rhythm
The exact rhythm of a Shakespearean sonnet
A rhythm with no defined pattern at all

quiz.q: What does a limerick traditionally build toward in its final line?
options: A punchline or absurd twist
A detailed historical account
A solemn, tragic conclusion
A line with no connection to the rest of the poem

quiz.q: Why is the limerick well suited to wordplay and light satire?
options: Its structure is identical to a serious elegy
Limericks are always written about tragic subjects only
A limerick forbids any humour or wordplay of any kind
Its compact, rhythmic, comic structure invites exaggeration and a punchline twist

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: An Introduction to Antiderivatives and Integration
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: an antiderivative of a function reverses the process of differentiation, finding a function whose derivative matches the original one, and this idea underlies integration, a tool used to determine quantities such as total accumulated change or the area beneath a curve.

quiz.q: What does an antiderivative of a function do?
options: It only applies to constant functions
It removes all variables from a function entirely
It reverses the process of differentiation
It always produces the same function unchanged

quiz.q: What must be true of the derivative of an antiderivative?
options: It must always equal zero
It must be undefined at every point
It must match the original function
It must always equal a different unrelated function

quiz.q: What broader mathematical tool does the idea of an antiderivative underlie?
options: Integration
A tool with no connection to calculus
The quadratic formula
Multiplication of matrices

quiz.q: Name one quantity that integration can be used to determine.
options: The area beneath a curve
The slope of a single fixed point with no curve involved
The number of terms in an unrelated sequence
The exact colour of a graph

quiz.q: Why is finding an antiderivative sometimes described as the reverse of finding a derivative?
options: Antiderivatives and derivatives are entirely unrelated operations
Differentiation and integration always produce identical results
Finding an antiderivative always produces a numerical constant with no function attached
Differentiating the antiderivative returns the original function you started with

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Human Ecological Footprint and Carrying Capacity
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: an ecological footprint estimates the amount of biologically productive land and water a population requires to produce the resources it consumes and absorb the waste it generates, and comparing that footprint to the carrying capacity of the available land highlights whether current human resource use is sustainable over the long term.

quiz.q: What does an ecological footprint estimate?
options: The amount of biologically productive land and water a population requires
A measurement with no connection to resource use
The exact number of people living in a single city
The total number of species found in a single ecosystem

quiz.q: What two things does an ecological footprint account for in a population resource use?
options: The resources it consumes and the waste it generates
Only the resources it consumes, with no reference to waste
Neither resource consumption nor waste generation
Only the waste it generates, with no reference to resources

quiz.q: What does comparing an ecological footprint to carrying capacity help reveal?
options: The total number of predators in an ecosystem
The exact temperature of a given ecosystem
Whether current resource use is sustainable over the long term
A comparison with no practical meaning at all

quiz.q: What happens when a populations ecological footprint exceeds the carrying capacity of its available land?
options: Resource use becomes unsustainable over time
Carrying capacity has no relationship to ecological footprint at all
The population immediately disappears with no further effect
Resource use automatically becomes more sustainable

quiz.q: Why is the concept of an ecological footprint useful for evaluating sustainability?
options: It converts complex resource use into a single land-based measure that can be compared across populations
It only applies to non-human species, never to humans
It ignores all forms of resource consumption entirely
It has no practical application in evaluating sustainability

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: The Chemistry of Rust — Iron Oxidation and Corrosion Mechanisms
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water in an electrochemical process, in which iron atoms lose electrons to become iron ions at one region of the metal surface while oxygen is reduced at another, and the resulting iron oxide product is a flaky, porous compound that fails to protect the underlying metal from further corrosion.

quiz.q: What two substances does iron react with to form rust?
options: A noble gas with no reactivity at all
Pure carbon dioxide alone
Oxygen and water
Only nitrogen gas, with no other reactant

quiz.q: What type of process is rust formation classified as?
options: A nuclear process involving isotopes
A process that occurs with no reaction of any kind
A purely mechanical process with no chemical reaction
An electrochemical process

quiz.q: What happens to iron atoms at one region of the metal surface during rust formation?
options: They convert directly into rust with no electron transfer at all
They gain electrons and become neutral oxygen
They remain completely unchanged throughout the process
They lose electrons to become iron ions

quiz.q: What physical property of rust makes it a poor protective layer for the underlying metal?
options: It is denser than the original iron metal
It is flaky and porous
It is perfectly smooth and completely impermeable
It forms a layer that never separates from the metal surface

quiz.q: Why does rust fail to prevent further corrosion, unlike some other metal oxide coatings?
options: Rust formation stops permanently after the first layer forms
Rust always forms a perfectly sealed layer that blocks all further reaction
Rust prevents any further contact between the metal and its environment
Its flaky, porous structure lets oxygen and water continue reaching the metal underneath

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Restaurant Review as Evaluative Writing
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a restaurant review evaluates a dining experience across categories such as food quality, service, and atmosphere, combining specific sensory detail with a clearly stated overall judgment, so that a reader can both picture the experience and understand exactly how the writer weighed its strengths against its weaknesses.

quiz.q: What categories does a restaurant review typically evaluate?
options: Only the price of the parking lot outside
A single category with no further detail given
Food quality, service, and atmosphere
The architectural style of unrelated nearby buildings

quiz.q: What kind of detail does a restaurant review combine with its overall judgment?
options: No detail at all, only a numeric score
A summary of the restaurants complete financial history
Detail unrelated to the dining experience
Specific sensory detail

quiz.q: Why does a restaurant review need a clearly stated overall judgment?
options: A restaurant review must remain entirely neutral with no evaluation
So a reader understands how the writer weighed strengths against weaknesses
An overall judgment would make the review less useful to a reader
A restaurant review should never state any judgment at all

quiz.q: What allows a reader to picture the dining experience described in a review?
options: A list of unrelated statistics with no sensory content
Specific sensory detail about food, service, and atmosphere
A complete absence of any descriptive language
A review written with no reference to the actual meal

quiz.q: Why is evaluative writing like a restaurant review useful practice for other forms of argument?
options: It has no connection to argumentative writing of any kind
It requires supporting a judgment with specific, concrete evidence
Evaluative writing never requires any supporting evidence
A restaurant review must avoid forming any judgment whatsoever

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Quadratic Functions: Completing the Square and Vertex Form
subjects.summary: Students convert quadratic functions from standard form to vertex form by completing the square, and use vertex form to identify the vertex and axis of symmetry.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Quadratic Functions: Completing the Square and Vertex Form

quiz.q: What is the vertex of y = (x - 2)² + 5?
Convert y = x² + 6x + 5 to vertex form by completing the square.
What is the axis of symmetry for y = 2(x - 4)² + 1?
When completing the square for y = x² - 8x + 3, what value is added and subtracted in the process?
Which vertex form represents a parabola with vertex (-1, -3) that opens downward and is narrower than y = x² (a = -2)?

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Sensory Adaptation and Habituation in Nervous Systems
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: sensory adaptation is a decrease in a sensory receptors response to a constant, unchanging stimulus, while habituation is a related but distinct decrease in behavioural response that occurs within the nervous system itself after repeated exposure to a stimulus, together explaining why a constant background smell or sound gradually fades from conscious awareness.

quiz.q: What is sensory adaptation?
options: A process that only affects vision, never any other sense
A decrease in a sensory receptors response to a constant, unchanging stimulus
An increase in a sensory receptors response to every stimulus
A process with no connection to sensory receptors at all

quiz.q: What is habituation?
options: A process identical in every way to muscle contraction
An increase in behavioural response after a single exposure to a stimulus
A decrease in behavioural response within the nervous system after repeated exposure to a stimulus
A process that has no connection to repeated stimulus exposure

quiz.q: Where does habituation occur, distinguishing it from sensory adaptation at the receptor level?
options: In bone tissue exclusively
Only within muscle tissue, with no nervous involvement
Within the nervous system itself
Entirely outside the body, with no biological basis

quiz.q: What everyday experience can sensory adaptation and habituation together help explain?
options: Why every stimulus becomes more noticeable the longer it is present
Why a constant background smell or sound gradually fades from conscious awareness
A phenomenon with no connection to everyday sensory experience
Why a sudden loud noise always goes completely unnoticed

quiz.q: Why might sensory adaptation and habituation be considered biologically useful?
options: They allow an organism to filter out unchanging background stimuli and focus attention on new or changing information
They cause every stimulus to become permanently more intense over time
They have no adaptive value to an organism at all
They prevent an organism from ever detecting any stimulus again

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Osmotic Pressure and Its Role Among the Colligative Properties
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: osmotic pressure is the pressure that must be applied to a solution to stop the net inward flow of solvent across a semipermeable membrane from a region of lower solute concentration, and like boiling point elevation and freezing point depression it is classified as a colligative property because it depends on the number of dissolved particles rather than their identity.

quiz.q: What is osmotic pressure?
options: A pressure that only applies to solids, never to solutions
The pressure needed to stop the net inward flow of solvent across a semipermeable membrane
A pressure with no connection to solvent movement at all
The pressure inside a sealed container of pure gas

quiz.q: What kind of membrane is involved in the phenomenon of osmotic pressure?
options: A semipermeable membrane
A structure that is not a membrane at all
A membrane that allows every substance to pass equally
A membrane that blocks every substance completely

quiz.q: What category of property is osmotic pressure classified under?
options: A property with no defined classification
A purely physical property unrelated to solute concentration
A colligative property
A property that depends only on the identity of the solute

quiz.q: What determines the size of a colligative property such as osmotic pressure?
options: The exact chemical identity of the solute, rather than particle count
The colour of the dissolved particles
The number of dissolved particles, rather than their identity
A factor entirely unrelated to the solute

quiz.q: Name another colligative property besides osmotic pressure mentioned as a comparison.
options: The colour of a transition metal complex
Electrical conductivity of a pure metal
The radioactive half-life of an isotope
Boiling point elevation

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: English Review: Free Verse, Ellipsis, Recitation, and Campus Fiction
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand review: students revisit free verse, the ellipsis, reading aloud and recitation, the campus novel, and the restaurant review.

quiz.q: What does free verse abandon compared to traditional poetic forms?
options: All use of line breaks of any kind
The ability to use imagery at all
Every reference to natural speech patterns
A fixed meter and a regular rhyme scheme

quiz.q: How is an ellipsis typically shown in a printed sentence?
options: As a single exclamation mark
As a capitalized word in brackets
As three spaced periods
As a colon followed by a dash

quiz.q: What does prosody refer to when reading a text aloud?
options: A quality that applies only to written text, never spoken performance
The physical size of the printed page
The exact spelling of every word in the text
The rhythm, stress, and intonation a speaker brings to the reading

quiz.q: Where is a campus novel typically set?
options: On a remote island with no institution present
Entirely within a single family household
In a courtroom with no academic setting involved
Within the enclosed world of a college or university

quiz.q: What categories does a restaurant review typically evaluate?
options: The architectural style of unrelated nearby buildings
Only the price of the parking lot outside
Food quality, service, and atmosphere
A single category with no further detail given

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Algebra: Factoring Polynomials — Common Factors, Grouping, and Special Patterns
subjects.summary: Students factor polynomial expressions using common factoring, factoring by grouping, and special patterns such as difference of squares and perfect square trinomials.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Algebra: Factoring Polynomials — Common Factors, Grouping, and Special Patterns

quiz.q: Factor completely: 6x² + 9x
Factor: x² - 49
Factor by grouping: x³ + 2x² + 3x + 6
Which correctly factors the perfect square trinomial x² + 10x + 25?
Factor completely: 2x² - 8

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology Review: Hemostasis, Endocrine Physiology, Coevolution, and Biotechnology
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand review: students revisit hemostasis, the pancreas, predator-prey coevolution, genomic libraries, and sensory adaptation and habituation.

quiz.q: What is hemostasis?
options: A process that only occurs in bone tissue
A process with no connection to blood vessels at all
The process that stops bleeding after an injury
A process that causes bleeding to increase after an injury

quiz.q: What is the exocrine role of the pancreas?
options: Producing red blood cells
Filtering toxins out of the blood
Secreting digestive enzymes into the small intestine
Releasing insulin directly into the bloodstream

quiz.q: What is predator-prey coevolution?
options: A process with no connection to natural selection at all
A reciprocal evolutionary process in which predator and prey adaptations drive one another
A process in which only the prey ever changes over time
A process in which only the predator ever changes over time

quiz.q: What is a genomic library?
options: A physical building that stores printed books about genetics
A collection of DNA fragments from an organisms entire genome
A single unbroken strand of DNA with no fragments at all
A collection containing no DNA of any kind

quiz.q: What is sensory adaptation?
options: A process with no connection to sensory receptors at all
A process that only affects vision, never any other sense
An increase in a sensory receptors response to every stimulus
A decrease in a sensory receptors response to a constant, unchanging stimulus

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry Review: Bonding, Materials, Energy, and Catalysis
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand review: students revisit Lewis structures and formal charge, the chemistry of glass, photovoltaic cells, enzymes compared with industrial catalysts, and osmotic pressure.

quiz.q: What does a Lewis structure represent?
options: A structure with no connection to electrons at all
The physical state of a substance at room temperature
The arrangement of valence electrons around bonded atoms
The total mass of a molecule

quiz.q: What type of solid is glass classified as?
options: A gas at room temperature
A pure metal
An amorphous solid
A perfect crystalline solid

quiz.q: What does a photovoltaic cell convert sunlight into?
options: A gas with no other product formed
Electricity
Heat with no electrical output at all
Pure water

quiz.q: What are enzymes classified as?
options: A type of inorganic mineral
A substance with no effect on reaction rate
Structural proteins with no catalytic role
Biological catalysts

quiz.q: What is osmotic pressure?
options: The pressure inside a sealed container of pure gas
The pressure needed to stop the net inward flow of solvent across a semipermeable membrane
A pressure with no connection to solvent movement at all
A pressure that only applies to solids, never to solutions

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Pastoral Tradition — Idyllic Nature in Poetry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: pastoral poetry idealizes rural life and the natural landscape, often through the voice of a shepherd or countryside speaker, contrasting the simplicity and harmony of nature with the corruption or stress of urban and courtly life.

quiz.q: What does pastoral poetry typically idealize?
options: The chaos of a crowded courtroom
A setting with no connection to nature at all
Rural life and the natural landscape
The stress of urban and courtly life

quiz.q: Whose voice does pastoral poetry often adopt as its speaker?
options: A judge presiding over a trial
A speaker with no connection to the countryside
A factory worker in a city
A shepherd or countryside speaker

quiz.q: What contrast does pastoral poetry frequently draw?
options: A contrast between two unrelated cities
No contrast of any kind
The harmony of nature against the corruption of urban or courtly life
The equal chaos of both country and city life

quiz.q: What quality of rural life does pastoral poetry emphasize?
options: Constant conflict and disorder
A total absence of any landscape description
The complexity of industrial machinery
Simplicity and harmony

quiz.q: Why might a poet use the pastoral mode to comment indirectly on court or city life?
options: An idealized countryside offers a contrasting backdrop that implicitly critiques urban corruption
Rural and urban settings are treated as identical in pastoral poetry
Pastoral poetry is required to ignore any urban subject entirely
The pastoral mode forbids any form of implicit commentary

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Calculus: Definite Integrals and the Area Under a Curve
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: a definite integral uses upper and lower bounds to calculate the exact accumulated area between a curve and the horizontal axis, building on the idea of an antiderivative to turn the informal notion of area under a curve into a precise, calculable quantity.

quiz.q: What does a definite integral calculate?
options: The number of times a curve crosses the vertical axis
The slope of a curve at a single point
A quantity with no connection to area at all
The exact accumulated area between a curve and the horizontal axis

quiz.q: What two values define the range over which a definite integral is calculated?
options: The maximum and minimum of an unrelated function
A range with no defined limits at all
Only a single fixed point
An upper bound and a lower bound

quiz.q: What earlier idea does the definite integral build on?
options: The multiplication table
A concept with no connection to calculus
The Pythagorean theorem
The antiderivative

quiz.q: What does the definite integral turn the informal notion of area under a curve into?
options: A precise, calculable quantity
A quantity with no numerical value at all
A concept limited only to straight lines
An estimate that can never be calculated exactly

quiz.q: Why is finding an antiderivative a useful first step before evaluating a definite integral?
options: The antiderivative, evaluated at the bounds, gives the accumulated area directly
An antiderivative has no connection to evaluating area at all
A definite integral can only be evaluated without any antiderivative
Antiderivatives always produce a result of zero regardless of the function

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Karyotyping and Chromosomal Analysis Techniques
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: a karyotype is an organized image of an individuals complete set of chromosomes, arranged by size and banding pattern, that geneticists use to detect structural abnormalities and changes in chromosome number that a standard genetic test might otherwise miss.

quiz.q: What is a karyotype?
options: A photograph of a whole living cell
An organized image of an individuals complete set of chromosomes
An image with no connection to chromosomes at all
A single strand of unpaired DNA

quiz.q: How are chromosomes typically arranged in a karyotype?
options: In a random, unordered arrangement
By size and banding pattern
In alphabetical order by chromosome name
By colour only, with no reference to size

quiz.q: What can a karyotype help geneticists detect?
options: Structural abnormalities and changes in chromosome number
A quantity with no genetic significance at all
The colour of a persons eyes
The exact age of the individual being tested

quiz.q: Why is a karyotype useful compared to some other genetic tests?
options: It replaces the need for any chromosomes to be examined
It can only be performed on plant cells, never human cells
It reveals no genetic information of any kind
It can reveal large-scale chromosomal changes that other tests might miss

quiz.q: What might an unusual number of chromosomes visible in a karyotype indicate?
options: A chromosomal abnormality such as an extra or missing chromosome
A condition unrelated to chromosomes entirely
A completely normal and expected genetic result in every case
That the sample was not actually taken from a living cell

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Grahams Law of Effusion and Gas Diffusion Rates
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: Grahams law states that the rate at which a gas effuses through a tiny opening is inversely proportional to the square root of its molar mass, meaning lighter gas molecules escape faster than heavier ones under the same conditions.

quiz.q: What does Grahams law describe?
options: The exact colour of a gas sample
The rate at which a gas effuses through a tiny opening
The boiling point of a liquid
A quantity with no connection to gases at all

quiz.q: According to Grahams law, what is the rate of effusion inversely proportional to?
options: The colour of the container holding the gas
The temperature of the surrounding room only
The square root of the gas molar mass
A quantity with no relationship to molar mass

quiz.q: Which gas molecules escape faster under Grahams law, given the same conditions?
options: Heavier gas molecules
Lighter gas molecules
Only gas molecules with no mass at all
Molecules of any mass escape at an identical rate

quiz.q: What does effusion refer to in the context of Grahams law?
options: A process with no connection to gas particles
A liquid boiling at constant pressure
A gas escaping through a tiny opening
A solid melting into a liquid

quiz.q: Why might helium escape from a small opening faster than carbon dioxide under identical conditions?
options: Helium has a higher molar mass than carbon dioxide
Helium has a much lower molar mass, so it effuses more quickly
Molar mass has no effect on the rate of effusion
Helium and carbon dioxide always effuse at exactly the same rate

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Grammar: Sentence Fragments and Run-Ons — Deliberate and Accidental
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a sentence fragment lacks a complete subject-verb combination or a complete thought, while a run-on sentence jams two or more independent clauses together without proper punctuation, and skilled writers distinguish between these as accidental errors to fix and deliberate fragments used for stylistic emphasis.

quiz.q: What does a sentence fragment lack?
options: A complete subject-verb combination or a complete thought
A title at the start of the sentence
Any punctuation whatsoever
A minimum of ten words

quiz.q: What happens in a run-on sentence?
options: No clauses of any kind are present in the sentence
A single independent clause is left entirely unpunctuated
Two or more independent clauses are joined without proper punctuation
A sentence is broken into several very short fragments

quiz.q: When might a skilled writer use a sentence fragment on purpose?
options: Only when writing formal academic essays with no exceptions
For stylistic emphasis
Only in legal documents that forbid complete sentences
Fragments are never used deliberately under any circumstance

quiz.q: What is one way to correct a run-on sentence?
options: Deleting the subject of every clause in the sentence
Joining the independent clauses with proper punctuation or a conjunction
Adding more independent clauses without any punctuation
Removing all punctuation from the sentence entirely

quiz.q: Why is it useful for a writer to recognize the difference between an accidental fragment and a deliberate one?
options: It lets the writer distinguish between an error to fix and a stylistic choice worth keeping
Accidental fragments always improve the clarity of a sentence
Deliberate fragments are always considered grammatical errors
There is no meaningful difference between the two in any context

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Functions: Graphing Polynomial Functions — Degree, End Behaviour, and Turning Points
subjects.summary: Students use the degree and leading coefficient of a polynomial function to predict end behaviour, and determine the maximum number of turning points and zeros a polynomial can have.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Functions: Graphing Polynomial Functions — Degree, End Behaviour, and Turning Points

quiz.q: A polynomial function has degree 4 and a positive leading coefficient. What is its end behaviour?
options: left end down, right end up
both ends point downward
left end up, right end down
both ends point upward

quiz.q: What is the maximum number of turning points a degree-5 polynomial function can have?
A polynomial function has degree 3 and a negative leading coefficient. As x → ∞, what happens to y?
options: y stays constant

quiz.q: What is the maximum number of real zeros a degree-6 polynomial function can have?
Which degree and leading coefficient combination describes a graph that falls to the left and rises to the right?
options: even degree, positive leading coefficient
odd degree, negative leading coefficient
even degree, negative leading coefficient
odd degree, positive leading coefficient

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Biology: Allergies and Hypersensitivity — When Immune Responses Overreact
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: an allergy is a hypersensitive immune response in which the body treats a normally harmless substance such as pollen or a food protein as a threat, triggering mast cells to release histamine and other chemicals that produce symptoms ranging from mild irritation to a severe, life-threatening reaction.

quiz.q: What is an allergy?
options: A hypersensitive immune response to a normally harmless substance
A response in which the immune system never reacts to anything
A condition with no connection to the immune system at all
A permanent absence of any immune activity

quiz.q: What kind of substance can trigger an allergic reaction?
options: A substance with no biological origin at all
Only substances that are inherently toxic to every person
A substance found only inside bacteria
A normally harmless substance such as pollen or a food protein

quiz.q: What cell type releases histamine during an allergic reaction?
options: Mast cells
Muscle cells
A cell type with no role in immune responses
Red blood cells

quiz.q: What chemical do mast cells release that produces many allergy symptoms?
options: Insulin
A chemical unrelated to any immune response
Histamine
Hemoglobin

quiz.q: What range of severity can allergic reactions have, from mild to extreme?
options: From mild irritation to a severe, life-threatening reaction
Allergic reactions always require no immune involvement at all
Allergic reactions are always mild and never dangerous
Every allergic reaction is identical in severity with no variation

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Net Ionic Equations and Spectator Ions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: a net ionic equation shows only the ions and molecules that actually participate in a chemical change, removing spectator ions that appear unchanged on both sides of the full equation, which highlights the specific reaction actually taking place in an aqueous solution.

quiz.q: What does a net ionic equation show?
options: A description with no connection to a chemical reaction
Only the ions and molecules that actually participate in a chemical change
A full molecular equation with no ions removed
Every single ion present in the solution, whether or not it reacts

quiz.q: What is a spectator ion?
options: An ion with no presence in the original solution at all
An ion that appears unchanged on both sides of the full equation
An ion that changes into a different element entirely
An ion that is completely consumed during the reaction

quiz.q: What happens to spectator ions when writing a net ionic equation?
options: They are converted into solid precipitates automatically
They are removed from the equation
They become the only ions shown in the equation
They are duplicated on both sides of the equation

quiz.q: What does a net ionic equation highlight about a reaction in aqueous solution?
options: The specific reaction actually taking place
A process entirely unrelated to the original reactants
Only the physical appearance of the solution
A reaction that never actually occurs in solution

quiz.q: Why is identifying spectator ions useful when analyzing a reaction in solution?
options: Removing spectator ions always eliminates the entire reaction
It isolates the actual chemical change from ions that are present but do not react
Spectator ions cannot be identified in any aqueous solution
Spectator ions are always the most important part of any reaction

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Literature: The Epic — Conventions of a Sweeping Poetic Form
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: an epic is a long narrative poem that follows a hero of great cultural significance through a series of trials often spanning vast distances or timescales, traditionally opening with an invocation to a muse and employing an elevated, formal style suited to its grand subject matter.

quiz.q: What kind of narrative is an epic?
options: A poem with no central character of any kind
A brief riddle with no narrative content
A short lyric poem about a single private emotion
A long narrative poem following a hero of great cultural significance

quiz.q: What does an epic hero typically undergo throughout the poem?
options: A trial that is resolved before the poem even begins
A single uneventful day with no challenges at all
No challenges of any kind throughout the narrative
A series of trials often spanning vast distances or timescales

quiz.q: What does an epic traditionally open with?
options: A list of unrelated characters with no context
An invocation to a muse
A modern news bulletin
A detailed weather report

quiz.q: What kind of style does an epic traditionally employ?
options: An elevated, formal style suited to its grand subject matter
A casual, conversational style with no formality
A style that avoids any elevated language whatsoever
A style identical to a text message

quiz.q: Why might an epics vast scope of distance or time suit its subject matter?
options: Epic poems must always be shorter than a single stanza
A vast scope has no connection to a heros significance
Epics are always confined to a single room with no scope at all
A grand, sweeping scale reflects the heros larger-than-life cultural significance

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Statistics: Correlation and the Line of Best Fit
subjects.summary: Students analyze scatter plots to describe the strength and direction of correlation between two variables and use a line of best fit to make predictions.
subjects.resourceLabel: YouTube: Statistics: Correlation and the Line of Best Fit

quiz.q: A scatter plot shows points closely clustered around a line that rises from left to right. This indicates:
options: strong negative correlation
weak positive correlation
no correlation
strong positive correlation

quiz.q: A correlation coefficient of r = -0.92 indicates:
options: a strong negative correlation
a strong positive correlation
a weak negative correlation
no correlation

quiz.q: Using a line of best fit y = 2.5x + 10, what is the predicted value of y when x = 8?
Which correlation coefficient represents the weakest relationship between two variables?
Using a line of best fit to predict a value far outside the range of the original data is called:
options: interpolation
regression
extrapolation
correlation

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Plant Biology: Seed Dispersal Strategies — Wind, Water, and Animal Vectors
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: plants have evolved a range of seed dispersal strategies, from lightweight winged or feathery seeds carried by wind, to buoyant seeds that float on water, to fruits and burrs that attract or attach to animals, all of which reduce competition with the parent plant and help colonize new habitats.

quiz.q: What is one strategy plants use to disperse seeds by wind?
options: Lightweight winged or feathery seeds
Seeds that dissolve completely before they can travel
Seeds that are extremely dense and heavy
Seeds with no adaptation for movement of any kind

quiz.q: What feature allows some seeds to be dispersed by water?
options: An inability to survive contact with water at all
Buoyancy that lets them float
A structure that immediately sinks in water
A complete lack of any protective coating

quiz.q: How do burrs typically achieve dispersal by animals?
options: By repelling every animal that comes near them
By attaching to fur or feathers as an animal passes by
By being completely ignored by every animal
By dissolving instantly on contact with an animal

quiz.q: What advantage does seed dispersal provide relative to the parent plant?
options: It reduces competition with the parent plant for resources
It guarantees the seed will never germinate at all
It has no effect on competition of any kind
It increases competition between the seed and the parent plant

quiz.q: Why is colonizing new habitats an important outcome of effective seed dispersal?
options: Seed dispersal has no connection to colonizing new areas
Colonizing new habitats always reduces a species chances of survival
New habitats always prevent a seed from germinating
It allows a plant species to spread into new areas and increase its chances of survival

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Significant Figures and Precision in Quantitative Chemistry
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: significant figures represent the digits in a measurement that carry meaningful information about its precision, and applying consistent rules for significant figures in calculations ensures that a final answer does not falsely imply more precision than the original measured data actually supports.

quiz.q: What do significant figures represent in a measurement?
options: A quantity with no connection to precision at all
Only the first digit of any measured value
Every digit in a number regardless of its meaning
The digits that carry meaningful information about its precision

quiz.q: Why are consistent rules for significant figures applied during calculations?
options: Significant figures have no effect on the precision implied by an answer
To ensure a final answer does not falsely imply more precision than the original data supports
To remove all decimal points from every calculated value
To make every calculated answer appear as precise as possible regardless of the data

quiz.q: What might happen if significant figures are ignored in a chemistry calculation?
options: The final answer could imply a level of precision the original measurements do not support
The final answer would always become less precise than the original data
The calculation would be entirely unaffected by any precision issue
Ignoring significant figures always produces a completely correct result

quiz.q: What kind of information do significant figures help communicate about measured data?
options: How precisely a quantity was actually measured
A value with no connection to measurement at all
The colour of the substance being measured
The exact chemical identity of a substance

quiz.q: Why is precision in quantitative chemistry important when reporting experimental results?
options: Significant figures are only relevant to qualitative, not quantitative, chemistry
It ensures other scientists can accurately judge the reliability of the reported data
Precision has no bearing on how other scientists interpret results
Reported results never need to reflect the precision of the original measurement

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Drama: The Comedy of Manners — Wit and Social Satire on Stage
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a comedy of manners satirizes the behaviour and pretensions of a particular social class, relying on witty, polished dialogue and characters obsessed with reputation and social status to expose the gap between how people present themselves and how they actually behave.

quiz.q: What does a comedy of manners satirize?
options: A tragic historical event with no comedic elements
A purely private, solitary experience with no social dimension
A setting with no connection to any social class
The behaviour and pretensions of a particular social class

quiz.q: What kind of dialogue does a comedy of manners typically rely on?
options: Dialogue borrowed entirely from a formal legal document
Silence, with no spoken dialogue at all
Dialogue with no wit or polish of any kind
Witty, polished dialogue

quiz.q: What are characters in a comedy of manners often preoccupied with?
options: A complete indifference to how others perceive them
Physical survival in a wilderness setting
Reputation and social status
Scientific discovery with no social concern at all

quiz.q: What gap does a comedy of manners often expose?
options: The gap between two entirely different literary genres
No gap of any kind, since characters are always sincere
The gap between how people present themselves and how they actually behave
A gap between two unrelated historical periods

quiz.q: Why is witty dialogue especially important to the comedy of manners genre?
options: Witty dialogue has no connection to satire of any kind
It sharpens the satire of social pretension through clever, pointed exchanges
A comedy of manners forbids any form of humour
Dialogue in this genre must always be entirely serious and formal

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Geometry: The Distance from a Point to a Plane in Three Dimensions
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Functions strand: the distance from a point to a plane in three dimensions is found by projecting the vector from a known point on the plane to the given point onto the planes normal vector, giving the shortest, perpendicular distance between the point and the plane.

quiz.q: What is being calculated when finding the distance from a point to a plane?
options: A quantity with no connection to distance at all
A distance measured only along the plane itself
The longest possible path between the point and the plane
The shortest, perpendicular distance between the point and the plane

quiz.q: What vector is used to help calculate the distance from a point to a plane?
options: The vector describing an entirely different plane
A vector with no defined direction at all
The planes normal vector
A vector lying entirely within an unrelated line

quiz.q: What kind of distance does this method always produce, relative to the plane?
options: A perpendicular distance
A distance with no defined geometric meaning
A distance that varies depending on the angle chosen
A distance measured parallel to the plane

quiz.q: What is projected onto the normal vector during this calculation?
options: A vector with no connection to either the point or the plane
The equation of an entirely unrelated line
The vector from a known point on the plane to the given point
The coordinates of the origin only

quiz.q: How does this calculation relate to the earlier idea of finding where a line intersects a plane?
options: The two calculations have no mathematical relationship at all
Distance from a point to a plane cannot be calculated using the planes normal vector
Finding a line-plane intersection never involves the planes equation
Both rely on the planes equation and normal vector to describe the planes geometry precisely

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Ecology: Edge Effects and Habitat Fragmentation
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: habitat fragmentation breaks a large, continuous habitat into smaller, isolated patches, increasing the amount of edge relative to interior habitat, and this edge effect exposes interior species to different light, wind, and predation conditions that can reduce biodiversity even when total habitat area seems only modestly reduced.

quiz.q: What does habitat fragmentation do to a large, continuous habitat?
options: Expands it into an even larger continuous area
Leaves it completely unchanged in every way
Breaks it into smaller, isolated patches
Converts it entirely into open ocean

quiz.q: What increases relative to interior habitat as fragmentation occurs?
options: The amount of edge habitat
The total number of unrelated species with no connection to edges
The distance between the fragments and the nearest ocean
The amount of interior habitat, with no change to edge

quiz.q: What conditions can differ at a habitats edge compared to its interior?
options: Conditions identical in every way to the interior
Light, wind, and predation conditions
Only the colour of the surrounding rock
A condition with no ecological relevance at all

quiz.q: What can the edge effect do to species adapted to interior habitat conditions?
options: Expose them to unfavourable conditions that can reduce biodiversity
Have no effect on interior species whatsoever
Guarantee an increase in their population size
Immediately improve their survival with no negative effect at all

quiz.q: Why can habitat fragmentation harm biodiversity even when the total habitat area is only modestly reduced?
options: Total habitat area has no connection to species survival
Edge habitat is always identical in quality to interior habitat
A larger proportion of the remaining habitat becomes edge habitat, unsuitable for many interior species
Fragmentation always increases the amount of usable interior habitat

subjects.subject: Chemistry
subjects.title: Chemistry: Boiling Point Elevation and Its Real-World Applications
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Chemistry strand: boiling point elevation occurs when dissolving a solute raises the boiling point of a solvent above its pure value, a colligative property that depends on the number of dissolved particles, which explains why adding salt to a pot of water raises the temperature at which it boils.

quiz.q: What happens to a solvents boiling point when a solute is dissolved in it?
options: The boiling point is always lowered below its pure value
The solvent stops boiling entirely once a solute is added
The boiling point is raised above its pure value
The boiling point remains completely unchanged in every case

quiz.q: What category of property is boiling point elevation classified as?
options: A property that depends only on solute identity
A property unrelated to the number of dissolved particles
A purely physical property with no chemical basis
A colligative property

quiz.q: What determines the size of the boiling point elevation for a given solvent?
options: A factor with no connection to the solute at all
The exact colour of the dissolved solute
The identity of the solute rather than particle count
The number of dissolved particles

quiz.q: What everyday example illustrates boiling point elevation?
options: Adding salt to a pot of water raises the temperature at which it boils
Salt has no measurable effect on the boiling point of water
Adding salt to water always lowers its boiling point
Boiling water always occurs at exactly the same temperature regardless of what is dissolved in it

quiz.q: How does boiling point elevation relate to other colligative properties such as freezing point depression?
options: Freezing point depression depends only on solute identity, unlike boiling point elevation
Both depend on the number of dissolved particles in a solution, not their identity
Colligative properties depend on particle identity rather than particle count
Boiling point elevation and freezing point depression have no relationship to each other

subjects.subject: English
subjects.title: Writing: The Toast — A Short Speech of Celebration
subjects.summary: Grade 11 English strand: a toast is a brief, warm speech delivered to celebrate a person or occasion, typically opening with a short anecdote or observation, expressing genuine appreciation, and closing with a concise, memorable line that invites the audience to raise a glass together.

quiz.q: What is a toast?
options: A brief, warm speech delivered to celebrate a person or occasion
A lengthy, formal lecture on an academic subject
A speech intended to criticize rather than celebrate its subject
A written letter with no spoken component at all

quiz.q: What does a toast often open with?
options: A short anecdote or observation
A lengthy historical timeline
A list of unrelated statistics
A detailed legal disclaimer

quiz.q: What tone does a toast typically aim to express?
options: A tone with no emotional content at all
Genuine appreciation
Harsh criticism of the person being celebrated
Complete indifference to the occasion

quiz.q: How does a toast typically close?
options: With an extended argument on an unrelated topic
With a detailed critique of the occasion itself
With no closing line of any kind
With a concise, memorable line inviting the audience to raise a glass

quiz.q: Why does a toast benefit from being brief rather than long?
options: Length has no effect on how a toast is received
Its brevity keeps the celebratory moment focused and memorable for the audience
A toast is always more effective the longer it becomes
Toasts are required by convention to last at least ten minutes

subjects.subject: Functions
subjects.title: Probability: Permutations and Combinations
subjects.summary: Students use permutations and combinations to count arrangements and selections, applying the formulas nPr and nCr to solve counting problems.

quiz.q: How many ways can 4 different books be arranged in a row on a shelf?
Evaluate 5P2 (permutations of 5 items taken 2 at a time).
Evaluate 6C2 (combinations of 6 items taken 2 at a time).
A committee of 3 people is chosen from a group of 8, where order does not matter. How many different committees are possible?
Which situation requires a permutation rather than a combination?
options: selecting a 4-person committee from 10 people
assigning 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place medals among 6 runners
choosing 3 toppings for a pizza from 6 options
choosing 2 books to bring on vacation from a shelf of 5

subjects.subject: Biology
subjects.title: Microbiology: Protists — Diverse Life Strategies Beyond Animals, Plants, and Fungi
subjects.summary: Grade 11 Biology strand: protists are a highly diverse group of mostly single-celled eukaryotic organisms that do not fit neatly into the animal, plant, or fungus kingdoms, including photosynthetic algae, animal-like protozoa that actively hunt prey, and fungus-like slime moulds, reflecting a wide range of feeding and reproductive strategies.

quiz.q: What type of cell do most protists have?
options: No cells of any kind
A single prokaryotic cell
A single eukaryotic cell
Multiple cells with no nucleus at all

quiz.q: Why are protists considered difficult to classify?
options: They fit perfectly and exclusively into the plant kingdom
They fit perfectly and exclusively into the animal kingdom
They do not fit neatly into the animal, plant, or fungus kingdoms
They have no classification difficulties at all

quiz.q: Name one photosynthetic type of protist.
options: A true fungus
A vertebrate animal
Algae
A bacterium with no chloroplasts

quiz.q: What behaviour do animal-like protozoa often display?
options: Remaining completely immobile at all times
Photosynthesizing using chlorophyll
Actively hunting prey
Forming a rigid cell wall identical to plants

quiz.q: What does the wide range of protist feeding and reproductive strategies suggest about the group?

Adding moisture to dry air
Removing moisture from the air as a desiccant

Adsorption
Sublimation
A process with no connection to moisture at all

quiz.q: Where do water molecules attach during adsorption by silica gel?

The exact centre of each individual silica gel bead
A surface that repels water molecules completely
The vast internal surface area of its microscopic pores

quiz.q: How does adsorption differ from absorption?
options: Adsorption involves molecules sticking to a surface, while absorption takes a substance into the bulk volume of a material
Absorption always occurs only at a materials surface, never within its volume
Adsorption and absorption describe exactly the same physical process
